49905.q: What colours is the flag of Argentina?
49905.e: The flag has two light blue stripes and one white stripe. In the middle there is a golden sun.
49905.m: Argentina's flag is light blue and white.

49906.q: What is the capital of Peru?
49906.e: Lima lies on the coast of Peru. It is the largest city in the country.
49906.m: Lima is the capital of Peru.

49907.q: Which dish made of raw fish with lime juice is famous in Peru?
49907.e: For ceviche, raw fish is soaked in lime juice. The juice makes the fish firm.
49907.m: Ceviche is a famous dish from Peru.

49908.q: What colours is the flag of Peru?
49908.e: Peru's flag has three vertical stripes: red, white, red. The Swiss flag has the same colours.
49908.m: Peru's flag is red and white.

49909.q: What is the currency of Peru?
49909.e: In Peru people pay with the sol. The word means “sun” in Spanish.
49909.m: The money in Peru is called the sol.

49910.q: Which city in Peru used to be the capital of the Inca?
49910.e: Cusco lies high in the mountains at about 3400 metres. Many walls from Inca times are still standing there today.
49910.m: Cusco was the capital of the Inca.

49911.q: Which huge pictures in the desert ground of Peru can best be seen from the air?
49911.e: The Nazca Lines are over 1500 years old. They show, for example, a monkey, a hummingbird and a spider.
49911.m: The Nazca Lines are huge pictures in Peru's desert.

49912.q: Which old language from the Andes is an official language in Peru?
49912.e: Quechua was already spoken in the Inca Empire. Millions of people in the Andes still speak it today.
49912.m: People in Peru also speak Quechua.

49913.q: What can you see in the blue square on the flag of Chile?
49913.e: Chile's flag is white and red. At the top left there is a blue square with a white star.
49913.m: There is a white star on Chile's flag.

49914.q: What is the capital of Chile?
49914.e: Santiago de Chile lies in a valley in front of high mountains. Over a third of all people in Chile live in the greater city area.
49914.m: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

49915.q: Which very long and narrow country lies on the west coast of South America?
49915.e: Chile is over 4000 kilometres long but mostly less than 200 kilometres wide. It lies between the Pacific and the Andes.
49915.m: Chile is a long, narrow country on the Pacific.

49916.q: Which country borders Chile to the north?
49916.e: To the north, Peru is Chile's neighbour. Bolivia lies to the north-east.
49916.m: Peru borders Chile to the north.

49917.q: In which country was the strongest earthquake ever measured, in 1960?
49917.e: The Valdivia earthquake in 1960 had a magnitude of 9.5. The earth often shakes in Chile because tectonic plates push against each other there.
49917.m: The strongest earthquake ever measured was in Chile in 1960.

49918.q: Which metal does Chile mine more of than any other country in the world?
49918.e: Chile has huge copper mines. No country mines more copper.
49918.m: Chile mines the most copper in the world.

49919.q: Which penguin lives on the coasts of Chile and Peru?
49919.e: The Humboldt penguin is named after the explorer Alexander von Humboldt. It lives on the cool Pacific coast.
49919.m: The Humboldt penguin lives in Chile and Peru.

49920.q: What is the capital of Colombia?
49920.e: Bogotá lies high in the mountains at about 2600 metres. It is the largest city in the country.
49920.m: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.

49921.q: Which two seas does Colombia border?
a: The Pacific and the Caribbean Sea
The North Sea and the Baltic Sea
49921.e: Colombia has a coast on the Pacific in the west and on the Caribbean Sea in the north. No other country in South America has that.

49922.q: Which green gemstones is Colombia famous for?
49922.e: Many of the most beautiful emeralds in the world come from Colombia. Emeralds are bright green.

49923.q: Which seafarer is Colombia named after?
49923.e: Christopher Columbus came to America in 1492. The country of Colombia bears his name.
49923.m: Colombia is named after Christopher Columbus.

49924.q: Which country has the most bird species in the world?
49924.e: Almost 2000 different bird species live in Colombia. That is more than in any other country.
49924.m: Colombia has the most bird species in the world.

49925.q: Which old port city with a city wall lies on Colombia's Caribbean coast?
49925.e: Cartagena was founded by the Spanish and protected by a thick wall. Today the old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
49925.m: Cartagena is an old port city in Colombia.

49926.q: What colour is the top half of Colombia's flag?
49926.e: The flag has a wide yellow stripe at the top. Below it come a blue and a red stripe.
49926.m: Colombia's flag is yellow, blue and red.

49927.q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
49927.e: Caracas lies in the north of the country, close to the sea. It is the largest city in Venezuela.
49927.m: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela.

49928.q: Which sea is the coast in the north of Venezuela on?
49928.e: Venezuela has a long coast in the north. There are also many small islands there.
49928.m: Venezuela lies on the Caribbean Sea.

49929.q: What is the name of the largest river in Venezuela?
49929.e: The Orinoco flows right across Venezuela. It flows into the Atlantic.
49929.m: The Orinoco is Venezuela's largest river.

49930.q: Of which natural resource does Venezuela have the largest reserves in the world?
49930.e: There is a great deal of oil under the ground in Venezuela. No country has proven larger reserves.
49930.m: Venezuela has the largest oil reserves in the world.

49931.q: Which city in Italy is Venezuela named after?
49931.e: Seafarers saw houses on stilts in the water there. It reminded them of Venice, so they called the country “Little Venice”.

49932.q: Which famous freedom fighter was born in Caracas?
49932.e: Simón Bolívar freed several South American countries from Spanish rule. The country of Bolivia is named after him.
49932.m: Simón Bolívar was a freedom fighter from Venezuela.

49933.q: What are the high table mountains with flat tops in Venezuela called?
49933.e: The tepuis have steep rock walls and a flat area on top. Plants live on them that are found nowhere else.
49933.m: The tepuis are table mountains in Venezuela.

49934.q: What is the name of the famous rocky mountain in Rio de Janeiro with a cable car?
49934.e: Sugarloaf Mountain rises straight up from the sea. A cable car takes visitors to the top.
49934.m: Sugarloaf Mountain is a landmark of Rio de Janeiro.

49935.q: What is the name of the most famous beach in Rio de Janeiro?
49935.e: Copacabana is a sandy beach about 4 kilometres long. Many people celebrate New Year's Eve there.
49935.m: Copacabana is a famous beach in Rio.

49936.q: Until which year was Rio de Janeiro the capital of Brazil?
49936.e: Rio de Janeiro was the capital for a long time. In 1960 the government moved to a new capital.
49936.m: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960.

49937.q: In which year were the Summer Olympic Games held in Rio de Janeiro?
49937.e: The 2016 Games were the first Olympic Games in South America.
49937.m: Rio de Janeiro hosted the Olympics in 2016.

49938.q: What does the name Rio de Janeiro mean in English?
49938.e: Portuguese seafarers came into the bay in January 1502. They thought it was the mouth of a river.
49938.m: Rio de Janeiro means “River of January”.

49939.q: What is the name of the famous football stadium in Rio de Janeiro?
49939.e: The Maracanã is one of the best-known stadiums in the world. The deciding matches of the 1950 and 2014 World Cups were played there.
49939.m: The Maracanã is Rio's famous stadium.

49940.q: Which huge statue stands on a mountain above Rio de Janeiro?
a: A statue of Christ with outstretched arms
A statue of a rider on horseback
49940.e: The statue of Christ stands on Corcovado mountain. It spreads its arms over the city and is a landmark of Rio.
49940.m: A huge statue of Christ stands above Rio de Janeiro.

49941.q: Which ocean is Rio de Janeiro on?
49941.e: Rio de Janeiro lies on the east coast of Brazil. That is where the Atlantic Ocean is.
49941.m: Rio de Janeiro lies on the Atlantic.

49942.q: What does “Cristo Redentor” mean in English?
49942.e: “Redentor” is Portuguese and means “redeemer”. The statue shows Jesus Christ.

49943.q: How do many visitors travel up to the Christ the Redeemer statue?
49943.e: A rack railway runs through the forest almost to the statue. For the last part you take the stairs or a lift.
49943.m: A rack railway goes up to the statue of Christ.

49944.q: About how tall is the statue of Christ without its base?
49944.e: The figure is about 30 metres tall. With the base it is about 38 metres.
49944.m: The statue of Christ is about 30 metres tall.

49945.q: How does the statue of Christ in Rio hold its arms?
49945.e: The statue spreads its arms wide to the left and right. From far away it looks like a cross.
49945.m: The statue of Christ spreads its arms wide.

49946.q: In which year was the Christ the Redeemer statue opened?
49946.e: The statue was built from 1922 to 1931. In 1931 it was officially opened.
49946.m: The statue of Christ was opened in 1931.

49947.q: Which famous list has the Christ the Redeemer statue been part of since 2007?
a: New Seven Wonders of the World
49947.e: In 2007, millions of people voted for new wonders of the world. The statue of Christ was chosen.
49947.m: The statue of Christ is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

49948.q: What colour is the large statue of Christ in Rio on the outside?
49948.e: Inside, the statue is made of reinforced concrete. Outside, it is covered with many small, light tiles of soapstone.
49948.m: The statue of Christ in Rio is light, almost white.

49949.q: Why did the builders of Machu Picchu make terraces on the steep slopes?
49949.e: Maize and potatoes could be planted on the flat steps. The terraces also stopped the slope from sliding.
49949.m: The terraces of Machu Picchu were fields.

49950.q: Which animals often graze among the ruins of Machu Picchu today?
49950.e: Llamas walk around freely between the old walls. They keep the grass short.

49951.q: At about what altitude does Machu Picchu lie?
49951.e: Machu Picchu lies at about 2430 metres above sea level. That is about as high as many Alpine peaks.
49951.m: Machu Picchu lies at about 2400 metres.

49952.q: In which century was Machu Picchu built?
49952.e: Machu Picchu was built around the year 1450. That is in the 15th century.

49953.q: In which year did an explorer make Machu Picchu famous around the world?
49953.e: The American Hiram Bingham visited Machu Picchu in 1911. Afterwards he told the whole world about it.

49954.q: What holds many of the stone walls of the temples in Machu Picchu together?
a: The stones fit exactly on top of each other
49954.e: The stones were cut so precisely that they hold without mortar. Often not even a knife fits between them.
49954.m: Many walls of Machu Picchu hold without mortar.

49955.q: What does the name Machu Picchu mean in English?
49955.e: The name comes from an old language of the Andes. It means “old mountain” or “old peak”.

49956.q: Which two countries is Patagonia divided between?
49956.e: Patagonia is the southernmost part of South America. The larger part belongs to Argentina, the smaller part to Chile.
49956.m: Patagonia lies in Argentina and Chile.

49957.q: What is the weather in Patagonia especially known for?
49957.e: In Patagonia a fierce wind often blows from the west. Trees there sometimes grow crooked.
49957.m: Strong winds often blow in Patagonia.

49958.q: What is the name of the famous glacier in the Argentine part of Patagonia?
49958.e: The Perito Moreno Glacier ends in a lake. Again and again, large pieces of ice break off and crash into the water.
49958.m: The Perito Moreno Glacier lies in Patagonia.

49959.q: Which animals are raised on huge pastures in Patagonia?
49959.e: In Patagonia there are large farms with thousands of sheep. Their wool is sold all over the world.
49959.m: Many sheep are raised in Patagonia.

49960.q: Which penguin breeds on the coasts of Patagonia?
49960.e: The Magellanic penguin is named after the seafarer Ferdinand Magellan. It digs its nests in the ground.
49960.m: The Magellanic penguin breeds in Patagonia.

49961.q: Which national park with three tall rock towers lies in the Chilean part of Patagonia?
49961.e: “Torres” means “towers” in Spanish. The three steep granite towers are the symbol of the park.
49961.m: Torres del Paine National Park lies in Patagonia.

49962.q: What is the name of the group of islands at the southern tip of South America?
49962.e: Seafarers saw many fires lit by the people on the shore. So they called the islands Tierra del Fuego, “Land of Fire”.
49962.m: Tierra del Fuego lies at the southern tip of South America.

49963.q: Seen from above, what does the layout of Brasília look like?
49963.e: The city plan has a long body and two wings. From above it looks like an aeroplane or a bird.
49963.m: Brasília has the shape of an aeroplane.

a: In the interior of the country
49964.e: Brasília lies on a plateau in the middle of the country. This was meant to help the interior of Brazil grow too.
49964.m: Brasília lies in the interior of the country.

49965.q: How was the large Lake Paranoá in Brasília formed?
a: It was made by damming a river
49965.e: When the city was built, a river was blocked with a dam. This created Lake Paranoá.
49965.m: Lake Paranoá in Brasília is a reservoir.

49966.q: What is Brazil's capital Brasília known for?
a: It was built from scratch to a plan in just a few years
It is the oldest city in America
It lies right by the sea
It is the largest city in Brazil
49966.e: Brasília was built in the middle of the country from 1956 and became the capital in 1960. From above, the city plan looks like an aeroplane. Today the city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

49967.q: In which country is the city of Buenos Aires?
49967.e: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina. It lies on the wide mouth of the Río de la Plata.

49968.q: Which dance comes from Buenos Aires?
49968.e: The tango began over 100 years ago in the harbour districts of Buenos Aires. Samba comes from Brazil, flamenco from Spain.
49968.m: The tango comes from Buenos Aires.

49969.q: Which tall, pointed monument stands in the middle of Buenos Aires?
49969.e: The Obelisk of Buenos Aires is about 68 metres tall. It is a landmark of the city.
49969.m: The Obelisk is a landmark of Buenos Aires.

49970.q: What is the Avenida 9 de Julio in Buenos Aires known for?
a: It is one of the widest streets in the world
It is the steepest street in the world
It is the oldest street in South America
It is the narrowest alley in the city
49970.e: The Avenida 9 de Julio has many lanes in each direction. On foot you need several sets of traffic lights to cross it.
49970.m: The Avenida 9 de Julio is very wide.

49971.q: What is the La Boca district in Buenos Aires known for?
49971.e: In La Boca many houses are painted in bright colours. In the past people used leftover paint from the harbour for this.
49971.m: La Boca is a colourful district in Buenos Aires.

49972.q: What is grown in many fields of the Pampas today?
49972.e: The soil of the Pampas is very fertile. That is why huge fields of wheat, maize and soya grow there today.
49972.m: Wheat and soya grow in the Pampas.

49973.e: The word comes from an old language of South America. It fits well, because the Pampas are almost completely flat.

49974.q: The mara lives in the Pampas. What does this animal look like?
a: Like a hare with long legs
Like a fat mouse without ears
49974.e: The mara is also called the Patagonian hare. It is not a real hare but is related to the guinea pig.
49974.m: The mara looks like a hare with long legs.

49975.q: Which animals graze in large herds on the Pampas?
49975.e: Millions of cattle live on the pastures of the Pampas. That is why Argentina is known for its beef.
49975.m: Many cattle graze on the Pampas.

49976.q: Which large running bird lives in the Pampas?
49976.e: The rhea cannot fly, but it can run very fast. It lives only in South America.
49976.m: The rhea is a running bird of the Pampas.

49977.q: A strong wind from the south sometimes blows across the Pampas. What does it bring?
49977.e: The wind is called the pampero. It comes from the cold south and suddenly brings cool, often stormy weather.
49977.m: The pampero brings cool weather to the Pampas.

49978.q: The herders on the Pampas are called gauchos. Which tea do they like to drink from a cup with a drinking straw?
49978.e: Mate is made from the leaves of a plant. It is drunk from a small cup with a metal straw.

49979.q: Which way do most of the moai on Easter Island face?
49979.e: Most moai stand on the coast but look towards the inside of the island. They were probably meant to protect the villages.

49980.q: Which country does Easter Island belong to?
49980.e: Easter Island has belonged to this country since 1888. But it lies far away from the mainland.

49981.q: In which ocean is Easter Island?
49981.e: Easter Island lies in the middle of the largest ocean in the world. It is one of the most remote inhabited islands.
49981.m: Easter Island lies in the Pacific.

49982.q: What do the inhabitants call Easter Island in their own language?
49982.e: Rapa Nui is the name of the island, its people and their language. It means roughly “great Rapa”.
49982.m: Easter Island is also called Rapa Nui.

49983.q: Where did the first inhabitants of Easter Island come from?
49983.e: Polynesian seafarers came to the island by boat about 800 to 1000 years ago. They found their way across the open sea.
49983.m: The first inhabitants of Easter Island came from Polynesia.

49984.q: What material are the moai made of?
49984.e: The moai were carved from soft volcanic rock. The rock comes from an old crater on the island.
49984.m: The moai are made of volcanic rock.

49985.q: In which city is the famous opera house with a roof that looks like sails?
49985.e: The opera house stands at the harbour of Sydney in Australia. It is one of the best-known buildings in the world.
49985.m: The opera house with the sail roof is in Sydney.

49986.q: What does the roof of the Sydney Opera House remind many people of?
49986.e: The white, curved parts of the roof look like billowing sails. That fits well, because the building stands right by the harbour.
49986.m: The roof of the opera house looks like sails.

49987.q: In which country is the Sydney Opera House?
49987.e: The opera house is in Sydney, the largest city in Australia. It is one of the best-known buildings in the world.
49987.m: The Sydney Opera House is in Australia.

49988.q: In which century was the Sydney Opera House opened?
49988.e: The opera house was opened in 1973 by Queen Elizabeth II. Building it took much longer than planned.
49988.m: The Sydney Opera House is a 20th-century building.

49989.q: What is the shiny surface of the Sydney Opera House roofs made of?
49989.e: The roofs are covered with over a million small white and cream-coloured tiles. That is why they shine in the sun.
49989.m: The roofs of the opera house are covered with tiles.

49990.q: Which famous bridge stands very close to the Sydney Opera House?
49990.e: The large steel arch bridge across the harbour is called the Sydney Harbour Bridge. Because of its shape, people call it “the Coathanger”.
49990.m: Next to the opera house, the Harbour Bridge spans the harbour.

49991.q: Since 2007, the Sydney Opera House has been on a special list. Which one?
a: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
The tallest buildings in the world
The oldest houses in the world
49991.e: Since 2007 the opera house has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Switzerland also has World Heritage Sites, for example the old town of Bern.
49991.m: The Sydney Opera House is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

49992.q: What can you experience at the Sydney Opera House?
49992.e: The opera house has several halls for opera, concerts, theatre and ballet. Over a thousand performances take place there every year.
49992.m: The Sydney Opera House has concerts, opera and theatre.

49993.e: Uluru is a gigantic rock in the middle of flat land. It is one of Australia's landmarks.
49993.m: Uluru is a huge red rock in Australia.

a: Roughly in the middle of the country
On an island in the south
49994.e: Uluru lies in the dry centre of Australia, far away from the big cities on the coast.
49994.m: Uluru lies in the middle of Australia.

49995.q: What did European settlers use to call Uluru?
49995.e: An explorer gave the rock the name Ayers Rock in 1873. Today the old name Uluru is mostly used again.
49995.m: Uluru used to be called Ayers Rock.

49996.q: What colour does Uluru often turn at sunset?
49996.e: In the evening the rock glows strongly red and orange in the light of the low sun. Many visitors come just for that.

49997.q: About how high does Uluru rise above the flat land?
49997.e: Uluru rises about 348 metres above the plain. That is more than twice as high as the Prime Tower in Zurich.
49997.m: Uluru rises about 350 metres above the land.

49998.q: For which people is Uluru a sacred place?
49998.e: For the first people of Australia, especially the Anangu, Uluru is sacred. There are many old stories about it.
49998.m: Uluru is a sacred place for the Aboriginal people.

49999.q: What has been banned at Uluru since October 2019?
49999.e: Out of respect for the Aboriginal people, nobody has been allowed to climb the rock since 2019. But you may still walk around it.

50000.q: What kind of landscape is Uluru in?
50000.e: Uluru stands in the dry, hot heart of Australia. All around there is red sand and only a few bushes.
50000.m: Uluru stands in the Australian desert.

50001.q: Which two large islands mainly make up New Zealand?
50001.e: New Zealand has two main islands, the North Island and the South Island. There are also many smaller islands.
50001.m: New Zealand is mainly made up of the North Island and the South Island.

50002.q: Which bird is the national symbol of New Zealand?
50002.e: The kiwi is a small bird that cannot fly. New Zealanders like to call themselves “Kiwis”.
50002.m: The kiwi is New Zealand's national symbol.

50003.q: What are the first people of New Zealand called?
50003.e: The Maori came to New Zealand by boat about 700 years ago. Today their language is an official language.
50003.m: The first people of New Zealand are the Maori.

50004.q: What is the name of the well-known Maori war dance that rugby players perform before a match?
50004.e: In the haka the dancers stamp, shout loudly and stick out their tongues. The rugby team the “All Blacks” performs it before every match.
50004.m: The haka is the famous dance of the Maori.

50005.q: Which is the largest city in New Zealand?
50005.e: Auckland on the North Island is the largest city. About a third of all New Zealanders live there.
50005.m: Auckland is New Zealand's largest city.

50006.q: Which animals are there more of than people in New Zealand?
50006.e: About 5.3 million people live in New Zealand (2024), but over 20 million sheep. Sheep farming is very important there.
50006.m: New Zealand has more sheep than people.

50007.q: What is the mountain range on New Zealand's South Island called?
50007.e: The Southern Alps are also called the New Zealand Alps. As in Switzerland, there are high mountains and glaciers there.
50007.m: The Southern Alps are on the South Island.

50008.q: Which is the highest mountain in New Zealand?
50008.e: Aoraki, also called Mount Cook, is about 3700 metres high. It is on the South Island and surrounded by glaciers.
50008.m: New Zealand's highest mountain is Aoraki or Mount Cook.

50009.q: In 1893, New Zealand was the first country to allow women to do something. What?
50009.e: In 1893 women in New Zealand were the first in the world allowed to vote nationally. In Switzerland this only happened in 1971.
50009.m: In 1893 New Zealand was the first country to give women the vote.

50010.q: Which city is the capital of New Zealand?
50010.e: Wellington is the capital, but not the largest city in the country. Parliament meets there.
50010.m: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand.

50011.q: In which country is the city of Wellington?
50011.e: Wellington lies at the southern tip of New Zealand's North Island. It is the capital of the country.

50012.q: What nickname does Wellington have because of its weather?
50012.e: Strong winds often blow in Wellington because the city lies on a strait. People call it “Windy Wellington”.
50012.m: Wellington is known as a very windy city.

50013.q: What is special about Wellington's location in the world?
a: It is the southernmost capital of a country
It is the northernmost capital of a country
It is the highest capital of a country
It is the coldest capital of a country
50013.e: No other capital of an independent country lies as far south as Wellington.
50013.m: Wellington is the southernmost capital in the world.

50014.q: Why is Wellington so important for New Zealand?
a: Parliament and the government work there
50014.e: Wellington is the capital. Parliament and the government meet there. But the largest city is Auckland.
50014.m: New Zealand's parliament and government work in Wellington.

50015.q: Which red means of transport takes you up the hill in Wellington?
50015.e: The Wellington Cable Car is a red funicular railway. It runs from the city centre up to the Botanic Garden.
50015.m: A red funicular railway goes up the hill in Wellington.

50016.q: Which language does the name of the national museum Te Papa in Wellington come from?
50016.e: The Maori are the first people of New Zealand. The national museum in Wellington has a name in their language.
50016.m: Te Papa is a name in the Maori language.

50017.q: In which ocean is the island nation of Fiji?
50017.e: Fiji lies in the southern Pacific Ocean, north of New Zealand.

a: A country made up of many islands
50018.e: Fiji is a country in the Pacific. It is made up of over 300 islands.
50018.m: Fiji is a country made up of many islands.

50019.q: What is the weather usually like on the islands of Fiji?
50019.e: Fiji lies near the equator. It is warm there all year round.
50019.m: It is warm in Fiji all year round.

50020.q: Which trees grow on the beaches of Fiji?
50020.e: Many coconut palms grow on Fiji's warm beaches. Fir, birch and beech trees need cooler weather.
50020.m: Palm trees grow on Fiji's beaches.

50021.q: In which sport did Fiji win its first Olympic gold medal in 2016?
50021.e: At the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio, Fiji won gold in rugby sevens. It was the country's very first Olympic medal.
50021.m: Fiji won Olympic gold in rugby sevens in 2016.

50022.q: What grows under water around the islands of Fiji?
50022.e: Around Fiji there are colourful coral reefs with lots of fish. That is why many divers go there.
50022.m: Colourful coral reefs grow around Fiji.

50023.q: Which plant is grown a lot in Fiji to make sugar?
50023.e: A lot of sugar cane grows in Fiji. Sugar is made from it and sold to other countries.
50023.m: A lot of sugar cane is grown in Fiji.

a: A country on a large island
50024.e: Papua New Guinea lies on the eastern half of the island of New Guinea, plus many smaller islands.
50024.m: Papua New Guinea lies on the island of New Guinea.

50025.q: Which country does the western half of the island of New Guinea belong to?
50025.e: The island is divided. The east is Papua New Guinea, the west belongs to Indonesia.
50025.m: The western half of New Guinea belongs to Indonesia.

50026.q: Which island is even bigger than New Guinea?
50026.e: New Guinea is the second-largest island in the world. Only Greenland is bigger.
50026.m: New Guinea is the second-largest island in the world after Greenland.

50027.q: Which bird is shown on the flag of Papua New Guinea?
50027.e: The flag shows a yellow bird of paradise. These birds with splendid feathers live in the country's forests.
50027.m: There is a bird of paradise on the flag of Papua New Guinea.

50028.q: What is special about the languages in Papua New Guinea?
50028.e: Over 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, more than in any other country. Switzerland has four national languages.
50028.m: Over 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea.

50029.q: What is the weather usually like in Papua New Guinea?
50029.e: Papua New Guinea lies close to the equator. So it is almost always warm there, and it often rains.
50029.m: Papua New Guinea is usually warm and humid.

50030.q: What covers large parts of Papua New Guinea?
50030.e: Large parts of the country are covered with thick tropical rainforest. Many rare animals live there.
50030.m: Papua New Guinea has a lot of rainforest.

50031.q: Where is the island of Tasmania?
50031.e: Tasmania lies to the south, off the Australian mainland. It is a state of Australia.
50031.m: Tasmania lies south of the Australian mainland.

50032.q: Which small black predator with a loud screech lives in the wild almost only in Tasmania?
50032.e: The Tasmanian devil is a marsupial. It screams loudly when it eats.
50032.m: The Tasmanian devil lives in the wild almost only in Tasmania.

50034.e: The Dutch seafarer Abel Tasman reached the island in 1642. Later it was named after him.
50034.m: Tasmania is named after the seafarer Abel Tasman.

50035.q: How do you get from the Australian mainland to Tasmania?
50035.e: A wide stretch of sea, the Bass Strait, lies between Tasmania and the mainland. There is no bridge and no tunnel, so you travel by ferry or plane.
50035.m: You get to Tasmania by ferry or by plane.

50036.q: Which striped animal used to live in Tasmania and is now extinct?
50036.e: The thylacine had stripes on its back and so was also called the Tasmanian tiger. The last known animal died in a zoo in 1936.

50037.q: Which is the smallest state of Australia?
50037.e: Tasmania is the smallest of Australia's six states. Even so, it is bigger than Switzerland.

50038.q: What is there especially a lot of on the island of Tasmania?
50038.e: Tasmania has many mountains, lakes and thick forests. A large part of the island is national park.
50038.m: Tasmania has many forests and mountains.

50039.q: What is Tasmania's climate like compared with northern Australia?
50039.e: Tasmania lies far to the south and closer to the cold Southern Ocean. That is why it is cooler there than in hot northern Australia.
50039.m: Tasmania is cooler than northern Australia.

50040.q: How did most Aboriginal people live in the past?
50040.e: Aboriginal people hunted animals and gathered fruit, roots and seeds. They knew their land and its water holes very well.
50040.m: Aboriginal people used to live as hunters and gatherers.

50041.q: For about how long have Aboriginal people lived in Australia?
50041.e: Researchers estimate that the ancestors of Aboriginal people have lived in Australia for at least 50,000 years. It is one of the oldest cultures in the world.
50041.m: Aboriginal people have lived in Australia for over 50,000 years.

50042.q: What is the long Aboriginal wind instrument made from a hollow branch called?
50042.e: The didgeridoo is a wooden tube that was often hollowed out by termites. It has a deep, humming sound, a bit like the alphorn.
50042.m: The didgeridoo is the wind instrument of the Aboriginal people.

50043.q: What are many Aboriginal paintings made of?
50043.e: In dot painting, pictures are made from countless coloured dots. They often tell old stories.
50043.m: Many Aboriginal paintings are made of dots.

50044.q: What is the time called when, according to Aboriginal stories, the world was created?
50044.e: According to Aboriginal stories, ancestral beings shaped the land, the animals and the people in the Dreamtime.
50044.m: According to Aboriginal people, the world was created in the Dreamtime.

50045.q: What colours is the Aboriginal flag?
50045.e: Black stands for the people, red for the earth and the yellow circle for the sun. Today it is an official flag of Australia.
50045.m: The Aboriginal flag is black, red and yellow.

50046.q: Where did Aboriginal people already paint pictures a very long time ago?
50046.e: Australia has very old Aboriginal rock paintings. They show animals, people and stories.
50046.m: Aboriginal people painted pictures on rocks long ago.

50047.q: About how many languages did Aboriginal people speak before the Europeans came?
50047.e: There used to be over 250 Aboriginal languages. Today many of them are hardly spoken any more.
50047.m: Aboriginal people used to have over 250 languages.

50048.e: A boomerang is a curved, flat piece of wood. Aboriginal people in Australia have used it for a very long time.
50048.m: A boomerang is a curved throwing stick.

50049.q: What does a boomerang for playing do if you throw it correctly?
a: It flies back to the thrower
It falls to the ground at once
It stays still in the air
50049.e: Because of its special shape, it flies in a big curve. That is how it comes back to the thrower.
50049.m: A boomerang thrown correctly flies back.

50050.q: What did Aboriginal people mainly use boomerangs for in the past?
50050.e: Aboriginal people hunted animals such as birds with boomerangs. Boomerangs were also used as tools and toys.

50051.q: Do all boomerangs come back after being thrown?
a: No, hunting boomerangs keep flying straight
Yes, they all always come back
Yes, but only in strong wind
50051.e: Heavy hunting boomerangs fly far and straight to hit an animal. Only light returning boomerangs come back.

50052.q: What does a boomerang do the whole time while it is flying?
a: It stands still in the air
50052.e: A thrown boomerang spins round quickly. This spinning keeps it in the air and steers it into a curve.
50052.m: A boomerang spins quickly as it flies.

50053.q: Which group of animals does the wombat belong to?
50053.e: Wombats are marsupials like the kangaroo. The young grow up in the mother's pouch.

50054.q: What special shape is a wombat's poo?
50054.e: Wombats make cube-shaped droppings. They use them to mark their territory, and the cubes do not roll away.

50055.q: Which way does a mother wombat's pouch open?
50055.e: The pouch opens backwards. That way no earth falls in on the baby when she digs.

50056.e: Wombats dig long tunnels in the ground with their strong paws. They rest there during the day.
50056.m: Wombats live in burrows they dig themselves.

50057.e: Wombats are plant eaters. They mainly eat grasses, herbs and roots.
50057.m: Wombats eat plants such as grass and roots.

50058.q: When are wombats usually out and about?
50058.e: Wombats are mainly active at night. During the day they sleep in their cool burrows.
50058.m: Wombats are usually out and about at night.

50059.q: What does a wombat's body look like?
50059.e: Wombats are stocky and have short, strong legs. They look a bit like small bears.
50059.m: Wombats are round and have short legs.

50060.q: What is special about wombats' teeth?
a: They keep growing all their lives
They are pointed like a cat's
They only grow in the young
50060.e: As in rodents, wombats' teeth keep growing. They wear down when the wombats chew tough grass.

50061.q: What can the emu not do, even though it is a bird?
50061.e: The emu has only small wings and is far too heavy to fly. But it is a very good runner.
50061.m: The emu is a bird that cannot fly.

50062.q: Which bird is even bigger than the emu?
50062.e: The emu is the second-tallest bird in the world. Only the ostrich from Africa grows bigger.
50062.m: The emu is the second-tallest bird in the world after the ostrich.

50063.q: About how fast can an emu run?
50063.e: With its long legs an emu reaches about 50 kilometres per hour. That is as fast as a car in town.
50063.m: An emu can run at about 50 km/h.

50064.q: Who hatches the eggs in emus?
50064.e: In emus the male sits on the eggs for about eight weeks. Afterwards he also looks after the chicks.
50064.m: In emus the father hatches the eggs.

50065.e: Emu eggs are large and dark green. They weigh about as much as ten hens' eggs.

50066.q: Which animal holds up Australia's coat of arms together with the kangaroo?
50066.e: The emu and the kangaroo hold up Australia's shield together. Both animals live in the wild only there.
50066.m: The emu and the kangaroo are on Australia's coat of arms.

50067.q: About how tall can an emu grow?
50067.e: A fully grown emu can be almost two metres tall. That often makes it taller than a person.
50067.m: An emu can grow almost two metres tall.

50068.q: What do an emu's feathers look like?
50068.e: The emu's feathers are brownish grey and look scruffy like hair. This camouflages it well in dry grass.
50068.m: The emu has brown, shaggy feathers.

50069.q: In which ocean are the South Sea islands?
50069.e: The South Seas are the southern part of the Pacific Ocean. Thousands of islands lie there.
50069.m: The South Sea islands lie in the Pacific.

50070.q: Why is the small island nation of Tuvalu threatened by the sea?
a: Because its islands are very flat
50070.e: Tuvalu's islands are only a few metres above sea level. If the sea level rises, land can be flooded.
50070.m: Tuvalu is threatened because its islands are very flat.

50071.q: What do you call a ring-shaped coral island with a lake in the middle?
50071.e: An atoll is a ring of coral. In the middle there is a calm lagoon with light blue water.
50071.m: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island.

50072.q: Which trees typically grow on the beaches of the South Sea islands?
50072.e: Coconut palms stand on many South Sea beaches. Their nuts provide water, flesh and fibres.
50072.m: Coconut palms grow on the beaches of the South Seas.

50073.q: What are guests often given to wear around their necks as a welcome on many South Sea islands?
50073.e: In Polynesia, for example on Tahiti, guests are often given a garland of fragrant flowers. It is a sign of welcome.
50073.m: In the South Seas guests are often welcomed with a flower garland.

50074.q: Which country does the South Sea island of Tahiti belong to?
50074.e: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia. That is why French is also spoken there.

50075.q: What is the water in the lagoons of the South Seas often like?
50075.e: It is warm all year round in the South Seas. The water in the lagoons is clear and shines light blue.
50075.m: In the South Seas the water is warm and light blue.

50076.q: What does the name Polynesia mean?
50076.e: Polynesia comes from Greek: “poly” means many, “nesos” means island. The area has a great many islands.

50077.q: How did people in the past travel from one South Sea island to the next?
a: On rafts made of tree trunks
50077.e: The seafarers of the South Seas built canoes with outriggers that do not tip over. In them they travelled thousands of kilometres across the sea.
50077.m: The people of the South Seas travelled in outrigger canoes.

50078.q: What is the Great Ocean Road?
a: A hiking trail through the desert
50078.e: The Great Ocean Road is a famous road right beside the sea. It offers beautiful views of cliffs and beaches.
50078.m: The Great Ocean Road is a coastal road in Australia.

50079.q: In which country is the Great Ocean Road?
50079.e: The Great Ocean Road is in the south of Australia, in the state of Victoria.
50079.m: The Great Ocean Road is in Australia.

50080.q: Which big city is near the start of the Great Ocean Road?
50080.e: The road begins west of Melbourne. Many people go on a trip there from the city.
50080.m: The Great Ocean Road begins not far from Melbourne.

50081.q: What are the well-known rock pillars in the sea along the Great Ocean Road called?
50081.e: The Twelve Apostles are tall limestone pillars in the sea. Waves have washed them out of the coast.
50081.m: The Twelve Apostles are rock pillars on the Great Ocean Road.

50082.q: About how long is the Great Ocean Road?
50082.e: The road is about 240 kilometres long.
50082.m: The Great Ocean Road is about 240 kilometres long.

50083.q: Who built the Great Ocean Road in Australia?
50083.e: Soldiers who came back from the First World War built the road from 1919. It is also a memorial to the soldiers who died.
50083.m: Soldiers who had come home built the Great Ocean Road.

50084.q: Which animals can you often see in the eucalyptus trees along the Great Ocean Road?
50084.e: Wild koalas live in the eucalyptus forests along the road. They sleep for many hours in the trees.
50084.m: You can see koalas in the trees along the Great Ocean Road.

50085.q: What do you call a big building with many flats on top of each other?
50085.e: In cities, many families live in blocks of flats. That way lots of people fit on a small piece of land.
50085.m: In the city many families live in blocks of flats.

50086.q: What often happens in big cities when lots of cars are driving at the same time?
50086.e: When there are too many cars on the road, they can hardly move forward. This is called a traffic jam.
50086.m: Big cities often have traffic jams.

50087.q: In which country is the huge city of Mumbai?
50087.e: Mumbai lies on the west coast of India. Many millions of people live there.
50087.m: Mumbai is a huge city in India.

50088.q: In which country is the big city of São Paulo?
50088.e: São Paulo is the largest city in Brazil. It is in South America.
50088.m: São Paulo is Brazil's largest city.

50089.q: In which country is the huge city of Lagos?
50089.e: Lagos lies in Nigeria on the coast of West Africa. It is one of the largest cities in Africa.
50089.m: Lagos is a huge city in Nigeria.

50090.q: Where in a city are there especially many shops, offices and restaurants close together?
a: At the edge of the forest
50090.e: The centre of a city is where most is going on. There are lots of shops, offices and restaurants there.
50090.m: The city centre has many shops and offices.

50091.q: Which huge city lies on the River Thames?
50091.e: London is the capital of the United Kingdom. The Thames flows right through the middle of the city.

50092.q: In which country is the big city of Shanghai?
50092.e: Shanghai lies on the east coast of China. It is one of the largest cities in the world.
50092.m: Shanghai is a huge city in China.

50093.q: What do you call a small settlement with a few houses in the countryside?
50093.e: A village is a small settlement in the countryside. Many people there know each other.
50093.m: In the countryside many people live in villages.

50094.q: Where do many people in the countryside work?
50094.e: In the countryside there are many fields and meadows. Farmers work there on their farms.
50094.m: In the countryside many people work on farms.

50095.q: Where is there usually more space and fewer houses?
50095.e: In the countryside the houses are further apart. In between there are fields, meadows and woods.
50095.m: In the countryside there is lots of space and few houses.

50096.q: Where do children in some villages without running water get their water from?
50096.e: In some villages in Africa and Asia there are no water pipes in the houses. Then children and adults carry water home from the well.
50096.m: In some villages people fetch water from the well.

50097.q: What is an alp in Switzerland?
a: A summer pasture in the mountains
A railway station in the city
50097.e: In summer, farmers take their cows up to the alp. There the animals eat fresh grass in the mountains.
50097.m: In summer the cows graze on the alp.

50098.q: What do farmers in some poor countries still use to plough their fields today?
50098.e: Not all farmers can buy a tractor. Then strong animals such as oxen or water buffalo pull the plough.
50098.m: In some countries strong animals still pull the plough.

50099.q: What is it called when many people move from the countryside to the city?
50099.e: Many people leave their village and move to the city because they are looking for work there. This is called rural exodus.
50099.m: In a rural exodus people move from the countryside to the city.

a: A group of just a few houses
50100.e: A hamlet is even smaller than a village. Often there are just a few farmhouses.
50100.m: A hamlet has only a few houses.

50101.q: What are the cattle herders on horseback in the western USA called?
50101.e: Cowboys drive large herds of cattle in the western USA. The word comes from “cow”.
50101.m: Cowboys herd cattle in the USA.

50102.e: A stilt house stands on long posts. This way the floor of the house is higher than the ground or the water.
50102.m: A stilt house stands on posts.

50103.q: Why do many houses by the water stand on posts?
50103.e: When the water rises, the house on posts stays dry. The posts lift the floor above the water.
50103.m: Posts protect the house from floods.

50104.q: Where were the stilt house settlements in Switzerland thousands of years ago?
50104.e: People built their villages on the shores of lakes and in moors. Many remains have been found on Lake Zurich and Lake Biel.
50104.m: The old stilt houses stood on the shores of lakes.

50105.q: What were the pile dwellings found at Swiss lakes?
a: Houses on wooden posts on the lake shore
50105.e: A few thousand years ago people built their houses on posts on the shores of lakes. Since 2011 the pile dwellings around the Alps have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
50105.m: The pile dwellings around the Alps are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50106.q: What were the posts of the old pile dwellings made of?
50106.e: People drove tree trunks into the soft ground. On top they built their houses of wood, clay and reeds.
50106.m: The posts of the pile dwellings were made of wood.

50107.q: In which period did people in Switzerland begin to build pile dwelling villages?
50107.e: The first pile dwelling villages were built in the New Stone Age, over 6000 years ago. People were already farmers then.
50107.m: The first pile dwellers lived in the New Stone Age.

50108.q: Why have remains of the old pile dwellings survived for so long?
a: They lay under water and mud
50108.e: Under water and in mud there is no air. That is why wood, seeds and tools rotted only very slowly.
50108.m: Old remains survive a long time in mud under water.

50109.q: Which city in Italy stands on millions of wooden posts in the water?
50109.e: Venice was built in a lagoon. The houses stand on many wooden posts in the ground.

50110.q: Why do people in the tropics often build their houses on stilts?
50110.e: In the tropics it rains a lot and the ground is often wet. On stilts the house stays dry and animals find it harder to get in.

a: People who move from place to place
50111.e: Nomads do not have a fixed home. They move with their animals from place to place.
50111.m: Nomads move around with their animals.

50112.q: What do nomads do with their tent when they move on?
a: They take it down and take it with them
50112.e: Nomads need a home they can carry. So they take down their tent and load it onto animals or carts.
50112.m: Nomads take their tent with them when they move on.

50113.q: What is a yurt covered with on the outside to keep it warm?
50113.e: Felt is made from sheep's wool. It keeps out the cold and the wind well.
50113.m: A yurt is covered with warm felt.

50114.q: What do many nomads mainly live from?
50114.e: The animals give the nomads milk, meat, wool and leather. That is why the herds are very valuable to them.

50115.q: Which animals do many Sami in northern Scandinavia herd?
50115.e: The Sami live in the far north of Norway, Sweden and Finland. Many of them raise reindeer.

50116.q: What is the pointed tent of the Indigenous peoples of the North American prairie called?
50116.e: A tipi is made of long poles and animal skins. It is pointed like a cone.
50116.m: The tipi is a pointed tent.

50117.q: Why do nomads keep moving on with their herds?
a: They are looking for food and water
They want to go to the cinema
They are looking for high-rise buildings
50117.e: When the animals have eaten the grass in one place, they need new pastures. That is why the nomads move on.
50117.m: Nomads move on when their animals need new food.

50118.q: Which animals are especially important for the nomads of Mongolia?
50118.e: In Mongolia even small children ride horses. As well as horses, the nomads also keep sheep, goats and cattle.
50118.m: Horses are very important for the nomads of Mongolia.

50119.q: What are the nomads of the Arabian deserts called?
50119.e: Bedouins live in the deserts of Arabia and North Africa. In the past they lived in tents made of goat hair.
50119.m: Bedouins are nomads of the Arabian desert.

a: A boat that people live on
A house on posts in a lake
50120.e: A houseboat has a kitchen, beds and a living room. People live there like in a flat, but on the water.
50120.m: On a houseboat you live on the water.

50121.q: In which city are there many houseboats on the canals?
50121.e: In Amsterdam in the Netherlands there are over 2000 houseboats. They are moored along the banks of the canals.
50121.m: Many people in Amsterdam live on houseboats.

50122.q: What are the canals in Amsterdam called?
50122.e: The grachten are canals in the middle of the city. Many houseboats are moored along their banks.
50122.m: The canals in Amsterdam are called grachten.

50123.q: In which country do houseboats travel along the waterways of Kerala?
50123.e: Kerala is in the south of India. Tourists there like to spend the night on houseboats made of wood and bamboo.
50123.m: There are many houseboats in Kerala in India.

50124.q: What is used to tie a houseboat to the bank?
50124.e: A houseboat is tied to the bank with strong ropes. That way it does not drift away.
50124.m: Ropes hold the houseboat to the bank.

50125.q: In which country do long, narrow houseboats travel on many canals?
50125.e: England has a large network of canals. Long, narrow boats travel on them, and people can live on them too.
50125.m: Narrowboats travel on canals in England.

50126.q: On which river in Paris are there many houseboats?
50126.e: The Seine flows right through Paris. Along its banks there are many boats that people live on.
50126.m: In Paris there are houseboats on the Seine.

50127.e: Skyscrapers are very tall high-rise buildings. They almost seem to scrape the clouds.
50127.m: A skyscraper is a very tall building.

50128.q: What are the outer walls of many modern skyscrapers made of?
50128.e: Many skyscrapers have walls made of glass. That lets a lot of daylight into the offices and flats.
50128.m: Modern skyscrapers often have glass walls.

50129.q: What takes people up quickly in a skyscraper?
50129.e: Tall buildings have fast lifts. Without a lift you would have to climb a great many stairs.
50129.m: In a skyscraper you take the lift up.

50130.q: In which city is the Prime Tower, one of the tallest high-rise buildings in Switzerland?
50130.e: The Prime Tower is in Zurich and is 126 metres tall. From 2011 to 2015 it was the tallest building in Switzerland.
50130.m: The Prime Tower is in Zurich.

50131.q: In which city is the tallest building in Switzerland (as of 2025)?
50131.e: The second Roche Tower in Basel is 205 metres tall. It is the tallest building in Switzerland.
50131.m: The tallest building in Switzerland is in Basel.

50132.q: Why are very tall buildings often built in big cities?
50132.e: In big cities land is scarce and expensive. If you build upwards, many people fit on a small piece of land.
50132.m: Where there is little space, people build upwards.

50133.q: In which Asian city are the Petronas Twin Towers?
50133.e: The Petronas Towers are in Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia. The two towers are connected by a bridge.
50133.m: The Petronas Towers are in Kuala Lumpur.

50134.q: What is the strong frame of a skyscraper made of?
50134.e: Steel and concrete are very strong. They carry the great weight of the tall building.
50134.m: Skyscrapers have a frame of steel and concrete.

50135.q: Which city in Asia has especially many skyscrapers by the harbour and was British for a long time?
50135.e: Hong Kong has a great many high-rise buildings in a small space. Until 1997 the city belonged to the United Kingdom.
50135.m: Hong Kong is a city full of skyscrapers.

50136.q: Which language do the most people speak as their mother tongue?
50136.e: Chinese, especially Mandarin, is the mother tongue of more people than any other language. That is because a great many people live in China.
50136.m: Chinese is the most common mother tongue in the world.

50137.q: Which language is spoken in Austria?
50137.e: In Austria people speak German, as in a large part of Switzerland. But there are some words of their own, for example “Paradeiser” for tomato.

50138.q: About how many languages are there in the world?
50138.e: Researchers count about 7000 languages in the world. Some of them are spoken by only a few people.
50138.m: There are about 7000 languages in the world.

50139.q: Which language do the most people in the world learn as a foreign language?
50139.e: English is learnt at school in many countries. Pilots and air traffic controllers also speak English to each other.
50139.m: English is the most important foreign language in the world.

50140.q: In which direction is Arabic written?
50140.e: Arabic is written from right to left. English is written from left to right.
50140.m: Arabic is written from right to left.

50141.q: Which two languages are mainly spoken in Belgium?
50141.e: In the north of Belgium people speak Dutch, in the south French. In the east there is also a small German-speaking area.
50141.m: Belgium mainly speaks Dutch and French.

50142.q: What does Chinese use instead of letters?
50142.e: Chinese has thousands of characters. One character often stands for a whole word or a syllable.

50143.q: Which language is spoken in the province of Quebec in Canada?
50143.e: In Canada people speak English and French. In Quebec most people speak French.

50145.q: How do you greet friends in Italian?
50145.e: People say “ciao” to friends in Italy and in Ticino. It means “hello” and also “bye”.
50145.m: In Italian you greet friends with “ciao”.

50146.q: How do you say “hello” in Spanish?
50146.e: “Hola” means “hello” in Spanish. The H is not pronounced.

50147.q: How do people in Japan often greet each other?
50147.e: In Japan people bow when they greet each other. The deeper the bow, the more polite it is.
50147.m: In Japan people bow as a greeting.

50148.q: What does the word “aloha” mean in Hawaii?
50148.e: People greet each other with “aloha” in Hawaii. The word also means love and friendship.
50148.m: In Hawaii people greet each other with “aloha”.

50149.q: How do you greet someone politely in Swiss German?
50149.e: In German-speaking Switzerland people say “Grüezi” to people they address formally. To friends they say “Hoi” or “Sali”.
50149.m: In Swiss German you greet politely with “Grüezi”.

50150.q: How do you greet someone in Romansh?
50150.e: “Allegra” is a Romansh greeting. You hear it in the Grisons.

50151.q: How do the Maori in New Zealand traditionally greet each other?
a: They press their noses and foreheads together
50151.e: This greeting is called the “hongi”. The nose and forehead touch.
50151.m: The Maori greet with nose and forehead.

50152.q: How many kisses on the cheek do people in Switzerland often give as a greeting?
50152.e: In Switzerland friends and relatives often give each other three kisses. In other countries it is one or two.
50152.m: In Switzerland people often greet each other with three kisses.

50153.q: Which English greeting do you use in the morning?
50153.e: In the morning you say “good morning”. “Good night” is for bedtime and “goodbye” is for leaving.
50153.m: In the morning you say “good morning”.

50154.e: “Merhaba” is a greeting in Turkish. You use it like “hello”.

50155.q: Which country in South Asia lies north-west of India and has over 200 million inhabitants?
50155.e: Pakistan lies west of India and borders it. Over 200 million people live there.
50155.m: Pakistan has a very large population.

50156.q: About how many people live in India (as of 2025)?
50156.e: About 1.4 billion people live in India. That is over 150 times more than in Switzerland.
50156.m: About 1.4 billion people live in India.

50157.q: About how many people live in Japan (as of 2024)?
50157.e: About 124 million people live in Japan. Most live in big cities on the coast.
50157.m: About 120 million people live in Japan.

50159.q: Which country in Asia has the most inhabitants after India and China?
50159.e: Over 270 million people live in Indonesia. The country is made up of thousands of islands.
50159.m: Indonesia has a very large population.

50160.q: Which country has the second-largest population in the world (as of 2025)?
50160.e: China has about 1.4 billion inhabitants. Only India has slightly more people.
50160.m: China has the second-largest population in the world.

50161.q: About how many people live in Switzerland (as of 2024)?
50161.e: At the end of 2024 about 9 million people lived in Switzerland. Compared with countries in Asia, that is not many.
50161.m: About 9 million people live in Switzerland.

50162.q: Which small city-state in South-East Asia has very many people in a small space?
50162.e: Singapore is a city and a country at the same time. About 6 million people live there in a small area.
50162.m: In Singapore many people live in a small space.

50163.q: In which Asian country is the huge city of Dhaka?
50163.e: Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh. The city is very densely populated.
50163.m: Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh.

50164.q: What colour are school buses in the USA usually?
50164.e: School buses in the USA are yellow. That makes them easy to see in traffic.
50164.m: School buses in the USA are yellow.

50165.q: How do many children in Switzerland get to school?
50165.e: Many Swiss children walk to school. On the way they often meet other children.

50166.q: How does the Swiss road safety rule for crossing the street continue: “Wait, look, listen, ...”?
50166.e: The rule goes “Wait, look, listen, walk” (in Swiss German “Warte, luege, lose, laufe”). You wait, look, listen and only then cross the road.

50167.q: How do children in the Netherlands especially often get to school?
50167.e: The Netherlands is flat and has many cycle paths. That is why a great many children there cycle to school.
50167.m: Many children in the Netherlands cycle.

50168.q: How do some children in Bangladesh get to school when everything is flooded?
50168.e: Bangladesh often has floods. There are even schools on boats that pick the children up.
50168.m: In Bangladesh some children go to school by boat.

50169.q: What do children in many countries, for example England, wear at school?
50169.e: In England many children wear the same clothes at school. These clothes are called a school uniform.
50169.m: Many children in England wear a school uniform.

50170.q: What helps children to be seen well on the way to school in the dark?
50170.e: Reflective strips shine brightly when car headlights fall on them. That way drivers see the children early.
50170.m: Reflective strips make children visible in the dark.

50171.q: Where is the safest place to cross the road in Switzerland?
50171.e: Cars must stop at a zebra crossing. Even so, you look left, right and left again first.
50171.m: Cross the road at the zebra crossing.

50172.q: Why do some children in the world have a very long way to school?
a: The school is far away and there is no bus
50172.e: In some countries there are few schools in the countryside. Children there sometimes walk for over an hour.
50172.m: Some children walk a very long way to school.

50173.e: A bazaar is a large market in the Middle East. In many narrow lanes there are stalls and small shops.
50173.m: A bazaar is a large market.

50174.q: In which city is the famous Grand Bazaar?
50174.e: The Grand Bazaar in Istanbul is one of the largest covered markets in the world. It has thousands of shops.
50174.m: The Grand Bazaar is in Istanbul.

50175.q: What is a market in Morocco called?
50175.e: In Morocco and other Arab countries the market is called a souk. There you can buy spices, carpets and leather goods. The medina is the old town, where the souk often is.
50175.m: In Morocco the market is called a souk.

50176.e: In a market hall the stalls are inside a large building. That way you can shop even when it rains.
50176.m: In a market hall you shop under a roof.

50177.q: What do people do when shopping at many bazaars?
a: They always pay the price on the label
They only pay a week later
They may only buy one thing
50177.e: When haggling, buyer and seller bargain over the price. In the end they agree.
50177.m: At a bazaar people haggle over the price.

50178.q: What is mainly sold at the Zibelemärit in Bern?
50178.e: The Zibelemärit takes place in Bern every year in November. “Zibele” is Bernese German for onions.
50178.m: The Zibelemärit in Bern sells onions.

50179.q: What do many people buy from the stalls at a night market in Thailand?
50179.e: Night markets open when it gets dark. At many stalls food is freshly cooked that you can eat straight away.
50179.m: At the night market there is freshly cooked food.

50180.q: What do you buy at a flea market?
50180.e: At a flea market people sell things they no longer need. You can find old toys, books and clothes there.
50180.m: A flea market sells second-hand things.

50181.q: On which continent is the most rice grown?
50181.e: About nine out of ten grains of rice in the world grow in Asia. There, rice is the most important food for a great many people.
50181.m: Most of the world's rice grows in Asia.

50182.q: What do rice plants often stand in while they grow?
50182.e: Many rice fields are flooded with water. The water also keeps weeds away.
50182.m: Rice often grows in fields that are under water.

50183.q: What do you call rice fields that lie like steps on a mountain?
50183.e: On steep slopes farmers build flat steps into the mountain. That way the water stays on the field.
50183.m: Rice terraces are fields like steps on a mountain.

50184.q: Which two countries harvest the most rice?
50184.e: Together, India and China harvest more than half of the world's rice. In both countries rice is a staple food.
50184.m: India and China harvest the most rice.

50185.q: Which dish is made from rice?
50185.e: Risotto is a creamy rice dish from Italy. People in Ticino love it too.

50186.q: Which group of plants does rice belong to?
50186.e: Rice is a grass, just like wheat and barley. Its grains are the seeds of the plant.
50186.m: Rice is a grass whose grains we eat.

50187.q: In which Swiss canton is rice grown?
50187.e: Rice for risotto grows near Ascona in Ticino. It is one of the northernmost places in Europe where rice is grown.

50188.q: What is rice called when the brown skin stays on?
50188.e: In brown rice the thin brown skin stays on the grain. It contains many healthy substances.
50188.m: Brown rice still has its brown skin.

50189.q: What is a small, strong coffee from Italy called?
50189.e: An espresso is a small, strong coffee. It is made with hot water under high pressure.
50189.m: An espresso is a small, strong coffee.

50190.q: Which part of the coffee plant is roasted?
50190.e: Coffee beans are the seeds inside the fruit of the coffee bush. They are roasted and ground.
50190.m: Coffee is made from roasted beans.

50191.q: What are the red fruits of the coffee bush called?
50191.e: The fruits look like small red cherries. Each one usually contains two coffee beans.
50191.m: Coffee beans are inside red coffee cherries.

50192.q: What colour are coffee beans after roasting?
50192.e: Raw coffee beans are greenish. Only when they are roasted do they turn brown and smell nice.

50193.q: Which country harvests the most coffee (as of 2023)?
50193.e: Brazil in South America harvests almost a third of the world's coffee. Huge coffee fields lie there in the warm highlands.

50194.q: Which substance in coffee keeps you awake?
50194.e: Caffeine is a substance that makes tired people more alert. That is why coffee is not for children.
50194.m: The caffeine in coffee keeps you awake.

50195.q: In which climate does the coffee bush grow?
50195.e: Coffee needs warmth and rain and cannot cope with frost. It grows in countries around the equator.
50195.m: Coffee only grows where it is warm.

50196.q: Which country in Africa does the coffee plant come from?
50196.e: Arabica coffee has its home in the highlands of Ethiopia. From there it spread around the world.
50196.m: The coffee plant comes from Ethiopia.

50197.q: What does a raw cocoa bean taste like?
50197.e: Raw cocoa beans taste very bitter. Only with lots of sugar do they become sweet chocolate.

50198.q: Which country in West Africa harvests the most cocoa?
50198.e: The Ivory Coast harvests more cocoa than any other country. Almost half of the world's cocoa beans come from there (as of 2024).
50198.m: The Ivory Coast is the biggest cocoa country.

50199.q: Which country in West Africa also grows a lot of cocoa?
50199.e: Ghana is one of the most important cocoa countries in the world. It lies on the Gulf of Guinea.
50199.m: Ghana in West Africa also grows a lot of cocoa.

50200.q: Where do the fruits grow on the cocoa tree?
50200.e: Cocoa fruits grow directly on the trunk and on thick branches. That looks unusual.
50200.m: Cocoa fruits hang directly on the trunk.

50201.q: What is the fruit of the cocoa tree often called?
50201.e: The long fruit is often called a cocoa pod. Inside, many cocoa beans lie in white pulp.
50201.m: The cocoa beans are inside the cocoa pod.

50202.q: Which country is famous for chocolate even though no cocoa grows there?
50202.e: Switzerland is too cold for cocoa trees. The beans are imported and made into chocolate here.
50202.m: Switzerland makes fine chocolate from imported cocoa.

50203.q: Which people in Central America already drank cocoa a long time ago?
50203.e: The Maya made a bitter drink from cocoa. The cocoa tree comes from America.

50204.q: Which part of the cocoa is in white chocolate?
50204.e: White chocolate contains the pale fat of the cocoa bean. The brown cocoa powder is missing, which is why it is white.

50205.q: What did Daniel Peter from Vevey invent?
50205.e: Daniel Peter was the first to mix milk into chocolate. That is how milk chocolate was created in the 19th century.
50205.m: A Swiss man invented milk chocolate.

50206.q: What colour is a ripe banana usually?
50206.e: Ripe bananas usually have a yellow skin. Brown spots show that it is very ripe.

50207.q: What colour are bananas when they are harvested?
50207.e: Bananas are picked green. They only ripen on the long journey and in storage.

50208.q: What do you call a large field with many banana plants?
50208.e: On a plantation only one kind of plant grows in large numbers. Bananas often grow on huge plantations.

50209.q: How do bananas grow on the plant?
a: One by one in the ground
50209.e: Many bananas grow together on one large stalk. One bunch can carry over a hundred bananas.

50210.q: The banana plant looks like a tree. What is it really?
50210.e: The banana's stem is not made of wood but of rolled-up leaves. That is why it is a giant herb and not a tree.
50210.m: The banana plant is a giant herb, not a tree.

50211.q: Which country in South America do many of our bananas come from?
50211.e: Ecuador sells more bananas abroad than any other country. It lies on the equator, where it is always warm.

50212.q: How do bananas travel from South America to Europe?
50212.e: Bananas cross the Atlantic in refrigerated ships. The cold slows down the ripening.
50212.m: Bananas come to Europe by ship.

50213.q: What happens to a banana as it ripens?
50213.e: As it ripens, starch is turned into sugar. That is why a ripe banana tastes sweet and is soft.
50213.m: Ripe bananas are sweet and soft.

50214.q: Which part of the tea plant is black tea made from?
50214.e: For tea, the leaves of the tea bush are picked and dried. With hot water poured over them they make tea.
50214.m: Tea is made from the leaves of the tea plant.

50215.q: In which country is there a famous tea ceremony with green tea?
50215.e: In Japan green tea is prepared in a formal ceremony. Every movement follows a fixed order.
50215.m: Japan is known for its tea ceremony.

50216.q: Darjeeling is a well-known kind of tea. Which country does it come from?
50216.e: Darjeeling is an area in the north-east of India. Tea grows there at the foot of the Himalayas.

50217.q: In England, what is the time in the afternoon when people drink tea called?
50217.e: In England people like to have a cup of tea in the afternoon. It often comes with small cakes or sandwiches.
50217.m: In England people drink tea at teatime.

50218.q: What is green tea as a fine powder from Japan called?
50218.e: Matcha is finely ground green tea. It is whisked with hot water until frothy.
50218.m: Matcha is green tea in powder form.

50219.q: Which leaves are the best to pick for tea?
a: The young leaves at the top
The old leaves at the bottom
50219.e: Usually the bud and the top young leaves are picked. They make the finest tea.
50219.m: For good tea you pick the youngest leaves.

50220.q: Which tea is not made from the tea plant?
50220.e: Peppermint tea is a herbal tea made from mint leaves. It does not come from the tea bush.
50220.m: Peppermint tea is a herbal tea, not real tea.

50221.q: Where do green and black tea come from?
a: Green tea from grass, black from leaves
Green tea from leaves, black from roots
50221.e: Both come from the same tea bush. They are just processed differently.
50221.m: Green and black tea come from the same bush.

50222.q: Which country grows the most tea today?
50222.e: China harvests more tea than any other country. People there have been drinking tea for thousands of years.

50223.q: Which continent does maize come from?
50223.e: Maize was first grown by people in America. Only much later did it reach the rest of the world.

50224.q: In which present-day country was maize first grown?
50224.e: Thousands of years ago, people in Mexico bred maize from a wild grass. It is still very important there today.
50224.m: Maize was first grown in Mexico.

50225.q: What do you get when you heat certain maize kernels strongly?
50225.e: There is a little water in every kernel. When heated it turns to steam and the kernel bursts open.

50226.q: What is the part called on which the maize kernels sit?
50226.e: The maize kernels sit in rows on the cob. It is wrapped in green leaves.
50226.m: Maize kernels sit on the cob.

50227.q: Which Ticino dish is made from maize meal?
50227.e: Polenta is a porridge made from maize meal. It is very popular in Ticino and northern Italy.

50228.q: Who brought maize to Europe about 500 years ago?
50228.e: After the voyages of Columbus, Spanish seafarers brought maize to Europe. Before that it was unknown here.
50228.m: Spanish seafarers brought maize to Europe.

50229.q: What is a lot of maize grown for in Switzerland?
50229.e: A large part of Swiss maize is fed to cows and other animals. Often the whole plant is chopped up.
50229.m: In Switzerland maize is often animal feed.

50230.q: Which flatbread from Mexico is often made from maize?
50230.e: Tortillas are thin, round flatbreads. In Mexico they are traditionally made from maize flour.
50230.m: Tortillas are flatbreads made from maize.

50231.q: Which mountain range does the potato come from?
50231.e: The potato was first grown in the Andes in South America. Only later did it come to Europe.
50231.m: The potato comes from the Andes.

50232.q: Which potatoes do people in Switzerland like to eat with raclette?
50232.e: With raclette, Swiss people eat “Gschwellti”, potatoes boiled in their skins. Melted cheese is put over them.
50232.m: Raclette comes with potatoes boiled in their skins.

50233.q: Where do potatoes grow on the plant?
50233.e: Potatoes are tubers that grow under the ground. You have to dig them out of the soil.

50234.q: Which Swiss dish is made from grated potatoes?
50234.e: For rösti you grate potatoes and fry them golden brown in a pan. It is a typical Swiss dish.

50235.q: Which country in the Andes has a great many kinds of potato?
50235.e: Peru has thousands of different kinds of potato. Some are blue, red or purple.
50235.m: Peru has especially many kinds of potato.

50236.q: What should you do with green parts on potatoes?
50236.e: Green parts contain a poisonous substance called solanine. So you cut them off generously.

50237.q: What do you make from potato sticks in hot oil?
50237.e: For chips you cut potatoes into sticks. Then you deep-fry them in hot oil.

50238.q: What do you call potatoes that are put into the ground in spring?
50238.e: A new plant grows from a seed potato. In autumn, many new tubers hang from it.
50238.m: New potatoes grow from seed potatoes.

50239.q: What is mainly baked from wheat flour?
50239.e: Wheat flour, water and yeast make a dough. Bread is baked from it.
50239.m: Bread is often baked from wheat flour.

50240.q: What is the part of the wheat called where the grains sit?
50240.e: At the top of the stalk, wheat has an ear. The grains sit close together in it.
50240.m: Wheat grains sit in the ear.

50241.q: What colour is a ripe wheat field?
50241.e: Young wheat is green. When it is ripe, the field shines golden yellow.

50242.q: Which machine is used to harvest wheat today?
50242.e: The combine harvester cuts the stalks and separates the grains from the straw. It does both in one go.

50243.q: What do you get when you grind wheat grains finely?
50243.e: In the mill the grains are ground into a fine powder. This powder is flour.

50244.q: Which cereal is spaghetti made from?
50244.e: Spaghetti is made from wheat, more exactly from durum wheat semolina. That is why it stays nicely firm when cooked.

50245.q: In which season is wheat harvested in Switzerland?
50245.e: Wheat is usually harvested in July and August. Then the grains are ripe and dry.
50245.m: In Switzerland wheat is harvested in summer.

50246.q: Which country is called the breadbasket of Europe because of its large wheat fields?
50246.e: Ukraine has very fertile, dark soil. Wheat and other cereals grow there on huge fields.
50246.m: Ukraine is called the breadbasket of Europe.

50247.e: Cotton fibres are spun into yarn. From this, fabric for clothes such as T-shirts is woven.
50247.m: Many clothes are made of cotton.

50248.q: What do cotton fibres look like?
50248.e: Cotton fibres are white and soft like cotton wool. They wrap around the seeds of the plant.

50249.e: Cotton grows on a plant, the cotton bush. Wool from sheep is something completely different.

50250.q: Which large country in Asia grows a lot of cotton?
50250.e: India is one of the biggest cotton countries in the world. Cotton has been made into cloth there for thousands of years.
50250.m: India grows a lot of cotton.

50251.q: What weather does the cotton plant need?
50251.e: Cotton only grows in warm areas. It needs lots of sun and no frost.

50253.q: What material are most jeans made of?
50253.e: Jeans fabric is called denim and is tightly woven cotton. It is very tough.
50253.m: Jeans are mostly made of cotton.

50254.q: What does cotton need a lot of to grow?
50254.e: For a single T-shirt, the cotton needs many litres of water. In dry areas the fields are watered.
50254.m: Cotton needs a lot of water.

50255.q: Which country does sushi come from?
50255.e: Sushi is a typical dish from Japan. Today it is eaten all over the world.

50256.q: What is the most important ingredient in sushi?
50256.e: Sushi is always made with vinegared rice. Fish, vegetables or egg are added.
50256.m: Sushi is always made with rice.

50257.q: What is often on top of sushi?
50257.e: Many kinds of sushi have slices of raw fish on top, for example salmon or tuna. There is also sushi with vegetables.
50257.m: Sushi often has raw fish on top.

50258.q: What do people in Japan often eat sushi with?
50258.e: In Japan people eat with chopsticks. But you may also eat sushi with your fingers.
50258.m: In Japan people eat with chopsticks.

50259.q: What is the dark sheet around a sushi roll made of?
50259.e: The thin sheet is called nori and is made of dried seaweed. It holds the roll together.
50259.m: The sheet around sushi is made of seaweed.

50260.q: What is the hot green paste served with sushi called?
50260.e: Wasabi is a very hot green paste. You only use a tiny bit of it.

50261.q: Which sauce do people often dip sushi in?
50261.e: Soy sauce is a salty, dark sauce made from soya beans. You dip the sushi in it briefly.
50261.m: Sushi often comes with soy sauce.

50262.q: What is mixed into sushi rice?
50262.e: The cooked rice is mixed with rice vinegar, a little sugar and salt. That makes it slightly sour and sticky.
50262.m: Sushi rice is seasoned with vinegar.

50263.e: Cinnamon is the dried bark of the cinnamon tree. As it dries, it rolls up into sticks.

50264.q: Which spice was once so expensive that it was called black gold?
50264.e: Pepper came to Europe from India along long routes. That is why it used to be very expensive.
50264.m: Pepper used to be as valuable as gold.

50265.q: Which spice makes curry powder yellow?
50265.e: Turmeric is a bright yellow root from Asia. When ground, it gives curry its yellow colour.

50266.q: Which hot spice is a root that grows in the ground?
50266.e: Ginger is a knobbly root from Asia. It tastes fresh and hot.
50266.m: Ginger grows as a root in the ground.

50267.q: Which islands in Asia used to be called the Spice Islands?
50267.e: Nutmeg and cloves grew on the Moluccas in Indonesia. Seafarers from Europe sailed a long way to get there.
50267.m: The Moluccas are called the Spice Islands.

50268.q: Which spice looks like small nails?
50268.e: Cloves are dried flower buds. With their little heads they look like small nails.

50269.q: Which spice do people like to sprinkle on rice pudding?
50269.e: Cinnamon and sugar go very well with sweet rice pudding. Cinnamon tastes warm and sweetish.
50269.m: People like to sprinkle cinnamon on rice pudding.

50270.e: Pepper is a climbing plant from India. The corns hang in long clusters on the vine.
50270.m: Pepper grows on a climbing plant.

50271.q: Which expensive spice is grown in the village of Mund in Valais?
50271.e: Saffron is made of the red threads of a crocus flower. It has been grown in Mund in Valais for a long time.

50272.q: Which continent does the pineapple come from?
50272.e: The pineapple's home is in South America. Seafarers later brought it to other warm countries.
50272.m: The pineapple comes from South America.

a: High up on a palm tree
50273.e: The pineapple grows from the middle of a plant with spiky leaves. The plant is about one metre tall.
50273.m: The pineapple grows on a low plant.

50274.q: What does a pineapple have on top?
50274.e: At the top of the fruit there is a bunch of stiff green leaves. It is called the crown.
50274.m: The pineapple has a tuft of leaves on top.

50275.q: Which country in Central America do many of our pineapples come from?
50275.e: Costa Rica sells more fresh pineapples abroad than any other country. It is warm there all year round.
50275.m: Many pineapples come from Costa Rica.

50276.q: What can you grow from the top of a pineapple?
50276.e: If you put the top in soil, it grows roots. That way a new pineapple plant grows.
50276.m: A new plant grows from the top of a pineapple.

50277.q: What does a ripe pineapple taste like?
50277.e: Ripe pineapple is very juicy and sweet. It also tastes a little sour.
50277.m: Ripe pineapple tastes sweet and juicy.
