50278.q: Which pizza is known for its pieces of pineapple?
50278.e: A Hawaiian pizza has ham and pineapple on it. Hawaii used to be famous for its pineapple fields.
50278.m: Hawaiian pizza has pineapple on it.

50279.q: What does the skin of a pineapple feel like?
50279.e: The skin of the pineapple is made of many hard scales. You cut it off before eating.
50279.m: Pineapple skin is rough and prickly.

50280.q: Where do the pilots sit in an aeroplane?
50280.e: The cockpit is right at the front of the aeroplane. The pilots sit there with all the instruments.
50280.m: The pilots fly the aeroplane from the cockpit.

50281.q: Which card do you need to get on an aeroplane?
50281.e: Your boarding pass shows your name, your flight and your seat. It is checked when you get on.
50281.m: Without a boarding pass you may not board the aeroplane.

50282.q: About how high does a large passenger plane fly on long journeys?
50282.e: On long journeys large planes usually fly about 10 to 12 kilometres high. The air there is thin and they make good progress.
50282.m: On long flights planes fly much higher than the clouds.

50283.q: Which ocean do you fly over on the way from Zurich to New York?
50283.e: New York is in North America on the other side of the Atlantic. The flight takes about eight to nine hours.
50283.m: The Atlantic lies between Europe and North America.

50284.q: Who looks after the passengers during the flight?
50284.e: The cabin crew show the safety rules, bring food and help the passengers.
50284.m: The cabin crew look after the safety and comfort of passengers.

50285.q: What must you fasten at your seat during take-off and landing?
50285.e: During take-off and landing every passenger must be strapped in. The belt protects you when it gets bumpy.
50285.m: On a plane you fasten your seat belt for take-off and landing.

50286.q: What is the luggage called that you may take with you into the aeroplane cabin?
50286.e: You may take a small bag or a small suitcase to your seat. Large suitcases go in the hold of the aeroplane.
50286.m: Hand luggage travels with you in the cabin.

50287.q: Which is the largest passenger aeroplane in the world?
50287.e: The Airbus A380 has two decks along its whole length. It can carry over 500 people.
50287.m: The Airbus A380 is the largest passenger aeroplane in the world.

50288.q: What is a cruise ship often compared with?
50288.e: A cruise ship has rooms, restaurants, pools and theatres. You live there for the whole journey.
50288.m: A cruise ship is like a floating hotel.

50289.q: What is a room on a ship called?
50289.e: On ships people sleep in cabins. Some have a window onto the sea, others do not.
50289.m: On a ship you sleep in a cabin.

50290.q: What is the left side of a ship called when you face forwards?
50290.e: Sailors say port for left and starboard for right. That way there is no confusion.
50290.m: Port is the left side of a ship.

50291.q: What is the front part of a ship called?
50291.e: The bow is the pointed front of the ship. At the back is the stern.
50291.m: The bow is at the front of the ship.

50292.q: What is a floor on a ship called?
50292.e: Large ships have many decks on top of each other. The top deck often has deckchairs.
50292.m: The floors of a ship are called decks.

50293.q: What hangs on the side of a cruise ship for emergencies?
50293.e: In an emergency everyone on board can leave the ship in the lifeboats. There is a drill at the start of every voyage.
50293.m: Lifeboats save the people on board in an emergency.

50294.q: What is a round window on a ship called?
50294.e: Portholes are round, very tight windows. They keep water and wind out.
50294.m: A porthole is a round ship's window.

50295.q: On which river do river cruise ships travel from Switzerland to Holland?
50295.e: The Rhine flows from Switzerland through Germany to the Netherlands and the North Sea. River cruise ships also travel on it.
50295.m: Ships travel on the Rhine from Switzerland to the North Sea.

50296.q: What does a container ship carry?
a: Large metal boxes full of goods
50296.e: Container ships carry thousands of containers. Inside are goods such as clothes, toys or machines.
50296.m: Container ships carry goods across the sea in large boxes.

50297.q: What are shipping containers usually made of?
50297.e: Containers are made of sturdy steel. That way they can stand up to wind, waves and heavy stacking.
50297.m: Shipping containers are made of strong steel.

50298.q: What is used to lift containers off a ship in the port?
50298.e: Huge cranes on the quay lift the containers off the ship one by one. They are called container cranes.

50299.q: Why are all shipping containers the same size?
a: So they fit on ships, trains and lorries
50299.e: Because all containers are built the same way, they fit on every container ship, every goods train and every lorry. That saves a lot of time.
50299.m: Containers are the same size everywhere.

50300.q: What shape is a shipping container?
50300.e: Containers are long, rectangular boxes with doors at one end. That makes them easy to stack.
50300.m: Containers have corners so they can be stacked.

50301.q: Which port is the largest in Europe?
50301.e: Rotterdam lies in the Netherlands on the North Sea. It is the largest seaport in Europe.
50301.m: The largest port in Europe is Rotterdam.

50302.q: In which Swiss city are there Rhine ports for cargo ships?
50302.e: Cargo ships arrive via the Rhine in Basel and right next to it in Birsfelden and Muttenz. These ports connect Switzerland with the sea.
50302.m: The Swiss Rhine ports are in and near Basel.

50303.q: What shows ships the way along the coast at night with a bright light?
50303.e: Lighthouses stand on coasts and at harbour entrances. Their light warns of dangerous places.
50303.m: A lighthouse helps ships at night.

50304.q: Which small, powerful boats pull and push large ships in the port?
50304.e: Large ships find it hard to turn in a narrow port. Tugboats help them to dock and set off.
50304.m: Tugboats help large ships in the port.

50305.q: Who comes on board to guide the captain of a large ship safely into port?
50305.e: Pilots know the port and its dangers very well. They come on board and advise the captain on the way in.
50305.m: A pilot guides ships safely into port.

50306.q: In which country is the Suez Canal?
50306.e: The Suez Canal lies in the north-east of Egypt. Egypt runs the canal.
50306.m: The Suez Canal belongs to Egypt.

50307.q: Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect?
a: The Mediterranean and the Red Sea
The North Sea and the Baltic Sea
The Black Sea and the Mediterranean
The Red Sea and the Arabian Sea
50307.e: The canal runs from the Mediterranean in the north to the Red Sea in the south. That way ships get quickly from Europe to Asia.
50307.m: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

50308.q: Which continent did ships from Europe to Asia have to sail around in the past?
50308.e: Before the canal, ships sailed around the southern tip of Africa. The canal saves many thousands of kilometres.
50308.m: The Suez Canal saves ships the journey around Africa.

50309.q: In which century was the Suez Canal opened?
50309.e: The Suez Canal was opened in 1869. That was in the 19th century.
50309.m: The Suez Canal is over 150 years old.

50310.q: What does the Suez Canal not need, unlike the Panama Canal?
50310.e: The seas at both ends are almost at the same level. So ships pass through without locks.
50310.m: There are no locks in the Suez Canal.

50311.q: What kind of landscape does the Suez Canal mainly run through?
50311.e: On both sides of the canal there is mainly flat, dry desert. From far away it looks as if the ships are sailing through sand.
50311.m: The Suez Canal runs through the desert.

50312.q: What happened in the Suez Canal in 2021?
a: A huge container ship blocked it
50312.e: The container ship Ever Given got stuck sideways in the canal in March 2021. For several days hundreds of ships could not get through.
50312.m: A single ship can block a canal.

50313.q: About how long is the Suez Canal?
50313.e: The Suez Canal is about 193 kilometres long. Ships take about eleven hours to pass through.
50313.m: The Suez Canal is almost 200 kilometres long.

50314.q: Which port city lies at the northern end of the Suez Canal on the Mediterranean?
50314.e: Port Said was founded when the canal was built. There, ships enter the canal from the Mediterranean.
50314.m: Port Said lies at the northern end of the Suez Canal.

50315.q: What do the locks in the Panama Canal lift up?
50315.e: The canal crosses a lake that is higher than the sea. Locks lift the ships up and lower them again.
50315.m: Locks lift ships to a different level.

50316.q: In which year was the Panama Canal opened?
50316.e: After many years of building, the canal was opened in August 1914.
50316.m: The Panama Canal has been open since 1914.

50317.q: Which tip did ships have to sail around before the Panama Canal was built?
a: The southern tip of South America
50317.e: Without the canal, ships had to sail all the way around the southern tip of South America. That was a very long and dangerous detour.
50317.m: The Panama Canal saves the journey around South America.

50318.q: What lies in the middle of the Panama Canal?
50318.e: A river was dammed for the canal. This created a large lake that the ships sail across.
50318.m: A large lake lies in the middle of the Panama Canal.

50319.q: About how long does a ship take to pass through the Panama Canal?
50319.e: The journey through the canal with all the locks usually takes about ten to fifteen hours.
50319.m: The journey through the Panama Canal takes about half a day.

50320.q: What is very important for operating the locks in the Panama Canal?
a: Lots of fresh water from lakes
50320.e: Each time a ship goes through a lock, fresh water from the lakes flows into the sea. If there is too little rain, fewer ships can pass.
50320.m: Without enough rain the locks have too little water.

50321.q: Which creatures caused a lot of illness during the building of the Panama Canal?
50321.e: Mosquitoes spread yellow fever and malaria. Many workers fell ill and died.
50321.m: Mosquitoes made building the Panama Canal dangerous.

50322.q: What holds ships in the middle of the old locks of the Panama Canal with ropes?
50322.e: Small locomotives on rails beside the lock hold the ships in the middle with ropes. They are called mules.
50322.m: Small locomotives guide ships through the old locks.

50324.q: In which country does the Trans-Siberian Railway run?
50324.e: The Trans-Siberian runs right across Russia from Europe to Asia.
50324.m: The Trans-Siberian runs across the whole of Russia.

50325.q: In which city does the Trans-Siberian Railway begin?
50325.e: The line begins in Moscow, the capital of Russia.

50326.q: In which city on the Pacific does the Trans-Siberian Railway end?
50326.e: Vladivostok lies in the far east of Russia by the sea. The long line ends there.

50327.q: About how long is the Trans-Siberian Railway?
50327.e: From Moscow to Vladivostok it is about 9300 kilometres. It is the longest railway line in the world.
50327.m: The Trans-Siberian is the longest railway line in the world.

50328.q: About how long does the whole journey on the Trans-Siberian take without stopping?
50328.e: Without changing trains or stopping, you travel for about six to seven days. You sleep on the train.
50328.m: On the Trans-Siberian you travel for about a week.

50329.q: Which deep lake does the Trans-Siberian pass?
50329.e: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world. The railway runs along its shore for a long way.

50330.q: Through which huge, cold region does the Trans-Siberian run?
50330.e: Siberia is a huge region in the north of Asia. In winter it gets very cold there.

50331.q: Where do passengers sleep during the journey on the Trans-Siberian?
a: In a hotel at the station
50331.e: Because the journey takes many days, there are compartments with beds. During the day they become seats.
50331.m: On the Trans-Siberian you sleep in the sleeping car.

50332.q: Which trees do you see especially often from the Trans-Siberian?
50332.e: The train runs for days through the taiga. This is a huge forest with birches, larches, spruces and pines.
50332.m: From the Trans-Siberian you see a lot of taiga forest.

50333.q: Which dogs often pull sledges in the far north?
50333.e: Huskies have lots of stamina and thick fur. They love running and hardly feel the cold.

50334.q: What is the person who steers a dog sledge called?
50334.e: The musher stands at the back of the sledge. He steers the dogs by calling out.
50334.m: A musher steers the dog sledge.

50335.q: Which dog runs right at the front of the team?
50335.e: The lead dog listens to the commands and shows the other dogs the way.
50335.m: The lead dog leads the team of dogs.

50336.q: What does a dog sledge glide on?
50336.e: Runners are long, smooth rails under the sledge. They let it glide easily over snow and ice.

50337.q: In which US state does the famous Iditarod dog sledge race take place?
50337.e: The Iditarod runs for about 1500 kilometres through Alaska to the town of Nome. It usually takes more than a week.
50337.m: The Iditarod is a long dog sledge race in Alaska.

50338.q: What protects sledge dogs' paws on sharp ice?
50338.e: The dogs wear small fabric shoes called booties. They protect the paws from ice and injuries.
50338.m: Sledge dogs often wear small boots.

50339.q: What is the group of dogs called that pull a sledge together?
50339.e: Several dogs are harnessed together with lines in front of the sledge. This is called a team.
50339.m: Several sledge dogs make up a team.

50340.q: On which large, icy island do people still often travel by dog sledge today?
50340.e: Greenland is the largest island in the world and almost completely covered in ice. Dog sledges are still important there in winter.
50340.m: In Greenland people travel by dog sledge in winter.

50341.q: Which breed of dog with thick fur is known as a particularly strong sledge dog?
50341.e: The Alaskan Malamute is big and strong and has very thick fur. It can pull heavy loads.
50341.m: The Malamute is a strong sledge dog.

50342.q: What is a caravan in the desert?
a: A group travelling with animals in the desert
50342.e: In a caravan, people travel together with many pack animals. Usually they are camels.
50342.m: A caravan travels through the desert in a long line.

50343.q: What did camel caravans in the Sahara often carry from place to place in the past?
50343.e: Salt was very valuable. Caravans carried large slabs of salt from the desert to the cities in the south.
50343.m: Caravans used to trade in salt.

50344.q: What was the old trade route from China to Europe that caravans travelled along called?
50344.e: On the Silk Road, caravans brought silk, spices and other goods from China to the west.
50344.m: The Silk Road was a long caravan route.

50345.q: What was an inn where caravans stayed overnight in the past called?
50345.e: In a caravanserai, people and animals found shelter for the night. There was water and a safe courtyard. A medina is an old town, a souk a market and a kasbah a fortress.
50345.m: Caravans stayed overnight in a caravanserai.

50346.q: Why do caravans in the desert like to travel early in the morning or in the evening?
a: Because it is less hot then
Because the wells are fuller then
Because the camels walk faster then
50346.e: At midday the sun in the desert is very strong. In the morning and evening it is cooler.
50346.m: In the desert it is better to travel when it is cooler.

50347.q: What helps caravans find their way in the desert at night?
50347.e: There are hardly any paths in the desert, and the wind blows tracks away. In the clear night sky the stars show the direction.
50347.m: The stars show the way in the desert.

50348.q: What are the high sand hills that caravans cross called?
50348.e: The wind piles the sand up into dunes. Some dunes are over a hundred metres high.
50348.m: Sand hills in the desert are called dunes.

50349.q: How do camels in a caravan often walk one behind the other?
a: Tied to each other with ropes
50349.e: Each camel is often tied with a rope to the animal in front. That keeps the line together.
50349.m: In a caravan the camels walk in a line.

50350.q: Which large desert in North Africa have caravans crossed for centuries?
50350.e: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world. Caravans carried goods right across it.
50350.m: Many caravans crossed the Sahara for a long time.

50351.q: How many wheels does a tuk-tuk have?
50351.e: A tuk-tuk has one wheel at the front and two at the back. That makes it very easy to manoeuvre.
50351.m: A tuk-tuk runs on three wheels.

50352.q: Where does the tuk-tuk get its name from?
a: From the sound of its engine
50352.e: The small engine makes a rattling noise that sounds like “tuk tuk”. That is where the name comes from.
50352.m: The tuk-tuk is named after the sound of its engine.

50353.q: In which capital city are there especially many tuk-tuks?
50353.e: In Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, tuk-tuks are well-known taxis. Many tourists ride in them.
50353.m: In Bangkok tuk-tuks are typical taxis.

50354.q: What are tuk-tuks in Asia mostly used for?
50354.e: You wave down a tuk-tuk at the roadside and get a ride to where you want to go. People often agree on the price beforehand.
50354.m: Tuk-tuks in Asia are often small taxis.

50355.q: In which country is the tuk-tuk often called an auto rickshaw and very common?
50355.e: Millions of auto rickshaws drive around India. Many are yellow and green or yellow and black.
50355.m: There are a great many auto rickshaws in India.

50356.q: How was a rickshaw originally powered?
50356.e: The first rickshaw was a small cart that a person pulled on foot. Only later did rickshaws get pedals or an engine.
50356.m: In the past a person pulled the rickshaw.

50357.q: What does a tuk-tuk usually not have?
50357.e: Most tuk-tuks are open at the sides. That is why you feel the wind as you ride.
50357.m: A tuk-tuk is usually open at the sides.

50358.q: What is a rickshaw that is powered by pedals called?
50358.e: On a cycle rickshaw the driver pedals like on a bike. The passengers sit at the back.
50358.m: A cycle rickshaw is powered by muscle power.

50359.q: Why do tuk-tuks get along well in heavy city traffic?
a: Because they are small and nimble
50359.e: Tuk-tuks are narrow and short. They weave their way between cars and buses.

50360.q: What do you do on a round-the-world sailing trip?
a: You sail once around the Earth
You sail once across a lake
You sail along the coast and back
You sail from one island to the next
50360.e: On a round-the-world sailing trip you sail a sailing ship right around the Earth and arrive back at the start.
50360.m: On a round-the-world sailing trip you sail around the Earth.

50361.q: In which year did the first voyage around the Earth begin?
50361.e: Ferdinand Magellan's fleet set sail in 1519 and returned in 1522. Only one ship made it.
50361.m: The first voyage around the world began in 1519.

50362.q: Who led the first voyage around the world, which began in Spain in 1519?
50362.e: Magellan set off in 1519 with five ships. He died on the way, but one ship returned to Spain in 1522.
50362.m: Magellan led the first voyage around the world.

50363.q: What drives a sailing ship on a voyage around the world?
50363.e: The wind blows into the sails and pushes the ship forward. That way you can sail around the whole Earth without an engine.
50363.m: The wind drives a sailing ship.

50364.q: How old was Laura Dekker when she finished her solo voyage around the world in 2012?
50364.e: The Dutch girl Laura Dekker sailed alone around the world. When she arrived in January 2012 she was 16 years old.
50364.m: Laura Dekker sailed alone around the world as a teenager.

50365.q: Why do sailors on a voyage around the world need lots of drinking water on board?
a: There are no bottles at sea
50365.e: Seawater is salty. If you drink it, you get even thirstier. That is why sailors take lots of drinking water with them.
50365.m: Seawater is too salty to drink.

50366.q: Which dangerous cape at the southern tip of South America do round-the-world sailors often pass?
50366.e: At Cape Horn there are often storms and high waves. It is seen as one of the most dangerous places for sailors.

50367.q: Which instrument shows sailors the direction on the open sea?
50367.e: The needle of a compass always points north. That way sailors know which direction they are going even with no land in sight.
50367.m: A compass shows the direction at sea.

50368.q: What is always inside a passport?
50368.e: A passport has a photo, the name and the date of birth. That way you can check who the person is.
50368.m: Your passport shows who you are.

50369.q: Where is your passport checked when you enter a country?
50369.e: At the border or at passport control in the airport, officials look at your passport.
50369.m: You show your passport at the border.

50370.q: What is inside modern Swiss passports and stores data?
50370.e: A small chip in the passport stores the photo and fingerprints. This makes it hard to forge.

50371.q: Which document is enough for Swiss people to travel to many European countries instead of a passport?
50371.e: For many countries in Europe the Swiss identity card is enough. For long journeys you usually need your passport.
50371.m: In many European countries the identity card is enough.

50372.q: What do border officials sometimes press into your passport?
50372.e: A stamp shows when you entered or left a country.
50372.m: A stamp in your passport shows when you entered.

50373.q: Which animal is a well-known symbol of France?
50373.e: The Gallic cockerel is an old symbol of France. You can see it, for example, on the shirts of French sports teams.
50373.m: The cockerel is a symbol of France.

50374.q: On which day does France celebrate its national day?
50374.e: On 14 July France celebrates with parades and fireworks. Switzerland celebrates its national day on 1 August.
50374.m: France celebrates its national day on 14 July.

50375.q: What is the highest mountain in France called?
50375.e: Mont Blanc is about 4800 metres high. It is the highest mountain in the Alps and lies on the border with Italy.
50375.m: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in France.

50376.q: What is the long, thin bread typical of France called?
50376.e: The baguette is a long, narrow white loaf with a crunchy crust. In France people often buy it fresh from the baker every day.
50376.m: The baguette is a typical bread from France.

50377.q: Which large lake do Switzerland and France share?
50377.e: The southern shore of Lake Geneva belongs to France, the northern shore to Switzerland. In French it is called “Lac Léman”.
50377.m: Switzerland and France share Lake Geneva.

50378.q: For which event was the Eiffel Tower built?
50378.e: The tower was the entrance to a big world's fair in Paris. It was actually meant to be taken down again afterwards.
50378.m: The Eiffel Tower was built for a world's fair.

50379.q: Roughly how tall is the Eiffel Tower?
50379.e: With the aerials on top, the Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall (as of 2025). That is about as tall as a building with 100 floors.
50379.m: The Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall.

50380.q: How many levels for visitors does the Eiffel Tower have?
50380.e: Visitors can go up to three levels. The top one is very high and gives a wide view over Paris.
50380.m: The Eiffel Tower has three levels for visitors.

50381.q: What does the Eiffel Tower do every hour on the hour in the evening?
a: It turns round in a circle
50381.e: After sunset, thousands of lamps glitter for about five minutes every hour on the hour. It looks like twinkling stars.
50381.m: In the evening the Eiffel Tower sparkles every hour on the hour.

50382.q: Roughly every how many years is the Eiffel Tower repainted?
50382.e: To stop the iron rusting, the tower gets a new coat of paint about every seven years. This takes around 60 tonnes of paint.
50382.m: The Eiffel Tower is repainted about every seven years.

50383.q: What is the Louvre in Paris?
50383.e: The Louvre is a huge museum with paintings, statues and ancient treasures. It is one of the biggest museums in the world.
50383.m: The Louvre is a famous art museum.

50384.q: Which famous painting of a smiling woman hangs in the Louvre?
50384.e: The Mona Lisa is probably the most famous painting in the world. Every day lots of people stand in front of it to see her smile.
50384.m: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre.

50385.q: How is the most famous painting in the Louvre protected from damage?
50385.e: The famous painting is small and very valuable. That is why it hangs behind thick bulletproof glass that can also withstand blows.
50385.m: The most valuable painting in the Louvre hangs behind bulletproof glass.

50386.q: What stands in front of the entrance to the Louvre?
50386.e: A large glass pyramid stands in front of the Louvre. The museum's main entrance is underneath it.
50386.m: A glass pyramid stands in front of the Louvre.

50387.q: What was the Louvre before it became a museum?
50387.e: The Louvre used to be a castle and later a palace where kings of France lived. Only later were works of art put there for everyone.
50387.m: The Louvre used to be a palace of the kings.

50388.q: Which art museum has more visitors than any other in the world?
50388.e: The Louvre is the most visited museum in the world. Around 9 million people come every year (as of 2024).
50388.m: The Louvre is the most visited museum in the world.

50389.q: Which famous statue without arms stands in the Louvre?
50389.e: The Venus de Milo is an ancient marble statue from Greece. Its arms have been missing ever since it was discovered.
50389.m: The Venus de Milo stands in the Louvre.

50390.q: Which famous painting hangs in the Louvre in Paris?
50390.e: The Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci is the best-known painting in the Louvre. The museum has been open to everyone since 1793.
50390.m: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre.

a: A rock with a monastery in the sea
A high mountain in the Alps
50391.e: Mont-Saint-Michel is a small rocky island off the coast of France. At the very top there is an old monastery with a church.
50391.m: There is a monastery in the sea on Mont-Saint-Michel.

50392.q: In which region of France is Mont-Saint-Michel?
50392.e: Mont-Saint-Michel is in Normandy in northern France. There it is very close to the border with Brittany.

50393.q: What lies below the monastery on Mont-Saint-Michel?
a: A small village with narrow lanes
50393.e: On the slope below the monastery there is a small village with a steep, narrow main street. There are shops, restaurants and old houses.
50393.m: A small village lies below the monastery.

50394.q: Which golden figure stands at the very top of the spire of Mont-Saint-Michel?
50394.e: At the top stands a golden figure of the Archangel Michael. The whole mount is named after him.
50394.m: The Archangel Michael stands on top of the spire.

50395.q: How do you get to Mont-Saint-Michel on foot today?
50395.e: Since 2014, a long bridge has led from the mainland to the rock. That way you can cross with dry feet even at high tide.
50395.m: A bridge connects Mont-Saint-Michel with the mainland.

50396.e: Since 1979, Mont-Saint-Michel and its bay have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Such places are considered especially valuable for all of humanity.
50396.m: Mont-Saint-Michel is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50397.q: Which dish is especially famous on Mont-Saint-Michel?
50397.e: A restaurant on the rock has long been famous for its big, fluffy omelette. The eggs are beaten for a long time there.
50397.m: The omelette is famous on Mont-Saint-Michel.

50398.q: Who used to live in the monastery on Mont-Saint-Michel?
50398.e: Monks lived in the monastery for many centuries. They prayed there and kept extending the church.
50398.m: Monks used to live in the monastery on Mont-Saint-Michel.

50399.q: How many official languages does Belgium have?
50399.e: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German. Switzerland even has four national languages.

50400.q: Which baked treat with a grid pattern is Belgium known for?
50400.e: Belgian waffles have a pattern of small squares. They are often eaten with icing sugar, fruit or cream.
50400.m: Belgium is known for its waffles.

50401.q: Which filled chocolate sweet was invented in Belgium?
50401.e: The praline was invented in Belgium in 1912. It is made of a chocolate shell with a soft filling.
50401.m: The praline was invented in Belgium.

50402.q: What colours is the flag of Belgium?
50402.e: The Belgian flag has three vertical stripes in black, yellow and red. The colours come from old coats of arms of the country.
50402.m: The flag of Belgium is black, yellow and red.

50403.q: Which country do the Smurfs come from?
50403.e: The little blue Smurfs were created by the Belgian artist Peyo. They first appeared in a comic in 1958.

50404.q: Who is at the head of the country of Belgium?
50404.e: Belgium is a kingdom. Philippe has been King of the Belgians since 2013 (as of 2025).
50404.m: Belgium is led by a king.

50405.q: Which Belgian city is famous for trading diamonds?
50405.e: Diamonds have been traded and cut in Antwerp for centuries. The city also has a large port.
50405.m: Antwerp is the city of diamonds.

50406.q: Which country is a neighbour of Belgium?
50406.e: Belgium borders France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. To the north lies the North Sea.
50406.m: France is a neighbour of Belgium.

50407.q: What is the capital of Belgium?
50407.e: Brussels is the capital of Belgium. The king and his family also live there.
50407.m: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.

50408.q: What is the name of the small fountain statue of a boy that is very famous in Brussels?
50408.e: Manneken Pis is a bronze statue of a boy weeing, only about 60 centimetres tall. He owns more than 900 costumes, which he wears in turn.
50408.m: Manneken Pis is a famous statue in Brussels.

50409.q: Which building in Brussels is made of huge shiny balls?
50409.e: The Atomium was built in 1958 for a world fair. It shows a tiny building block of iron enlarged many billions of times.
50409.m: The Atomium in Brussels is made of big balls.

50410.q: Every two years a huge carpet lies on the big square in Brussels. What is it made of?
50410.e: Every two years in August, a carpet made of many thousands of flowers lies on the Grand-Place in Brussels.
50410.m: Brussels has a flower carpet every two years.

50411.q: Which group of countries has important buildings in Brussels?
50411.e: Important parts of the European Union work in Brussels, for example the European Commission. The Olympic Committee, FIFA and the Red Cross, on the other hand, have their headquarters in Switzerland.
50411.m: The European Union works in Brussels.

50412.q: Which two languages are official languages in Brussels?
50412.e: In Brussels, street signs are usually in two languages, French and Dutch. In everyday life you hear French the most.
50412.m: In Brussels people speak French and Dutch.

50413.q: What is painted on many house walls in Brussels?
50413.e: Brussels is known as the city of comics. Big pictures of famous comic characters are painted on many house walls.
50413.m: In Brussels you can see comic pictures on many house walls.

50414.q: What can you see in the Mini-Europe park in Brussels?
50414.e: In the Mini-Europe park, many well-known buildings from Europe stand as small models. Swissminiatur in Ticino is a similar park.
50414.m: Mini-Europe shows Europe's buildings in miniature.

50415.q: In which city does the government of the Netherlands work?
50415.e: The government and parliament of the Netherlands are based in The Hague. The king also lives there.
50415.m: The government of the Netherlands works in The Hague.

50416.q: What do many people call the Netherlands, even though it is only part of the country?
50416.e: Holland is really only a region in the west of the country with two provinces. Even so, many people say “Holland” for the whole country.
50416.m: Holland is only part of the Netherlands.

50417.q: Which language is spoken in the Netherlands?
50417.e: People in the Netherlands speak Dutch. It is related to German, so some words sound similar.
50417.m: Dutch is spoken in the Netherlands.

50418.q: What is special about many areas of the Netherlands?
a: They lie lower than the sea
50418.e: About a quarter of the country lies below sea level. Without protection, the sea would flood the land there.
50418.m: Many areas of the Netherlands lie lower than the sea.

50419.q: What protects the land in the Netherlands from the sea?
50419.e: Dykes are long, high banks of earth along the coast and the rivers. They keep the water away from the land.
50419.m: Dykes protect the Netherlands from the sea.

50420.q: Which means of transport do people in the Netherlands use especially often?
50420.e: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands. The country is flat and has a great many cycle paths.
50420.m: Lots of people in the Netherlands ride bicycles.

50421.q: What colour do Dutch fans wear at sports events?
50421.e: Orange is the colour of the royal family, which is called the “House of Orange”. That is why fans of the Netherlands wear orange.
50421.m: Fans of the Netherlands wear orange.

50422.q: Which kind of cheese is named after a town in the Netherlands?
50422.e: Gouda is a town in the Netherlands whose market has traded cheese for a long time. Emmental, on the other hand, comes from Switzerland.
50422.m: Gouda is a cheese from the Netherlands.

50423.q: What are the traditional Dutch shoes, called klompen, made of?
50423.e: Klompen are carved from a single piece of wood. In the past, farmers wore them for work in wet fields.

50424.q: What do the old houses along the canals in Amsterdam often look like?
50424.e: It is often said that taxes used to depend on how wide a house was along the canal. So houses were built narrow, but tall and deep.
50424.m: The old canal houses are narrow and tall.

50425.q: What are the grachten in Amsterdam?
50425.e: Grachten are canals that run like rings through the old town. In the past, ships carried goods along them right up to the houses.

50426.q: Roughly how many bridges are there in Amsterdam?
50426.e: Because there are so many canals, Amsterdam needs a great many bridges. There are well over 1,000.

50427.q: What do some people live on in the canals of Amsterdam?
50427.e: There are around 2,500 houseboats on the canals. People live in them just like in a flat.
50427.m: Some people in Amsterdam live on houseboats.

50428.q: Whose hiding place can you visit in a museum in Amsterdam?
50428.e: Anne Frank was a Jewish girl who had to hide with her family in a back building during the Second World War. There she wrote her famous diary.
50428.m: In Amsterdam you can visit Anne Frank's hiding place.

50429.q: Which painter is a famous museum in Amsterdam named after?
50429.e: The Van Gogh Museum has many of the painter's pictures, for example his sunflowers. He came from the Netherlands.
50429.m: Amsterdam has a museum for Vincent van Gogh.

50430.q: Which painter painted the large picture “The Night Watch”, which hangs in Amsterdam?
50430.e: Rembrandt was a famous painter from the Netherlands. “The Night Watch” hangs in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

50431.q: What is the hook at the top of many old houses in Amsterdam for?
50431.e: The stairs in the old houses are very steep. So large furniture is pulled up the outside with a rope on the hook and brought in through the window.
50431.m: The hook on the house is used to lift furniture.

50432.q: Which river is Amsterdam named after?
50432.e: The city grew up at a dam on the River Amstel. That is why it is called Amsterdam.
50432.m: Amsterdam is named after the River Amstel.

50433.q: What were many windmills in the Netherlands used for?
50433.e: Many mills pumped water from the low land into the canals. This kept fields and villages dry.
50433.m: Windmills in the Netherlands pumped water away.

50434.q: What did windmills often grind in the past?
50434.e: Heavy millstones turned in many windmills. They ground grain into flour for bread.

50435.q: At which place in the Netherlands do 19 old windmills stand close together?
50435.e: In Kinderdijk, 19 old windmills stand along canals. They have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
50435.m: There are 19 old windmills at Kinderdijk.

50436.q: How many sails does a typical windmill in the Netherlands have?
50436.e: Most old windmills have four large sails. The wind turns them and so drives the mill.
50436.m: A typical windmill has four sails.

50437.q: What do modern wind turbines produce?
50437.e: Modern wind turbines turn a generator that produces electricity. There are also some wind turbines in Switzerland, for example in the Jura.

50438.q: What does a tulip grow from?
50438.e: Tulips grow from flower bulbs that are planted in the ground in autumn. Food for the plant is stored in the bulb.
50438.m: A tulip grows from a bulb.

50439.q: In which season do tulips flower?
50439.e: Tulips are among the first colourful flowers of the year. They usually flower in April and May.

50440.q: What is the name of the famous flower park in the Netherlands with millions of tulips?
50440.e: Every spring, millions of flowers bloom at Keukenhof, mostly tulips. The park is only open for a few weeks a year.
50440.m: Keukenhof is a famous tulip park.

50441.q: What was going on with tulip bulbs in Holland almost 400 years ago?
50441.e: Around 1637, rare tulip bulbs were so sought after that some cost more than a house. This is called “tulip mania”.
50441.m: Tulip bulbs used to be very expensive in Holland.

50442.q: What is the capital of Luxembourg?
50442.e: The capital has the same name as the country. The city of Luxembourg sits on rocks above deep valleys.
50442.m: The capital of Luxembourg is also called Luxembourg.

50443.q: What kind of country is Luxembourg?
50443.e: Luxembourg is the only grand duchy in the world. A grand duke is at its head.

50444.q: Which language of their own do people in Luxembourg speak with each other?
50444.e: Luxembourgers speak Luxembourgish with each other. French and German are also official languages.
50444.m: Luxembourgish is the language of the Luxembourgers.

50445.q: How big is Luxembourg compared with Switzerland?
50445.e: Luxembourg is about 16 times smaller than Switzerland. It is roughly the size of the canton of Ticino.
50445.m: Luxembourg is much smaller than Switzerland.

50446.q: Which country is NOT a neighbour of Luxembourg?
50446.e: Luxembourg only borders Belgium, France and Germany. The Netherlands lies further north.
50446.m: Luxembourg borders Belgium, France and Germany.

50447.q: What has been free in Luxembourg since 2020?
50447.e: Since 2020, you can travel by bus, tram and train all over Luxembourg without a ticket. Luxembourg was the first country in the world to do this.
50447.m: In Luxembourg, buses and trains are free.

50448.q: What colours is the flag of Luxembourg?
50448.e: The flag has three horizontal stripes in red, white and light blue. It looks very similar to the flag of the Netherlands, only the blue is lighter.
50448.m: The flag of Luxembourg is red, white and light blue.

50449.q: What are the casemates in the city of Luxembourg?
50449.e: The casemates are long passages that were dug into the rock long ago. Soldiers could shelter there.
50449.m: The casemates are passages in the rock of Luxembourg.

50450.q: What does the name “Côte d'Azur” mean in English?
50450.e: “Côte” means coast and “azur” is a bright sky blue. The name suits the blue sea and sky.
50450.m: Côte d'Azur means Blue Coast in English.

50451.q: Which sea is the Côte d'Azur on?
50451.e: The Côte d'Azur is in the south-east of France on the Mediterranean. The water there is warm in summer.
50451.m: The Côte d'Azur is on the Mediterranean.

50452.q: Which is the largest city on the Côte d'Azur?
50452.e: Nice has around 340,000 inhabitants and is the largest city on this coast. It also has a large airport.
50452.m: Nice is the largest city on the Côte d'Azur.

50453.q: In which town on the Côte d'Azur is a famous film festival held every year?
50453.e: Film stars from all over the world meet in Cannes every May. Locarno in Ticino also has a well-known film festival, but not by the sea.
50453.m: Cannes has a famous film festival.

50454.q: In which city is the famous seafront promenade “Promenade des Anglais”?
50454.e: The Promenade des Anglais is a long path right by the sea in Nice. The name means “Promenade of the English”.
50454.m: The Promenade des Anglais is in Nice.

50455.q: What is the weather usually like on the Côte d'Azur in summer?
50455.e: The Côte d'Azur has a great many sunny days a year. The summers are hot and dry, the winters mild.
50455.m: On the Côte d'Azur it is usually warm and sunny in summer.

50456.q: Which mountains reach close to the sea on the Côte d'Azur?
50456.e: The Maritime Alps are the southernmost part of the Alps. They reach almost to the coast, so there you can swim and ski on the same day.
50456.m: On the Côte d'Azur the Alps reach close to the sea.

50457.q: What are many beaches on the Côte d'Azur made of?
50457.e: Many beaches there are made of round, smooth pebbles instead of fine sand. So beach shoes are handy.
50457.m: Many beaches on the Côte d'Azur have pebbles.

50458.e: Monaco is a principality. Albert II has been the Prince of Monaco since 2005 (as of 2025).
50458.m: Monaco is ruled by a prince.

50459.q: What can you watch every day in front of the Prince's Palace in Monaco?
50459.e: Every day shortly before noon, the guards in front of the palace change in a small ceremony. Many tourists watch.
50459.m: There is a changing of the guard in front of the Prince's Palace every day.

50460.q: Which motor race goes through the streets of Monaco every year?
50460.e: At the Monaco Grand Prix, Formula 1 cars race through narrow streets and bends. The track even goes through a tunnel.
50460.m: Formula 1 races through the streets of Monaco.

50461.q: What is the name of a well-known district of Monaco with a famous casino?
50461.e: Monte Carlo is a district of Monaco. It has a magnificent casino and many luxury hotels.
50461.m: Monte Carlo is a district of Monaco.

50462.q: Which country does Monaco border on land?
50462.e: On the land side, Monaco is completely surrounded by France. On the other side is the sea.

50463.q: What colours is the flag of Monaco?
50463.e: The flag of Monaco is red at the top and white at the bottom. These are the colours of the princely family.
50463.m: The flag of Monaco is red and white.

50464.q: Which famous museum in Monaco shows fish and other sea creatures?
50464.e: The Oceanographic Museum stands on a cliff right above the sea. It has a large aquarium with many sea creatures.
50464.m: In Monaco, the Oceanographic Museum shows sea creatures.

50465.q: What money do you pay with in Monaco?
50465.e: Monaco is not part of the European Union but still uses the euro. It is even allowed to mint its own euro coins.
50465.m: In Monaco you pay with euros.

50466.q: How many horses pull the chariot on the Brandenburg Gate?
50466.e: The chariot on top of the gate is pulled by four horses. A chariot with four horses is called a quadriga.

50467.q: Who drives the chariot on the Brandenburg Gate?
50467.e: Victoria, the goddess of victory, stands on the chariot. She holds a staff with an eagle.
50467.m: Victoria, the goddess of victory, drives the quadriga.

50468.q: What is the Brandenburg Gate built from?
50468.e: The gate was built from light sandstone more than 200 years ago.
50468.m: The Brandenburg Gate is made of sandstone.

50469.q: What used to stand right next to the Brandenburg Gate and divided Berlin into two parts?
50469.e: For almost 30 years, the Berlin Wall stood right next to the gate. Since the fall of the Wall in 1989, people can walk through it again.
50469.m: The Berlin Wall used to stand by the Brandenburg Gate.

50470.q: Which celebration do many people mark every year with fireworks in front of the Brandenburg Gate?
50470.e: On the night before 1 January there is a big New Year's Eve party with fireworks in front of the gate.
50470.m: People celebrate New Year's Eve in front of the Brandenburg Gate.

50472.q: Which German city has the largest port in Germany?
50472.e: Hamburg has the largest port in Germany. Every day, big ships from all over the world arrive there.
50472.m: Germany's largest port is in Hamburg.

50473.q: Which river is the port of Hamburg on?
50473.e: The port of Hamburg is on the Elbe. The ships travel along the river to the sea.

50474.q: What are the big metal boxes that ships use to carry goods called?
50474.e: Containers are big boxes made of metal. They fit on ships, lorries and trains.
50474.m: Containers are big boxes for goods.

50475.q: What is used to lift the containers off the ships in the port of Hamburg?
50475.e: Huge cranes lift the heavy containers off the ship and put them down on land.
50475.m: Cranes lift containers off the ships.

50476.q: What is the old district of red-brick warehouses at the port of Hamburg called?
50476.e: Coffee, tea and spices used to be stored in the Speicherstadt. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2015.
50476.m: The Speicherstadt is an old warehouse district in Hamburg.

50477.q: Which famous concert hall with a wavy glass roof stands at the port of Hamburg?
50477.e: The Elbphilharmonie stands on top of an old warehouse. Its roof looks like waves.
50477.m: The Elbphilharmonie is a concert hall at the port of Hamburg.

50478.q: Which market takes place at the port in Hamburg early every Sunday morning?
50478.e: The Hamburg fish market starts very early on Sundays. It sells not only fish but also fruit and much more.
50478.m: Hamburg has its fish market on Sunday mornings.

50479.q: Which big festival does Hamburg celebrate at the port every year in May?
50479.e: Many ships and visitors come for the port's birthday. There are parades on the water and fireworks.
50479.m: Hamburg celebrates the port's birthday every year.

50480.q: Which sea do ships sail into when they leave the port of Hamburg?
50480.e: The river at Hamburg flows into the North Sea. From there, ships sail all over the world.
50480.m: Ships from the port of Hamburg sail into the North Sea.

50481.q: Which big folk festival takes place in Munich every year?
50481.e: Oktoberfest is one of the biggest folk festivals in the world. It actually starts in September.

50482.q: Munich is the capital of which German state?
50482.e: Munich is the capital of Bavaria. Bavaria is in the south of Germany.
50482.m: Munich is the capital of Bavaria.

50483.q: What is the most famous square in the centre of Munich called?
50483.e: Marienplatz is the centre of Munich. The New Town Hall stands there.
50483.m: Marienplatz is in the centre of Munich.

50484.q: What dances to music in the tower of Munich's town hall?
50484.e: There is a glockenspiel in the tower of the New Town Hall. Colourful figures turn and dance to it.
50484.m: Figures dance at the glockenspiel in Munich.

50485.q: How many towers does the Frauenkirche in Munich have?
50485.e: The Frauenkirche has two towers with round domes. They are a landmark of Munich.

50486.e: The Isar flows through Munich. In summer, lots of people lie in the sun on its banks.

50487.q: What is the huge park in Munich called?
50487.e: The English Garden is one of the largest city parks in the world. It is even bigger than Central Park in New York.
50487.m: The big park in Munich is called the English Garden.

50488.q: What can you see at Hellabrunn Zoo in Munich?
a: Animals from all over the world
50488.e: Hellabrunn Zoo is in the south of Munich on the Isar. Animals from all over the world live there.
50488.m: Animals from all over the world live at Hellabrunn Zoo in Munich.

50489.q: What is the big museum of technology and science in Munich called?
50489.e: The Deutsches Museum is one of the largest technology museums in the world. You can see aeroplanes, ships and mines there.
50489.m: The Deutsches Museum in Munich shows technology.

50490.q: Which king had Neuschwanstein Castle built?
50490.e: King Ludwig II of Bavaria had the castle built. He is also called the Fairy Tale King.
50490.m: King Ludwig II had Neuschwanstein built.

50491.q: In which country is Neuschwanstein Castle?
50491.e: Neuschwanstein is in the south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

50492.q: What is Neuschwanstein often called because of how it looks?
50492.e: With its many white towers, Neuschwanstein looks like a castle from a fairy tale.
50492.m: Neuschwanstein is called a fairy-tale castle.

50493.q: Neuschwanstein Castle stands at the edge of which mountain range?
50493.e: The castle stands on a rock in front of the mountains of the Alps.
50493.m: Neuschwanstein stands at the edge of the Alps.

50494.q: The wall paintings in Neuschwanstein show stories from the operas of which composer?
50494.e: The king was a great fan of Richard Wagner's operas. So many pictures in the castle show legends from these operas.
50494.m: Neuschwanstein Castle has paintings about Wagner's operas.

50495.q: Was Neuschwanstein Castle ever completely finished?
50495.e: When the king died in 1886, the castle was not yet finished. Many rooms stayed empty.

50497.q: How long did the king live in Neuschwanstein Castle?
50497.e: Altogether the king lived in the castle for only about 170 days. Shortly afterwards he died.
50497.m: The king only lived in Neuschwanstein for a short time.

50498.q: Which kind of clock is typical of the Black Forest?
50498.e: Cuckoo clocks have been made in the Black Forest for a long time. Every full hour, a little bird calls out.
50498.m: The cuckoo clock comes from the Black Forest.

50499.q: Apart from cherries, what goes into a Black Forest gateau?
50499.e: A Black Forest gateau has layers of chocolate sponge, cream and cherries.
50499.m: Black Forest gateau is made with cherries and cream.

50500.q: What is on the famous Bollenhut hat from the Black Forest?
50500.e: The Bollenhut has big pompoms made of wool. Red pompoms are worn by women who are not yet married.

50501.q: Which trees make the Black Forest so dark?
50501.e: Many dark conifers such as firs and spruces grow in the Black Forest. That is why the forest looks almost black.
50501.m: Dark firs and spruces give the Black Forest its name.

50502.q: Which big river has its source in the Black Forest?
50502.e: The Danube begins in the Black Forest from two streams. It then flows right across Europe to the Black Sea.
50502.m: The Danube has its source in the Black Forest.

50503.q: What is the highest mountain in the Black Forest called?
50503.e: The Feldberg is around 1,500 metres high. In winter you can ski there.
50503.m: The Feldberg is the highest mountain in the Black Forest.

50504.q: In which German state is the Black Forest?
50504.e: The Black Forest is in the south-west of Germany, in the state of Baden-Württemberg.
50504.m: The Black Forest is in Baden-Württemberg.

50505.q: Which country does the Black Forest border in the south?
50505.e: In the south, the Black Forest ends at the Rhine. On the other side of the river is Switzerland.
50505.m: The Black Forest is close to Switzerland.

50506.q: Which city lies on the edge of the Black Forest?
50506.e: Freiburg im Breisgau lies right next to the Black Forest. You can get there quickly from Basel.
50506.m: Freiburg im Breisgau lies by the Black Forest.

50507.q: In which city is St Stephen's Cathedral?
50507.e: St Stephen's Cathedral stands in the middle of Vienna's old town. It is the city's landmark.
50507.m: St Stephen's Cathedral is the landmark of Vienna.

50508.q: What do the people of Vienna lovingly call St Stephen's Cathedral?
50508.e: The people of Vienna lovingly call their cathedral “Steffl”.
50508.m: In Vienna, St Stephen's Cathedral is also called Steffl.

50509.q: What is special about the roof of St Stephen's Cathedral?
a: It is made entirely of gold
50509.e: The roof is covered with many colourful tiles. They form zigzag patterns and eagles.
50509.m: St Stephen's Cathedral has a colourful tiled roof.

50510.q: What is the biggest bell of St Stephen's Cathedral called?
50510.e: The Pummerin is the biggest bell in Austria. It only rings on special occasions, for example at New Year.
50510.m: The Pummerin is the biggest bell in St Stephen's Cathedral.

50511.q: Roughly how tall is the south tower of St Stephen's Cathedral?
50511.e: The south tower is about 136 metres tall. It is one of the tallest church towers in Europe.
50511.m: The south tower of St Stephen's Cathedral is around 136 metres tall.

50512.q: Which tower of St Stephen's Cathedral is much taller?
50512.e: The north tower was never finished. That is why the south tower is much taller.
50512.m: The south tower is the tallest tower of St Stephen's Cathedral.

50513.q: On which square does St Stephen's Cathedral stand?
50513.e: The square around the cathedral is called Stephansplatz. Many shopping streets start there.
50513.m: St Stephen's Cathedral stands on Stephansplatz.

50514.q: What are the underground passages with graves beneath St Stephen's Cathedral called?
50514.e: There are catacombs under the cathedral. The graves of many people from earlier times lie there.
50514.m: There are catacombs under St Stephen's Cathedral.

50515.q: Which famous composer was born in Salzburg?
50515.e: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756. You can visit the house where he was born today.

50516.q: What is the big castle high above the city of Salzburg called?
50516.e: Hohensalzburg Fortress sits on a hill above the old town. It is one of the largest castles in Europe.

50517.e: The Salzach divides Salzburg into two parts. Many bridges cross the river.

50518.q: Which substance is the city of Salzburg named after?
50518.e: A lot of salt used to be mined near Salzburg. The salt made the city rich.

50519.q: What are the three peaks of Salzburger Nockerl meant to look like?
50519.e: Salzburger Nockerl is a fluffy sweet dish made from eggs. The three peaks are meant to remind you of the snowy mountains around Salzburg.
50519.m: Salzburger Nockerl look like snowy mountains.

50520.q: What takes place in Salzburg every summer?
a: A festival of music and theatre
A cycle race round the world
50520.e: The Salzburg Festival has existed for more than 100 years. Every summer, guests come from all over the world.
50520.m: Salzburg has its festival every summer.

50521.q: Which famous musical film about a singing family is set in Salzburg?
50521.e: The film tells the story of the Trapp family, who lived in Salzburg and sang together.
50521.m: The film The Sound of Music is set in Salzburg.

50522.q: Since 1996 the old town of Salzburg has been something special. What is it?
50522.e: The beautiful old town with its churches and squares has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996.
50522.m: The old town of Salzburg is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50523.q: What is the capital of the Austrian state of Tyrol?
50523.e: Innsbruck is the capital of Tyrol. The city lies in a valley between high mountains.
50523.m: Innsbruck is the capital of Tyrol.

50524.q: Which country does the state of Tyrol belong to?
50524.e: Tyrol is one of the nine states of Austria. It also borders Switzerland.
50524.m: The state of Tyrol belongs to Austria.

50525.q: Which country does Tyrol border in the south?
50525.e: Italy lies south of Tyrol. The part there is called South Tyrol.
50525.m: Tyrol borders Italy in the south.

50526.q: What are the shiny tiles of the Golden Roof in Innsbruck made of?
50526.e: The Golden Roof is a balcony with more than 2,600 gilded copper tiles. It was built more than 500 years ago.
50526.m: The Golden Roof has gilded copper tiles.

50527.q: What is the Streif in Kitzbühel in Tyrol famous for?
50527.e: The Hahnenkamm race takes place on the Streif every year. It is one of the hardest downhill runs in the world.
50527.m: Ski races are held on the Streif in Kitzbühel.

50528.q: Which mountain range is in Tyrol?
50528.e: Tyrol lies in the middle of the Alps. There are many high mountains, glaciers and ski areas there.

50529.q: Which round dish made from bread is very popular in Tyrol?
50529.e: Tyrolean dumplings are made from stale bread, often with bacon. They are eaten in soup or with sauerkraut.
50529.m: People in Tyrol love eating dumplings.

50530.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of Tyrol?
50530.e: The coat of arms of Tyrol shows a red eagle on a white background.
50530.m: There is a red eagle on the Tyrolean coat of arms.

50531.q: Which mountain is the highest in Austria?
50531.e: The Grossglockner is the highest mountain in Austria. It is much higher than any mountain in Germany.
50531.m: The Grossglockner is the highest mountain in Austria.

50532.q: Roughly how high is the Grossglockner?
50532.e: The Grossglockner is 3,798 metres high. That is almost 3,800 metres.
50532.m: The Grossglockner is almost 3,800 metres high.

50534.q: There is a national park around the Grossglockner. What is protected there?
50534.e: The Grossglockner is in the Hohe Tauern National Park. In a national park, nature, animals and plants are protected.
50534.m: A national park protects animals and plants.

50535.q: Which animal on the Grossglockner warns of danger with a loud whistle?
50535.e: Marmots live in burrows in the mountain meadows. If one sees an eagle, it whistles loudly.
50535.m: Marmots warn others with a whistle.

50536.q: Roughly how high is the Grossglockner, Austria's highest mountain?
50536.e: The Grossglockner is 3,798 m high. It was first climbed in 1800.
50536.m: The Grossglockner is almost 3,800 m high.

50537.q: What stands on the summit of the Grossglockner?
50537.e: There is a metal summit cross on the top. Climbers love taking a photo there.
50537.m: There is a summit cross on the Grossglockner.

50538.q: Which mountain range does the Grossglockner belong to?
50538.e: The Grossglockner belongs to the Alps, just like the high mountains of Switzerland.
50538.m: The Grossglockner is in the Alps.

50539.q: Which mountain is the highest in Germany?
50539.e: The Zugspitze is the highest mountain in Germany. It is in Bavaria.
50539.m: The Zugspitze is the highest mountain in Germany.

50540.q: Roughly how high is the Zugspitze?
50540.e: The Zugspitze is 2,962 metres high. That is almost 3,000 metres.
50540.m: The Zugspitze is almost 3,000 metres high.

50541.q: A border runs over the summit of the Zugspitze. With which country?
50541.e: Germany and Austria meet on the Zugspitze. You can walk across the border there.
50541.m: The border with Austria runs over the Zugspitze.

50542.q: What is there on the Zugspitze that hardly exists anywhere else in Germany?
50542.e: There are small glaciers on the Zugspitze. Germany has only very few glaciers.
50542.m: There are glaciers on the Zugspitze.

50543.q: What kind of railway can take you almost to the top of the Zugspitze?
50543.e: A rack railway runs through a tunnel to just below the summit. There are also cable cars.
50543.m: A rack railway goes up the Zugspitze.

50544.q: Which well-known town lies at the foot of the Zugspitze?
50544.e: Garmisch-Partenkirchen lies right below the Zugspitze. The railways up the mountain start there.
50544.m: Garmisch-Partenkirchen lies at the foot of the Zugspitze.

50545.q: What colour is the summit cross on the Zugspitze?
50545.e: The summit cross on the Zugspitze is gilded. In the sun it shines and can be seen from far away.
50545.m: The summit cross on the Zugspitze is golden.

50546.q: What do experts measure at the station on the summit of the Zugspitze?
50546.e: There is a weather station on the Zugspitze. Wind, temperature and snow have been measured there for more than 100 years.
50546.m: The weather is measured on the Zugspitze.

50547.q: Which two countries does Liechtenstein border?
50547.e: Liechtenstein lies between Switzerland and Austria. It has only these two neighbours.

50548.q: How many municipalities make up Liechtenstein?
50548.e: Liechtenstein has only 11 municipalities. The country is very small.

50549.q: About how many people live in Liechtenstein (as of 2024)?

50550.q: In which country is the town of Vaduz?
50550.e: Vaduz is the capital of Liechtenstein. The small country lies between Switzerland and Austria.

50551.q: What stands on a rock high above Vaduz?
50551.e: Vaduz Castle stands high above the town. It is several hundred years old.

50552.q: Who lives in the castle high above Vaduz?
50552.e: Liechtenstein is a principality. The princely family lives in Vaduz Castle.
50552.m: The prince lives in Vaduz Castle.

50553.q: What can you see at the Postal Museum in Vaduz?
50553.e: Liechtenstein is known for its beautiful stamps. You can see many of them in the Postal Museum.
50553.m: The Postal Museum in Vaduz has stamps.

50554.e: Vaduz lies in the Rhine valley. The Rhine flows past the town to the west.

50555.q: What is the parliament that meets in Vaduz called?
50555.e: The parliament of Liechtenstein is called the Landtag. It has 25 members.
50555.m: The parliament of Liechtenstein is called the Landtag.

50556.q: In which football league does FC Vaduz play?
50556.e: Liechtenstein has no football league of its own. So FC Vaduz and other clubs play in Switzerland.
50556.m: FC Vaduz plays in the Swiss league.

50557.q: What is the pedestrian zone in the centre of Vaduz called?
50557.e: The pedestrian zone of Vaduz is called Städtle. It has museums, shops and cafés.
50557.m: The centre of Vaduz is called Städtle.

50558.q: What kind of building is the Colosseum?
50558.e: The Colosseum is an amphitheatre, which means an arena with rows of seats all around. Lots of people watched the games there.
50558.m: The Colosseum is a huge arena.

50559.q: Who used to fight in front of spectators in the Colosseum?
50559.e: Gladiators were fighters in ancient Rome. They fought in the arena to entertain the crowd.

50560.e: The Colosseum was built by the Romans. It was the largest arena in the whole Roman Empire.
50560.m: The ancient Romans built the Colosseum.

50561.q: Roughly how old is the Colosseum?
50561.e: The Colosseum was opened in AD 80. That was almost 2,000 years ago.
50561.m: The Colosseum is almost 2,000 years old.

50562.q: What shape is the Colosseum when you look at it from above?
50562.e: The Colosseum is roundish and long, in other words oval. That way all the spectators could see into the arena well.

50563.q: About how many spectators fitted into the Colosseum?
50563.e: There was room for around 50,000 people in the Colosseum. That is about as many as in a big football stadium.
50563.m: About 50,000 people fitted into the Colosseum.

50564.q: What was there under the floor of the arena in the Colosseum?
50564.e: Under the arena there were many passages and chambers. Fighters and animals waited there for their turn.
50564.m: There were passages and rooms under the arena of the Colosseum.

50565.q: What does Venice have instead of many streets?
50565.e: In Venice, water flows through the city. People travel through the canals by boat.
50565.m: Venice has many canals instead of streets.

50566.q: What are the long, narrow boats in Venice called?
50566.e: Gondolas are the symbol of Venice. Tourists ride through the city in them.
50566.m: The typical boats in Venice are called gondolas.

50567.q: Where does the man who steers a gondola in Venice stand?
a: At the back of the gondola
At the front of the gondola
In the middle of the gondola
He sits down inside the gondola
50567.e: The gondolier stands at the back of the gondola. From there he steers it with a long oar.
50567.m: The gondolier stands at the back of the gondola.

50568.q: What does the gondolier use to move his gondola forward?
50568.e: The gondolier stands and moves the boat with a single long oar. A gondola has no engine.
50568.m: A gondola is moved with an oar.

50569.q: What colour are the gondolas in Venice almost always?
50569.e: For a long time, gondolas have been painted black. That is the rule.

50570.q: What shape is the Grand Canal, the biggest canal in Venice?
50570.e: The Grand Canal winds through the whole city in a big S-bend. It is the main street on the water.
50570.m: The Grand Canal flows through Venice in an S-bend.

50571.q: What is the famous old bridge over the biggest canal in Venice called?
50571.e: The Rialto Bridge is built of stone and has a high arch. It is the oldest bridge over the biggest canal.
50571.m: The Rialto Bridge is the most famous bridge in Venice.

50572.q: What is the big square with the church of San Marco in Venice called?
50572.e: St Mark's Square is the most important square in Venice. Lots of pigeons live there too.
50572.m: The big square with the church of San Marco is called St Mark's Square.

50573.e: Venice lies in the north-east of Italy on the Adriatic. The Adriatic is part of the Mediterranean.

50574.q: What is the city of Venice built on?
50574.e: Venice lies in a lagoon and is made up of more than a hundred small islands. Bridges connect the islands.
50574.m: Venice is built on lots of small islands.

50575.q: What is the Carnival of Venice especially known for?
50575.e: At the carnival, many people wear magnificent masks and costumes. Masks from Venice are known all over the world.
50575.m: The Carnival of Venice is known for its masks.

50576.q: Why is the Tower of Pisa so famous?
a: Because it is made of gold
50576.e: The tower tilts to one side. That is why it is also called the “Leaning Tower”.
50576.m: The Tower of Pisa is famous because it leans.

50577.q: Why did the Tower of Pisa start to lean?
a: It was built that way on purpose
50577.e: The ground under the tower is soft. Even while it was being built, the tower sank on one side.
50577.m: The Tower of Pisa leans because the ground is soft.

50578.q: What was the Tower of Pisa built as?
50578.e: The tower belongs to Pisa Cathedral. Its bells hang at the top.
50578.m: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is a bell tower.

50580.q: Roughly how tall is the Tower of Pisa?
50580.e: The tower is around 56 metres tall. That is about as tall as a building with 18 floors.
50580.m: The Tower of Pisa is about 56 metres tall.

50581.q: What did experts do so that the Tower of Pisa would not fall over?
50581.e: The tower was closed from 1990 to 2001. Experts made it safe and straightened it a little.
50581.m: Experts made the Tower of Pisa safe.

50582.q: What funny photo do many tourists take at the Tower of Pisa?
a: They pretend to hold it up
They lie on the ground in front of it
They stand on one leg in front of it
50582.e: Many visitors stand so that it looks in the photo as if they are holding the tower. That way it seems not to fall over.
50582.m: At the Tower of Pisa, many tourists pretend in photos to hold it up.

50583.q: What is the square on which the Tower of Pisa stands called?
50583.e: In Italian it is called “Piazza dei Miracoli”. The cathedral and the baptistery also stand there.
50583.m: The Tower of Pisa stands on the Square of Miracles.

50584.q: How can people at the Vatican tell that a new pope has been elected?
50584.e: During the election of a pope, the ballot papers are burnt after each vote. If white smoke rises from the chimney of the Sistine Chapel, a new pope has been elected.
50584.m: White smoke shows that a new pope has been elected.

50585.q: Who is the head of Vatican City?
50585.e: The Pope is the head of the Catholic Church. He also governs this small country.
50585.m: The Pope is the head of Vatican City.

50586.e: Swiss soldiers have protected the Pope since 1506. All the guards are Swiss citizens.
50586.m: The Swiss Guard protects the Pope.

50587.q: What colours is the colourful uniform of the Swiss Guard?
50587.e: The famous uniform has blue, yellow and red stripes. The guards often wear a helmet with it.
50587.m: The uniform of the Swiss Guard is blue, yellow and red.

50589.q: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican?
50589.e: Michelangelo painted the huge ceiling more than 500 years ago. He worked on it for about four years.
50589.m: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

50590.q: Roughly what shape is the island of Sicily?
50590.e: Sicily has three points, so it looks like a triangle. That is why the ancient Greeks called the island Trinacria, the three-pointed one.
50590.m: Sicily is roughly the shape of a triangle.

50591.q: What is the big volcano on Sicily called?
50591.e: Etna is the highest active volcano in Europe. It erupts often.
50591.m: The volcano Etna is on Sicily.

50592.q: What is the capital of Sicily?
50592.e: Palermo lies on the north coast of the island. It is the largest city in Sicily.
50592.m: Palermo is the capital of Sicily.

50593.q: Where is Sicily when you look at Italy on a map?
a: In front of the tip of the boot
In the middle of the Alps
50593.e: Sicily lies in the south, right in front of the tip of the boot. It looks as if the boot is kicking the island away.
50593.m: Sicily lies in front of the tip of the Italian boot.

50594.q: What is the narrow stretch of sea between Sicily and the mainland called?
50594.e: At its narrowest point, the Strait of Messina is only about three kilometres wide. Ferries go back and forth there.
50594.m: The Strait of Messina lies between Sicily and the mainland.

50595.q: How does a train get from the mainland to Sicily?
50595.e: There is no bridge and no tunnel to Sicily. So the train carriages are loaded onto a ferry.
50595.m: Trains get to Sicily by ferry.

50596.q: Which fruits grow in especially large amounts on Sicily?
50596.e: Sicily is warm and sunny. That is why a great many lemons and oranges grow there.
50596.m: Lots of lemons and oranges grow on Sicily.

50597.q: Which ancient buildings can you visit near Agrigento on Sicily?
50597.e: A very long time ago, Greeks lived on Sicily. Near Agrigento, their temples still stand today in the Valley of the Temples.
50597.m: Ancient Greek temples stand near Agrigento on Sicily.

50598.q: Which Roman town was buried when Vesuvius erupted?
50598.e: Pompeii was not far from the volcano and was buried in the eruption. Today you can visit the excavated town.
50598.m: Vesuvius buried the town of Pompeii.

50599.q: When did Vesuvius bury the ancient town of Pompeii?
50599.e: The great eruption was in AD 79. That was almost 2,000 years ago.

50600.q: What covered Pompeii when the volcano erupted?
50600.e: Vesuvius threw out huge amounts of ash and small stones. These fell on the town and buried it.
50600.m: Pompeii was covered with ash and small stones.

50601.q: Which other Roman town was also buried by Vesuvius?
50601.e: Herculaneum also lay at the foot of Vesuvius. The town was buried in the same eruption.
50601.m: Herculaneum was also buried by Vesuvius.

50602.q: Which big city lies at the foot of Vesuvius?
50602.e: Vesuvius rises above the Bay of Naples. It last erupted in 1944 and is watched closely.

50603.e: Vesuvius is around 1,281 metres high. So it is much smaller than the high mountains in the Alps.

50604.q: What is Milan called in Italian?
50604.e: Italians call their city Milano. In English we say Milan.
50604.m: Milan is called Milano in Italian.

50605.q: What is the famous big church in Milan called?
50605.e: Milan Cathedral has many pointed spires and countless statues. It is one of the largest churches in the world.
50605.m: The big church in Milan is called Milan Cathedral.

50606.q: What is Milan known for all over the world?
50606.e: Milan has many fashion houses and fashion shows. The city is seen as one of the fashion capitals.

50607.q: What is the famous opera house in Milan called?
50607.e: The Teatro alla Scala is one of the most famous opera houses in the world. Great singers perform there.
50607.m: The famous opera house in Milan is called La Scala.

50608.q: How many big football clubs play at the San Siro stadium in Milan?
50608.e: AC Milan and Inter Milan share the stadium. When they play each other, it is a big derby.
50608.m: Two big football clubs in Milan share one stadium.

50609.q: Which long tunnel does the train from Zurich to Milan go through?
50609.e: At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. Trains from Zurich towards Milan travel through it.
50609.m: The train from Zurich to Milan goes through the Gotthard Base Tunnel.

50610.q: Which famous wall painting by Leonardo da Vinci can you see in Milan?
50610.e: Leonardo da Vinci painted “The Last Supper” on a wall in a monastery in Milan. It shows Jesus eating with his disciples.
50610.m: Leonardo da Vinci's wall painting “The Last Supper” is in Milan.

50611.q: Which Christmas cake comes from Milan?
50611.e: Panettone is a tall, light cake with raisins. It originally comes from Milan.

50612.q: In which country is the city of Florence?
50612.e: Florence is in Italy. Italians call their city Firenze.

50613.q: Florence is the capital of which region?
50613.e: Florence is the capital of Tuscany. The region is known for its gentle hills.
50613.m: Florence is the capital of Tuscany.

50614.q: What is the river that flows through Florence called?
50614.e: The Arno flows right through the middle of Florence. Several bridges cross it.

50615.q: What is special about the Ponte Vecchio bridge in Florence?
a: There are small shops on it
50615.e: There are many small shops on the Ponte Vecchio. Today it is mostly goldsmiths who sell their jewellery there.
50615.m: There are small shops on the Ponte Vecchio in Florence.

50616.q: What is especially eye-catching about Florence Cathedral?
50616.e: The cathedral has an enormous dome made of red bricks. It is the city's landmark.
50616.m: Florence Cathedral has a huge red dome.

50617.q: Which famous statue by Michelangelo stands in Florence?
50617.e: Michelangelo carved David from a single large block of marble. The figure is more than five metres tall.
50617.m: Michelangelo's statue of David stands in Florence.

50618.q: What is the famous art museum in Florence called?
50618.e: Many famous paintings hang in the Uffizi. Millions of visitors come every year.
50618.m: The famous art museum in Florence is called the Uffizi.

50619.q: Which rich family ruled Florence for a long time?
50619.e: The Medici were rich bankers. They supported many artists in Florence.
50619.m: The Medici family ruled Florence for a long time.

a: The capital of the Tuscan island of Elba
50620.e: From 1865 to 1871, Florence was the capital of the Kingdom of Italy. After that, Rome became the capital.
50620.m: Florence was the capital of Italy for a few years.

50621.q: Which famous poet was born in Florence?
50621.e: Dante lived more than 700 years ago. He is regarded as Italy's most important poet.
50621.m: The poet Dante was born in Florence.

50622.q: Which region forms the heel of the Italian boot?
50622.e: Apulia is right in the south-east of Italy. On the map, that is the heel of the boot.
50622.m: Apulia is the heel of the Italian boot.

50623.q: Which region forms the toe of the Italian boot?
50623.e: Calabria is right in the south of the mainland. It is the toe of the boot.
50623.m: Calabria is the toe of the Italian boot.

50624.q: Which mountain range runs like a spine through the Italian boot?
50624.e: The Apennines run from north to south through almost all of Italy. They are like the backbone of the country.
50624.m: The Apennines run through the Italian boot.

50625.q: Which city is the capital of Italy?
50625.e: Rome is the capital and the largest city of Italy. The government is based there.
50625.m: The capital of Italy is Rome.

50626.q: Which of these countries is a neighbour of Italy?
50626.e: In the north, Italy borders Switzerland. The canton of Ticino lies right on the border.
50626.m: Switzerland is a neighbour of Italy.

50627.e: Italy juts far out into the Mediterranean. That is why the country has so many beaches.

50628.q: What is the second big island of Italy, which lies west of the boot, called?
50628.e: Sardinia lies out in the sea west of Italy. It is Italy's second-largest island.
50628.m: Sardinia is a large island of Italy.

50629.q: What is the longest river in Italy called?
50629.e: The Po flows through northern Italy to the Adriatic. It is around 650 kilometres long.
50629.m: The Po is Italy's longest river.

50630.q: Which language is spoken in Italy and also in Ticino?
50630.e: People in Italy speak Italian. Italian is also a national language in Switzerland.
50630.m: Italian is spoken in Italy and in Ticino.

50631.e: San Marino is a separate, independent country. It is one of the smallest countries in the world.
50631.m: San Marino is a very small country.

50632.q: What is the capital of San Marino?
50632.e: The capital has the same name as the country. It is a beautiful old town with walls.
50632.m: The capital of San Marino is also called San Marino.

50633.q: Where is the capital of San Marino?
50633.e: The old town lies high up on Monte Titano. From there you can see as far as the sea.
50633.m: The capital of San Marino is on a mountain.

50634.q: What is San Marino said to be?
a: The oldest republic in the world
The youngest country in the world
50634.e: According to legend, San Marino was founded in the year 301. It is regarded as the oldest republic in the world that still exists.
50634.m: San Marino is said to be the oldest republic in the world.

50635.q: How many towers stand on top of the mountain in San Marino?
50635.e: Three fortress towers stand on the summit. You can even see them on the flag of San Marino.
50635.m: Three towers stand on the mountain of San Marino.

50636.q: How many heads of state does San Marino have at the same time?
50636.e: San Marino is led by two Captains Regent. They change every six months.
50636.m: San Marino has two heads of state at the same time.

50637.q: What money do you pay with in San Marino?
50637.e: People in San Marino have paid with euros since 2002. San Marino is even allowed to mint its own euro coins.
50637.m: In San Marino you pay with euros.

50638.q: Who is San Marino named after?
50638.e: According to legend, the stonemason Marinus founded the country. Later he was honoured as a saint.
50638.m: San Marino is named after Saint Marinus.

50639.q: Roughly how many people live in San Marino?
50639.e: Around 34,000 people live in San Marino (as of 2023). That is about as many as in a smaller Swiss town.
50639.m: About 34,000 people live in San Marino.

50640.q: Which well-known seaside resort lies close to San Marino?
50640.e: Rimini is only just over 20 kilometres from San Marino, on the Adriatic. Many holidaymakers take a trip from there to San Marino.
50640.m: The seaside resort of Rimini lies close to San Marino.

50641.q: Which Italian city does pizza come from?
50641.e: Pizza as we know it was invented in Naples. There are still a great many pizzerias there today.

50642.q: Which cheese goes on a pizza Margherita?
50642.e: White mozzarella goes on a pizza Margherita. It melts nice and soft in the oven.
50642.m: Mozzarella goes on a pizza Margherita.

50643.q: Which green leaf is on a pizza Margherita?
50643.e: Fresh basil leaves lie on a pizza Margherita. They give the pizza a lovely smell.
50643.m: There is basil on a pizza Margherita.

50644.q: Who is the pizza Margherita named after?
