50644.e: The pizza was named after Queen Margherita of Italy. According to legend, she especially liked this pizza.
50644.m: The pizza Margherita is named after a queen.

50645.q: What is a real Neapolitan pizza traditionally baked in?
50645.e: The pizza goes into a very hot wood-fired oven. There it is ready in about one and a half minutes.
50645.m: Real Neapolitan pizza is baked in a wood-fired oven.

50646.q: What is a pizza maker called in Italy?
50646.e: A pizzaiolo makes the dough, puts on the toppings and bakes the pizza. The art of the pizzaioli of Naples is part of UNESCO's cultural heritage.
50646.m: A pizza maker is called a pizzaiolo in Italian.

50647.q: Which pizza from Naples has no cheese?
50647.e: Pizza Marinara has tomatoes, garlic, oregano and olive oil. Cheese does not go on it.
50647.m: Pizza Marinara is a pizza without cheese.

50648.q: What is pizza dough mainly made of?
50648.e: The dough only needs flour, water, yeast and salt. The yeast makes the dough rise.
50648.m: Pizza dough is made of flour, water, yeast and salt.

50649.q: On which square in Madrid do people eat twelve grapes to the chimes of the clock on New Year's Eve?
50649.e: At midnight a well-known clock strikes at the Puerta del Sol. With each chime you eat a grape, which is supposed to bring luck.
50649.m: On New Year's Eve, people eat twelve grapes at the Puerta del Sol.

50650.q: Which city in Spain has the most inhabitants?
50650.e: Madrid is the largest city in Spain. More than three million people live in the city (as of 2024).
50650.m: Madrid is the largest city in Spain.

50651.q: Roughly where in Spain is Madrid?
50651.e: Madrid lies almost exactly in the middle of the country. The main roads lead from there in all directions.
50651.m: Madrid lies in the middle of Spain.

50652.q: Which famous art museum is in Madrid?
50652.e: The Prado in Madrid is one of the most important art museums in the world. Many pictures by Spanish painters hang there.
50652.m: Famous paintings hang in the Prado in Madrid.

50653.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of Madrid?
50653.e: The coat of arms of Madrid shows a bear by a strawberry tree. This bear also stands as a statue in the city.
50653.m: The bear and the strawberry tree are the symbol of Madrid.

50654.q: What is Madrid's big city park with a lake called?
50654.e: The Retiro is the best-known park in Madrid. You can go out on its lake in small rowing boats.
50654.m: You can go boating in Retiro Park in Madrid.

a: No, far away from the sea
50655.e: Madrid lies in the middle of Spain, far from the coast. Only the small River Manzanares flows through the city.
50655.m: Madrid is not by the sea.

50656.q: What is the stadium of the football club Real Madrid called?
50656.e: Real Madrid plays at the Santiago Bernabéu stadium. It is named after a former president of the club.
50656.m: Real Madrid plays at the Santiago Bernabéu.

50657.q: Who has a huge palace in Madrid?
50657.e: Spain has a king. The Royal Palace in Madrid is used for ceremonies of the royal family.
50657.m: Spain is a kingdom with a royal palace in Madrid.

50658.e: Barcelona is on the east coast of Spain. There the city meets the Mediterranean.
50658.m: Barcelona is a city on the Mediterranean.

50659.q: In which region of Spain is Barcelona?
50659.e: Barcelona is the capital of the region of Catalonia. Catalonia is in the north-east of Spain.
50659.m: Barcelona is the capital of Catalonia.

50660.q: Which language is spoken in Barcelona besides Spanish?
50660.e: Many people in Barcelona speak Catalan and Spanish. Street signs are often in Catalan.
50660.m: In Barcelona people speak Catalan and Spanish.

50661.q: In which country is the city of Barcelona?
50661.e: Barcelona is in the north-east of Spain by the sea. It is one of the largest cities in the country.

50662.q: A big colourful lizard sits in a park in Barcelona. What is it made of?
a: Lots of small pieces of tile
50662.e: The lizard in Park Güell is a mosaic. It is put together from lots of small colourful pieces of tile.
50662.m: The colourful lizard in Barcelona is made of pieces of tile.

50663.q: Which big sporting event took place in Barcelona in 1992?
50663.e: The Summer Olympics took place in Barcelona in 1992. Many new sports facilities were built in the city for them.
50663.m: Barcelona hosted the Summer Olympics in 1992.

50664.q: Where does Barcelona rank among Spain's largest cities?
50664.e: Only one city in Spain has more inhabitants than Barcelona. So Barcelona is the second-largest city in the country.
50664.m: Barcelona is the second-largest city in Spain.

50665.q: What is the big football stadium of FC Barcelona called?
50665.e: FC Barcelona plays at the Camp Nou. It is the biggest football stadium in Europe.
50665.m: FC Barcelona plays at the Camp Nou.

50666.e: The Sagrada Família is a huge church. Its name means “Holy Family”.
50666.m: The Sagrada Família is a huge church.

50667.q: In which city is the Sagrada Família?
50667.e: The Sagrada Família is in Barcelona. Millions of people visit it every year.
50667.m: The Sagrada Família is in Barcelona.

50668.q: Which architect designed the Sagrada Família?
50668.e: Antoni Gaudí worked on the church for more than 40 years. He planned many round and playful shapes.
50668.m: Antoni Gaudí designed the Sagrada Família.

50669.q: In which year did building work on the Sagrada Família begin?
50669.e: The foundation stone was laid in 1882. The church has been under construction ever since.
50669.m: Building work on the Sagrada Família began in 1882.

50670.q: Is the Sagrada Família completely finished yet (as of 2026)?
a: No, it is still being built
50670.e: Even after more than 140 years, the church is not quite finished. Some towers and parts are still missing.
50670.m: The Sagrada Família has been under construction for more than 140 years.

50671.q: What is special about the Sagrada Família?
a: It has been under construction for more than 100 years
It is made entirely of wood
It is made entirely of glass
50671.e: Building work on the church began in 1882. Work still goes on today, and new towers keep being added.
50671.m: The Sagrada Família has been under construction for more than 100 years.

50672.q: What do the columns inside the Sagrada Família look like?
50672.e: At the top, the columns branch out like boughs. So the inside looks like a forest of stone.
50672.m: The columns in the Sagrada Família look like trees.

50673.q: Who is the tallest tower of the Sagrada Família dedicated to?
50673.e: The tower in the middle is dedicated to Jesus Christ. It is planned to be around 172 metres tall and rises above all the other towers.
50673.m: The tallest tower of the Sagrada Família is dedicated to Jesus Christ.

50674.q: How is the ongoing building of the Sagrada Família paid for?
50674.e: The church is being built with donations and with the money from entrance tickets. That was planned from the very start.
50674.m: Visitors to the Sagrada Família help with the building through their entrance fees.

50675.q: On how many hills is Lisbon said to be built?
50675.e: Lisbon is often called the city of seven hills. That is why there are so many steep alleys and steps there.
50675.m: Lisbon is also called the city of seven hills.

50676.e: Lisbon lies where the Tagus flows into the Atlantic. The river is very wide there.
50676.m: Lisbon is at the mouth of the Tagus.

50677.q: Which old means of transport is famous in Lisbon?
50677.e: Small yellow trams run through the narrow, steep streets. Line 28 is especially well known.
50677.m: Small yellow trams run in Lisbon.

50678.q: Which famous bridge does Lisbon's red suspension bridge look like?
50678.e: The 25 de Abril Bridge is red and looks like the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco. It crosses the River Tagus.
50678.m: The red bridge in Lisbon looks like the Golden Gate Bridge.

50679.q: What destroyed large parts of Lisbon in 1755?
50679.e: In 1755 the earth shook very strongly. Then came a tsunami and fires, and the city was rebuilt.
50679.m: A big earthquake destroyed Lisbon in 1755.

50680.q: What is the sad style of singing that Lisbon is known for called?
50680.e: Fado is an emotional, often sad song. It is usually accompanied by guitars and is part of UNESCO's cultural heritage.
50680.m: Fado is the well-known song from Lisbon.

50681.q: Which old tower stands right by the water in Lisbon?
50681.e: Belém Tower was built on the shore about 500 years ago. It was meant to protect the entrance to the harbour.
50681.m: Belém Tower stands on the shore in Lisbon.

50682.q: Which sweet pastry is especially popular in Lisbon?
50682.e: Pastéis de nata are small puff pastry tarts filled with custard. They are often eaten with cinnamon.
50682.m: Pastéis de nata are custard tarts from Portugal.

50683.q: What are many house walls in Lisbon decorated with?
50683.e: Many houses are covered with colourful tiles, often blue and white. These tiles are called azulejos.
50683.m: The painted tiles in Portugal are called azulejos.

50684.q: What does the sweet pastry ensaïmada from Majorca look like?
50684.e: The ensaïmada is a soft pastry from Majorca, coiled like a snail shell. There is often icing sugar on top.
50684.m: The ensaïmada is a coiled pastry from Majorca.

50685.q: Which group of islands does Majorca belong to?
50685.e: Majorca belongs to the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean. Menorca and Ibiza belong to them too.
50685.m: Majorca is one of the Balearic Islands.

50686.q: Are there high mountains on Majorca?
a: No, the island is completely flat
No, there are only sand dunes
50686.e: The highest mountain on Majorca is called Puig Major. It is around 1,445 metres high and lies in the north-west of the island.
50686.m: There are mountains over 1,000 metres on Majorca.

50687.q: What do German-speaking holidaymakers call the old train from Palma to Sóller?
50687.e: Since 1912, the train has run through the mountains to Sóller with old wood-panelled carriages. Because of its colour, German-speaking tourists call it “Roter Blitz”, which means Red Lightning.
50687.m: Tourists call the old train to Sóller Red Lightning.

50688.q: What is the mountain range in the north-west of Majorca called?
50688.e: The Serra de Tramuntana runs along the north-west coast. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
50688.m: The Serra de Tramuntana is the mountain range of Majorca.

50689.q: Which big old building stands right by the sea in Palma on Majorca?
50689.e: La Seu Cathedral is a huge church at the harbour of Palma. You can see it from far away.
50689.m: Palma's big church stands right by the sea.

50690.q: Which island lies east of Majorca?
50690.e: Menorca is the smaller neighbouring island to the east. By ferry you can get there in a few hours.
50690.m: Menorca is the neighbouring island east of Majorca.

50691.q: What is the cape with a lighthouse right in the north of Majorca called?
50691.e: Cap de Formentor lies at the end of a long, rocky peninsula. It is the northernmost point of Majorca.
50691.m: Cap de Formentor is right in the north of Majorca.

50692.q: Off which continent do the Canary Islands lie?
50692.e: The Canaries lie in the Atlantic off the coast of Africa. Morocco is not far away.
50692.m: The Canaries lie off the coast of Africa.

50693.q: How were the Canary Islands formed?
50693.e: The islands grew out of the sea through volcanic eruptions. That is why there is so much black lava rock there.
50693.m: The Canary Islands are volcanic islands.

50694.q: What is the high volcano on Tenerife called?
50694.e: Teide on Tenerife is 3,715 metres high. It is the highest mountain in Spain.
50694.m: Teide is the highest mountain in Spain.

50695.q: Which is the largest of the Canary Islands?
50695.e: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands. Most people live there too.
50695.m: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands.

50696.q: How many larger main islands do the Canaries have?
50696.e: The Canaries have seven larger islands, each with its own administration. There are also a few small islands.
50696.m: The Canaries have seven main islands.

50697.q: Which bird is named after the Canary Islands?
50697.e: The wild ancestor of the canary lives on the Canaries. Today many people keep yellow canaries as pets.
50697.m: The canary comes from the Canary Islands.

50698.e: The Canaries are volcanic islands. On Lanzarote there are still fire mountains today, where the ground is very hot.
50698.m: The Canary Islands were formed by volcanoes.

50699.q: Between which two countries is Andorra?
50699.e: Andorra lies between Spain to the south and France to the north. It is surrounded by both countries.
50699.m: Andorra lies between Spain and France.

50700.q: Which sport is very popular in Andorra in winter?
50700.e: Andorra has high mountains with lots of snow. In winter, many visitors come to ski.
50700.m: People love skiing in Andorra in winter.

50701.q: What is the capital of Andorra?
50701.e: The capital is called Andorra la Vella. It is one of the highest capitals in Europe.
50701.m: Andorra la Vella is the capital of Andorra.

50702.q: Which language is the official language in Andorra?
50702.e: Catalan is the only official language in Andorra. Many people also speak Spanish and French.
50702.m: Catalan is the official language in Andorra.

50703.q: Does Andorra have a coastline on the sea?
50703.e: Andorra lies in the mountains and has no coast. Like Switzerland, it is a landlocked country.
50703.m: Like Switzerland, Andorra has no sea.

50704.e: Andorra is a separate, very small country. It has fewer inhabitants than the city of Bern.
50704.m: Andorra is a very small country.

50705.q: What money do you pay with in Andorra?
50705.e: Andorra uses the euro, although it is not in the European Union. Spain and France also have the euro.
50705.m: In Andorra you pay with euros.

50706.q: How many heads of state does Andorra have?
50706.e: Andorra has two co-princes. One is the President of France, the other is a bishop from Spain.
50706.m: Andorra has two co-princes as heads of state.

50707.e: Flamenco is a Spanish art made up of singing, guitar playing and dancing. It is often very passionate.
50707.m: Flamenco is music and dance from Spain.

50708.q: Which region of Spain does flamenco come from?
50708.e: Flamenco comes from Andalusia in the south of Spain. There are still many flamenco festivals there today.

50709.q: Which instrument is usually played in flamenco?
50709.e: The flamenco guitar is the most important instrument. It accompanies the singing and the dancing.
50709.m: A guitar is usually played in flamenco.

50710.q: What are the small wooden clappers that dancers hold in their hands called?
50710.e: Castanets are two small wooden shells that are clicked together. They keep the beat.

50711.q: What do the audience and musicians often do in time to flamenco?
50711.e: In flamenco, people clap their hands in rhythm. The clapping is part of the music.

50712.q: What do flamenco dancers use to make loud sounds on the floor?
50712.e: The dancers stamp hard on the floor with their shoes. For this, the shoes have small nails in the toe and heel.
50712.m: Flamenco dancers stamp out the rhythm with their shoes.

50713.q: What does a typical flamenco dress look like?
a: It is made entirely of leather
50713.e: Flamenco dresses have lots of frills and are often spotted. When the dancer spins, the frills fly out beautifully.
50713.m: Flamenco dresses have lots of frills.

50714.q: What has flamenco been part of since 2010?
a: The Seven Wonders of the World
50714.e: In 2010, UNESCO added flamenco to the cultural heritage of humanity. This is meant to protect the art.
50714.m: Flamenco has been part of UNESCO's cultural heritage since 2010.

50715.q: Which two large countries are on the Iberian Peninsula?
50715.e: The Iberian Peninsula is mainly made up of Spain and Portugal. It is in the south-west of Europe.
50715.m: Spain and Portugal are on the Iberian Peninsula.

50716.q: Which two seas surround the Iberian Peninsula?
a: The North Sea and the Baltic Sea
The Red Sea and the Black Sea
The Pacific and the Indian Ocean
50716.e: To the west and north is the Atlantic, to the east and south the Mediterranean. The peninsula lies in between.
50716.m: The Iberian Peninsula lies between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

50717.q: Which is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula?
50717.e: The Tagus is more than 1,000 kilometres long. It flows from Spain through Portugal into the Atlantic.
50717.m: The Tagus is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula.

50718.q: What is the large plateau in the middle of Spain called?
50718.e: The Meseta is a wide, high plain. It takes up a large part of central Spain.
50718.m: The Meseta is the plateau in the middle of Spain.

50719.q: Which ancient people is the Iberian Peninsula named after?
50719.e: The Iberians lived in the east and south of the peninsula more than 2,000 years ago. It got its name from them.
50719.m: The Iberian Peninsula is named after the Iberians.

50720.q: Which country takes up most of the Iberian Peninsula?
50720.e: Spain is about five times as big as Portugal. It takes up most of the peninsula.
50720.m: Spain is much bigger than Portugal.

50721.q: In which part of the Iberian Peninsula is Portugal?
50721.e: Portugal is in the west of the peninsula on the Atlantic. To the east it borders Spain.
50721.m: Portugal is in the west of the Iberian Peninsula.

50722.q: How many neighbouring countries does Portugal have?
50722.e: Portugal only borders Spain. On the other side is the Atlantic.

50723.q: In which country is the Algarve?
50723.e: The Algarve is a region in Portugal. Many families go on holiday there.

50724.q: In which part of Portugal is the Algarve?
50724.e: The Algarve is the southernmost region of Portugal. Its coast faces south towards the sea.
50724.m: The Algarve is the south of Portugal.

50725.q: What is the coast of the Algarve famous for?
50725.e: The Algarve has golden-yellow rocks, caves in the water and beautiful beaches. You can go into the grottoes by boat.
50725.m: The Algarve has rocks, grottoes and beaches.

50726.q: What is the capital of the Algarve, with the big airport, called?
50726.e: Faro is the capital of the Algarve. Many holidaymakers land at Faro airport.
50726.m: Faro is the capital of the Algarve.

50727.q: Which special point lies in the Algarve at Cape St Vincent?
50727.e: Cape St Vincent is the south-westernmost point of mainland Europe. Beyond it there is only the Atlantic.
50727.m: The south-west corner of Europe is at Cape St Vincent.

50728.q: Why do so many people travel to the Algarve?
50728.e: The Algarve has a great many sunny days a year. On top of that there are warm summers and beautiful beaches.
50728.m: The sun shines very often in the Algarve.

50729.q: Which fruits often grow in the Algarve?
50729.e: There are many orange trees in the Algarve. The oranges there are known for their sweet taste.
50729.m: Lots of oranges grow in the Algarve.

50730.q: Which small sea fish is often grilled in the Algarve?
50730.e: Grilled sardines are a popular meal in the Algarve. Trout, carp and pike live in fresh water.
50730.m: People in the Algarve love grilled sardines.

50731.q: Which country does Gibraltar belong to?
50731.e: Gibraltar lies in the south of Spain but belongs to Britain. That is why English is the official language there.

50732.q: Which animals live in the wild on the Rock of Gibraltar?
50732.e: Barbary macaques live on the Rock. They are the only monkeys living in the wild in Europe.
50732.m: Monkeys live on the Rock of Gibraltar.

50733.q: Which two seas does the Strait of Gibraltar connect?
a: The North Sea and the Baltic Sea
The Mediterranean and the Red Sea
50733.e: The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow strait. Water flows through it between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
50733.m: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

50734.q: Which country in Africa lies opposite Gibraltar?
50734.e: Morocco lies opposite Gibraltar. At the narrowest point, Europe and Africa are only about 14 kilometres apart.
50734.m: From Gibraltar you can see Morocco.

50735.q: What is the Rock of Gibraltar made of?
50735.e: The Rock is made of limestone. Caves form easily in this kind of rock.
50735.m: The Rock of Gibraltar is made of limestone.

50736.q: Roughly how high is the Rock of Gibraltar?
50736.e: The Rock is about 426 metres high. It rises steeply out of the sea.
50736.m: The Rock of Gibraltar is about 430 metres high.

50737.q: What is there inside the Rock of Gibraltar?
50737.e: Inside the Rock there are caves with stalactites, such as St Michael's Cave. Soldiers also dug many tunnels long ago.
50737.m: The Rock of Gibraltar is full of caves and tunnels.

50738.q: What did the ancient Greeks call the Rock of Gibraltar?
50738.e: The Greeks called the rocks at the strait the Pillars of Heracles. They were seen as the end of the world known at the time.
50738.m: The Rock of Gibraltar used to be called a Pillar of Heracles.

50739.e: Paella is a Spanish dish made with rice. Vegetables, meat or seafood are added.
50739.m: Paella is a Spanish rice dish.

50740.q: Which area of Spain does paella come from?
50740.e: Paella comes from the area around Valencia. Rice has been grown there for a long time.

50741.e: Saffron colours the rice yellow and gives it flavour. It is one of the most expensive spices in the world.

50742.q: Over what is paella traditionally cooked in Valencia?
50742.e: In Valencia, paella is traditionally cooked outdoors over an open wood fire. The wood gives the rice a slightly smoky taste.
50742.m: Paella is traditionally cooked over an open wood fire.

50743.q: What does the word “paella” mean in Valencian?
50743.e: In Valencian, paella simply means “pan”. So the dish is named after its pan.

50744.q: What goes into a seafood paella?
50744.e: Paella de marisco contains seafood. This includes, for example, mussels, prawns and squid.
50744.m: Seafood paella contains mussels and prawns.

50745.q: Apart from chicken, which meat goes into a real paella from Valencia?
50745.e: Paella valenciana is cooked with chicken and rabbit. Green beans are added too.
50745.m: Paella valenciana contains chicken and rabbit.

50746.q: What is the crispy layer at the bottom of the paella pan?
50746.e: At the bottom, the rice turns slightly brown and crispy. This layer is called socarrat and is thought to be especially tasty.
50746.m: The crispy rice at the bottom of the pan is called socarrat.

50747.q: Which big park lies in the middle of London?
50747.e: Hyde Park is one of the biggest parks in London. You can go for walks, have picnics and go boating on a lake there.
50747.m: Hyde Park lies in the middle of London.

50748.q: What kind of buses are especially well known in London?
50748.e: The red buses with two decks are a symbol of London. From the top you get a great view.
50748.m: Red double-decker buses run in London.

50749.q: What do people in London call their underground railway?
50749.e: It is called the Tube because many of its tunnels are round like tubes. The London Underground is the oldest in the world and has been running since 1863.
50749.m: The London Underground is called the Tube.

50750.q: What colour are the well-known old telephone boxes in London?
50750.e: The red telephone boxes belong to London just like the red buses. Today some of them are only there as a reminder of the past.
50750.m: The old telephone boxes in London are red.

50751.q: What is the big Ferris wheel on the Thames in London called?
50751.e: The London Eye is around 135 metres tall. From the capsules you can see far across the whole city.
50751.m: The Ferris wheel in London is called the London Eye.

50752.q: In front of which palace in London do guards with tall fur hats stand?
50752.e: Buckingham Palace is the British king's palace in London. The famous changing of the guard takes place in front of it.
50752.m: Guards with fur hats stand in front of Buckingham Palace.

50753.q: What money do you pay with in London?
50753.e: In Britain you pay with the British pound. The euro is not used there.
50753.m: In London you pay with pounds.

50754.q: Roughly how many people live in London (as of 2024)?
50754.e: In 2024, around 9 million people lived in London. That is about as many as in the whole of Switzerland.
50754.m: About as many people live in London as in the whole of Switzerland.

50755.e: Big Ben is the name of the largest bell in the clock tower. But people often use the name for the whole tower.
50755.m: Big Ben is really a big bell.

50756.q: In which city is the clock tower with Big Ben?
50756.e: The tower with Big Ben is in London. It is one of the city's best-known landmarks.

50757.q: What has the tower of Big Ben officially been called since 2012?
50757.e: In 2012, the tower was renamed in honour of Queen Elizabeth II. Before that it was simply called the Clock Tower.
50757.m: The tower of Big Ben is officially called Elizabeth Tower.

50758.q: Which building does the tower with Big Ben belong to?
50758.e: The tower stands at the Palace of Westminster. The British Parliament meets there.
50758.m: The tower with Big Ben belongs to Parliament.

50759.q: What does Big Ben do every full hour?
50759.e: The great bell strikes every full hour. Its deep sound can be heard far and wide.
50759.m: Big Ben strikes every full hour.

50760.q: Roughly how long has the bell Big Ben been striking?
50760.e: Big Ben struck for the first time in 1859. Only during building work, for example from 2017 to 2022, was the bell mostly silent.
50760.m: Big Ben has been striking for more than 150 years.

50761.q: What can Tower Bridge in London do that many other bridges cannot?
a: It can open in the middle
It can hold back the water
50761.e: The roadway in the middle is made of two parts. These can be lifted up like flaps.
50761.m: Tower Bridge can open in the middle.

50762.q: Who does Tower Bridge open for?
50762.e: Tall ships do not fit under the bridge. So the two flaps are raised.
50762.m: Tower Bridge opens for tall ships.

50763.q: How many towers does Tower Bridge have?
50763.e: The bridge has two large towers. At the top they are connected by two walkways for pedestrians.

50764.q: What is the Tower of London, which stands next to Tower Bridge?
50764.e: The Tower of London is an old castle by the river. Tower Bridge gets its name from it.
50764.m: Tower Bridge is named after the castle called the Tower of London.

50765.q: What can Tower Bridge in London do?
a: It can open in the middle
50765.e: The two parts of the roadway of Tower Bridge can be raised. This lets big ships on the Thames pass through.
50765.m: Tower Bridge can be opened for ships.

50766.q: What is part of the floor in the upper walkways of Tower Bridge made of?
50766.e: Since 2014 there has been a glass floor in the high walkways. You can see the cars and ships below.
50766.m: There is a glass floor in the walkways of Tower Bridge.

50767.q: Which other bridge is Tower Bridge often confused with?
50767.e: Many people wrongly call Tower Bridge London Bridge. But London Bridge is a much plainer bridge nearby.
50767.m: Tower Bridge is not London Bridge.

50768.q: What colours are the steel parts of Tower Bridge today?
50768.e: Today the steel parts are painted blue and white. Only for the Queen's Silver Jubilee in 1977 was the bridge red, white and blue.
50768.m: Tower Bridge is painted blue and white.

50769.q: In which country are the Highlands?
50769.e: The Highlands are the upland area in the north of Scotland. There are many mountains and lakes there.

50770.q: What is the highest mountain in Great Britain called?
50770.e: Ben Nevis is in the Scottish Highlands. It is the highest mountain in the whole of Great Britain.
50770.m: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Great Britain.

50771.q: Roughly how high is Ben Nevis?
50771.e: Ben Nevis is 1,345 metres high. That makes it much lower than most Swiss Alpine peaks.
50771.m: Ben Nevis is around 1,300 metres high.

50772.q: Which animal with long, shaggy fur lives in the Highlands?
50772.e: The Highland cow has long fur and big horns. This helps it cope well with wind and rain.
50772.m: The Highland cow has long, shaggy fur.

50773.q: What is the tartan skirt that men wear in Scotland called?
50773.e: The kilt is a tartan woollen skirt. Each family often has its own tartan pattern.
50773.m: The Scottish tartan skirt is called a kilt.

50774.q: Which musical instrument is typical of Scotland?
50774.e: The bagpipes have a bag full of air and several pipes. Their loud sound belongs to Scotland.
50774.m: The bagpipes are the typical instrument of Scotland.

50775.q: Which plant turns the hills of the Highlands purple in late summer?
50775.e: In late summer, heather flowers everywhere. Then whole hills glow purple.

50776.q: What do people throw at the Highland Games?
50776.e: In tossing the caber, a long, heavy trunk is thrown up. It is supposed to flip over in the air.
50776.m: At the Highland Games people throw a tree trunk.

50777.q: What does the Scottish word “loch” mean?
50777.e: In Scotland, a lake is called a “loch”. So Loch Ness is the lake called Ness.
50777.m: In Scotland the word loch means lake.

50778.q: What is the famous monster of Loch Ness called?
50778.e: Many people tell stories about the lake monster Nessie. It is a famous legend.
50778.m: The Loch Ness monster is called Nessie.

50779.q: In which country is Loch Ness?
50779.e: Loch Ness is in the north of Scotland. It is one of the best-known lakes in the world.

50780.q: Has Nessie ever definitely been found?
50780.e: There are many photos and reports, but no proof. Some pictures were even faked.
50780.m: Nessie has never been definitely proven to exist.

50781.q: What colour is the water in Loch Ness?
50781.e: Streams bring soil from the moors into the lake. It colours the water dark brown, so you can hardly see into it.
50781.m: The water in Loch Ness is dark brown.

50782.q: Roughly how deep is Loch Ness at its deepest point?
50782.e: At its deepest point, Loch Ness is about 230 metres deep. It is one of the deepest lakes in Britain.
50782.m: Loch Ness is more than 200 metres deep.

50783.q: Which old castle ruin stands on the shore of Loch Ness?
50783.e: The ruin of Urquhart Castle stands right on the shore of the lake. It is a popular place for visitors.
50783.m: The castle ruin Urquhart Castle stands by Loch Ness.

50784.q: What is special about Loch Ness in Scotland?
a: It holds more water than all the lakes of England and Wales together
It is the largest lake in Europe
It is the deepest lake in the world
It has salt water like the sea
50784.e: Because it is so deep, Loch Ness holds a huge amount of fresh water. That is more than in all the lakes of England and Wales together.
50784.m: Loch Ness holds a huge amount of fresh water.

50785.q: What is the capital of Wales?
50785.e: Cardiff is the capital and largest city of Wales. It lies in the south by the sea.
50785.m: The capital of Wales is Cardiff.

50786.q: Which animal is on the flag of Wales?
50786.e: The flag of Wales shows a red dragon on green and white. It is the symbol of the country.
50786.m: There is a red dragon on the flag of Wales.

50787.q: Which language of their own do many people in Wales speak?
50787.e: In Wales people speak English and Welsh. Place-name signs are often written in both languages.
50787.m: People in Wales also speak Welsh.

50788.q: Which vegetable is a symbol of Wales?
50788.e: The leek is an old symbol of Wales. On the national day, some people pin a leek to their clothes.
50788.m: The leek is a symbol of Wales.

50789.q: What is the highest mountain in Wales called?
50789.e: Snowdon is 1,085 metres high. In Welsh it is called Yr Wyddfa.
50789.m: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.

50790.q: Which sport is especially popular in Wales?
50790.e: Rugby is very popular in Wales. Matches of the national team are big celebrations.
50790.m: Rugby is very popular in Wales.

50791.q: Wales is known for more than 600 of which kind of building?
50791.e: There are a great many castles in Wales. Some are more than 700 years old.
50791.m: Wales has a great many castles.

50792.q: Which animals outnumber people in Wales?
50792.e: Around 3 million people live in Wales, but there are far more sheep. You see them everywhere in the green fields.
50792.m: There are more sheep than people in Wales.

50793.e: Ireland has lush green fields everywhere. That is why it is called the Emerald Isle, the green island.
50793.m: Ireland is called the Emerald Isle.

a: Because it often rains and is mild
Because it is hot and dry there
Because only fir trees grow there
50794.e: In Ireland it rains often and the winters are mild. So the grass grows all year round.
50794.m: Lots of rain and mild weather make Ireland green.

50795.q: Which plant is a symbol of Ireland?
50795.e: The three-leaved clover is called a shamrock. It is the best-known symbol of Ireland.
50795.m: The shamrock is a symbol of Ireland.

50796.q: When is St Patrick's Day celebrated in Ireland?
50796.e: On 17 March, people honour Saint Patrick. He is the patron saint of Ireland.
50796.m: St Patrick's Day is on 17 March.

50797.q: What colours is the flag of the Republic of Ireland?
50797.e: The Irish flag has three vertical stripes. They are green, white and orange.
50797.m: The flag of Ireland is green, white and orange.

50798.q: What money do you pay with in the Republic of Ireland?
50798.e: The Republic of Ireland is part of the European Union and has the euro. In the northern part of the island, however, people pay with pounds.
50798.m: In the Republic of Ireland you pay with euros.

50799.q: Which musical instrument is shown on Irish euro coins?
50799.e: The harp is Ireland's national emblem. That is why it can be seen on all Irish euro coins.
50799.m: There is a harp on Irish coins.

50800.q: What is the little goblin from Irish legends with a pot of gold called?
50800.e: The leprechaun is a little shoemaker from Irish legends. He is said to hide a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
50800.m: The Irish goblin is called a leprechaun.

50801.q: Which language appears on street signs in Dublin alongside English?
50801.e: In Ireland, Irish and English are official languages. That is why signs in Dublin are written in both languages.
50801.m: In Dublin, signs are in Irish and English.

50802.q: Which river flows through the middle of Dublin?
50802.e: The Liffey divides Dublin into a northern and a southern part. Many bridges cross it.

50803.q: Who wrote the Book of Kells in Dublin by hand, more than 1,200 years ago?
50803.e: The Book of Kells is more than 1,200 years old. Monks wrote it by hand and decorated it magnificently.
50803.m: The Book of Kells was written by monks.

50804.e: Dublin lies on a bay of the Irish Sea. This sea separates Ireland from Great Britain.
50804.m: Dublin is on the Irish Sea.

50805.q: Which wild animals roam freely in the big Phoenix Park in Dublin?
50805.e: A large herd of fallow deer lives in Phoenix Park. The park is one of the largest city parks in Europe.
50805.m: Deer live in Phoenix Park in Dublin.

50806.q: What did the name Dublin originally mean?
50806.e: The name comes from the Irish “Dubh Linn”. That means “black pool”.

50807.q: Which seafarers founded a settlement in Dublin in the 9th century?
50807.e: Vikings came to Ireland in their ships. They founded a settlement and a trading post in Dublin.
50807.m: The Vikings founded a settlement in Dublin.

50808.q: What are many old houses in Dublin known for?
50808.e: Many old brick houses in Dublin have coloured front doors. They are a popular subject for photos.
50808.m: Dublin has lots of colourful front doors.

50809.e: The Thames flows right through the middle of London. Many famous bridges cross it.

50810.q: Which sea does the Thames flow into?
50810.e: East of London, the Thames gets wider and wider. Then it flows into the North Sea.
50810.m: The Thames flows into the North Sea.

50811.q: Roughly how long is the Thames?
50811.e: The Thames is about 346 kilometres long. It is the longest river that lies entirely in England.
50811.m: The Thames is around 350 kilometres long.

50813.q: What protects London from flooding from the sea during a storm surge?
a: A big barrier in the river
A high wall around the whole city
A tunnel that drains the water away
50813.e: The Thames Barrier is a huge gate in the river. It is closed during storm surges.
50813.m: A barrier protects London from flooding.

50814.q: Why does the water of the Thames in London rise and fall every day?
50814.e: The sea is not far away. That is why the tides can be felt as far as London.
50814.m: The Thames in London has tides.

50815.q: Which well-known university city is also on the Thames?
50815.e: The Thames flows through Oxford before it reaches London. Many rowers train there too.

50816.q: What did people in London do in the past when the Thames froze over completely in winter?
a: Held a fair on the ice
Held a big party in the palace
Held a market in the church
Held a party in the theatre
50816.e: In the past, the Thames sometimes froze over. Then there were fairs with stalls on the ice, the last one in 1814.
50816.m: There used to be fairs on the frozen Thames.

50817.q: Which two countries does the English Channel separate?
50817.e: The English Channel lies between the south coast of England and the north coast of France. It is part of the sea.
50817.m: The English Channel lies between England and France.

50818.q: Roughly how wide is the English Channel at its narrowest point?
50818.e: At the Strait of Dover the Channel is only about 33 kilometres wide. In clear weather you can see the other side.
50818.m: The English Channel is about 33 kilometres wide at its narrowest point.

50819.q: What is the English Channel called in French?
50819.e: “La Manche” is French for sleeve. The German name for the Channel, Ärmelkanal, also comes from this.
50819.m: In French the English Channel is called La Manche.

50820.q: What colour are the famous cliffs at Dover on the English Channel?
50820.e: The cliffs of Dover are made of chalk. That is why they shine white above the sea.
50820.m: The chalk cliffs of Dover are white.

50821.q: Which French port lies opposite Dover?
50821.e: Calais lies at the narrowest point of the Channel. Many ferries sail between Calais and Dover.

50822.q: Which island lies in the English Channel?
50822.e: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands. It lies close to the coast of France.
50822.m: Jersey is an island in the English Channel.

50823.q: What is the English Channel known for?
50823.e: The English Channel is one of the busiest waterways in the world. Hundreds of ships sail through it every day.
50823.m: Lots of ships sail on the English Channel.

50824.q: Where does the Channel Tunnel between England and France run?
50824.e: The tunnel runs deep under the seabed of the English Channel. The ships sail above it.
50824.m: The Channel Tunnel runs under the sea.

50825.q: In which year was the Channel Tunnel opened?
50825.e: The tunnel was officially opened in 1994. Before that, you could only get to England by ship or by plane.
50825.m: The Channel Tunnel has been open since 1994.

50826.q: Roughly how long is the Channel Tunnel?
50826.e: The tunnel is just over 50 kilometres long. Almost 38 kilometres of it lie under the sea.
50826.m: The Channel Tunnel is around 50 kilometres long.

50827.q: How do cars get through the Channel Tunnel?
50827.e: Cars drive into special train carriages. The train takes them to the other side in about half an hour.
50827.m: Cars travel through the Channel Tunnel on a train.

50828.q: Which two capitals does the Eurostar high-speed train connect through the tunnel?
50828.e: The Eurostar travels from London to Paris in just over two hours. On the way it goes through the tunnel.
50828.m: The Eurostar runs from London to Paris.

50829.q: How many tubes does the Channel Tunnel have?
50829.e: There are two tubes for the trains and one tube in the middle for emergencies and maintenance work.
50829.m: The Channel Tunnel has three tubes.

50830.q: Which Swiss tunnel is even longer than the Channel Tunnel?
50830.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is around 57 kilometres long. It is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
50830.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is longer than the Channel Tunnel.

50831.q: On which day do many people come to Stonehenge for the sunrise?
a: On the longest day in summer
50831.e: On the longest day of the year, the sun rises exactly over a particular stone. Many people want to see this.
50831.m: On the longest day the sun shines exactly through Stonehenge.

50832.e: Stonehenge was built by people of the Stone Age. They did not have any machines yet.

50833.q: Roughly how heavy are the big stones in the outer circle of Stonehenge?
50833.e: The big stones in the outer circle each weigh about 25 tonnes. That is as heavy as several lorries.
50833.m: The big stones of Stonehenge weigh about 25 tonnes.

50834.q: Where do the smaller bluestones of Stonehenge come from?
50834.e: Most of the bluestones come from the Preseli Hills in Wales, more than 200 kilometres away. How they were brought so far is still not fully understood.
50834.m: The bluestones of Stonehenge come from Wales.

50835.q: In which of these countries do cars drive on the left side of the road?
50835.e: In Great Britain, traffic drives on the left. In most other countries in Europe it is the other way round.
50835.m: In Great Britain cars drive on the left.

50836.q: What is different about British cars compared with Swiss cars?
a: The steering wheel is on the right
The engine is always at the back
50836.e: Because people drive on the left, the driver sits on the right. That way they can see the middle of the road better.
50836.m: In British cars the steering wheel is on the right.

50837.q: Which side of the road do cars drive on in Switzerland?
50837.e: In Switzerland, traffic drives on the right. Great Britain does the opposite and drives on the left.
50837.m: In Switzerland traffic drives on the right.

50838.q: What is often written on the road in front of zebra crossings in London?
50838.e: Many visitors look left first out of habit. So the writing reminds them to look right.
50838.m: In London you must look right first before crossing.

50839.q: Which country far away from Europe also drives on the left?
50839.e: People in Australia also drive on the left. This comes from the country's long ties with Great Britain.
50839.m: People in Australia also drive on the left.

50840.q: Which neighbour of Great Britain also drives on the left?
50840.e: People drive on the left on the whole island of Ireland. That applies to Northern Ireland and to the Republic of Ireland.
50840.m: People in Ireland also drive on the left.

50841.q: Which side do cyclists ride on in London?
a: Only in the middle of the road
50841.e: Bicycles belong on the road and follow the rule of driving on the left. So they ride on the left like the cars.
50841.m: In London bicycles also ride on the left.

a: A long, narrow inlet of the sea
50842.e: A fjord is a long, narrow arm of the sea that reaches far into the land. It often lies between high mountains.
50842.m: A fjord is a narrow arm of the sea between steep mountains.

50843.q: In which country are there especially many famous fjords?
50843.e: The west coast of Norway is full of fjords. They are one of the best-known sights there.
50843.m: Norway is the land of fjords.

50844.q: What shaped the fjords a long time ago?
50844.e: During the Ice Age, huge glaciers scraped out deep valleys. Later, seawater flowed into these valleys.
50844.m: Ice Age glaciers carved out the fjords.

50845.q: What kind of water is in a fjord?
50845.e: A fjord is connected to the open sea. That is why the water is salty.

50846.q: What is the longest fjord in Norway called?
50846.e: The Sognefjord is around 200 kilometres long. It is the longest fjord in Norway.
50846.m: The Sognefjord is Norway's longest fjord.

50847.q: What do the shores of many fjords look like?
50847.e: The shores often drop almost vertically into the water. Sometimes waterfalls tumble down over the rocks.
50847.m: Steep rock faces often tower over fjords.

50848.q: Which Norwegian fjord is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
50848.e: The Geirangerfjord became a World Heritage Site in 2005, together with the Nærøyfjord. Many tourists visit it by boat.
50848.m: The Geirangerfjord is a World Heritage Site.

50849.q: How do many visitors travel through a fjord?
50849.e: A fjord is a long arm of the sea between steep mountains. So the best way through is by ship.
50849.m: You travel through a fjord by ship.

50850.q: What are the colourful old houses at the harbour of Bergen in Norway built of?
50850.e: Bergen is on the west coast of Norway. The old wooden houses at the harbour are called Bryggen and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
50850.m: The old houses at the harbour of Bergen are made of wood.

50851.q: What money do you pay with in Norway?
50851.e: In Norway you pay with the Norwegian krone. Norway is not part of the European Union.
50851.m: In Norway you pay with kroner.

50852.q: On which day does Norway celebrate its national day?
50852.e: On 17 May 1814, Norway got its constitution. That is why many children march in parades through the streets on this day.
50852.m: Norway celebrates its national day on 17 May.

50853.q: What colour is the background of the flag of Norway?
50853.e: The flag of Norway is red. On it there is a blue cross with a white border.
50853.m: The flag of Norway is red with a blue cross.

50854.q: What is a famous cliff right in the north of Norway called?
50854.e: The North Cape is a cliff more than 300 metres high above the Norwegian Sea. Many travellers go all the way there because it is seen as the northernmost point of Europe.
50854.m: The North Cape is a famous cliff in the north of Norway.

50855.q: Which mythical creatures appear in many Norwegian legends?
50855.e: In Norwegian fairy tales, trolls live in mountains and forests. In Norway you often see them as figures in souvenir shops too.
50855.m: Trolls are the legendary creatures of Norway.

50856.q: Which sea does Norway border in the west?
a: The North Sea and the North Atlantic
50856.e: Norway has a very long coastline in the west. It lies on the North Sea and the North Atlantic.
50856.m: Norway's west coast is on the Atlantic.

50857.q: What colours is the flag of Sweden?
50857.e: The flag of Sweden is blue. On it there is a yellow cross.
50857.m: The Swedish flag shows a yellow cross on blue.

50858.q: Which country did the author Astrid Lindgren come from?
50858.e: Astrid Lindgren was a Swedish children's author. She wrote “Pippi Longstocking”, for example.

50859.q: Which painted wooden animal is a typical souvenir from Sweden?
50859.e: The Dala horse comes from the Dalarna area of Sweden. It is made of wood, usually red and brightly painted.
50859.m: The Dala horse is a painted wooden horse from Sweden.

50860.q: Which summer festival do people in Sweden celebrate in June with a decorated pole?
50860.e: At Midsummer, Swedes dance around a pole decorated with flowers. That is when the days are longest.
50860.m: Midsummer is the big summer festival of the Swedes.

50861.q: What is the largest lake in Sweden called?
50861.e: Vänern is the largest lake in Sweden. It is much bigger than any Swiss lake.
50861.m: Vänern is the largest lake in Sweden.

50862.q: Who is the head of state in Sweden?
50862.e: Sweden is a kingdom. Carl XVI Gustaf has been king since 1973.

50863.q: Which neighbouring country lies to the west of Sweden?
50863.e: Sweden and Norway share a long border in the mountains. Together they make up the Scandinavian Peninsula.
50863.m: Norway lies to the west of Sweden.

50864.q: What money do you pay with in Sweden?
50864.e: Sweden is in the EU, but it has not introduced the euro. People pay with Swedish kronor.
50864.m: In Sweden you pay with kronor.

50865.q: Stockholm is the capital of which country?
50865.e: Stockholm is the largest city in Sweden. The royal family also lives there.
50865.m: Stockholm is the capital of Sweden.

50866.e: The centre of Stockholm lies on 14 islands. Many bridges connect them.
50866.m: Stockholm is built on lots of islands.

50867.q: What is the old town of Stockholm called?
50867.e: Gamla Stan means “Old Town”. It has narrow alleys and colourful houses. Nyhavn is in Copenhagen, Alfama in Lisbon.
50867.m: Gamla Stan is the old town of Stockholm.

50868.q: Which old warship can you visit in a museum in Stockholm?
50868.e: The Vasa sank in 1628 on its very first voyage. Later it was raised and today it stands in the Vasa Museum.
50868.m: The ship Vasa stands in a museum in Stockholm.

50869.q: Which famous prize is presented in Stockholm every year?
50869.e: Most of the Nobel Prizes are presented in Stockholm on 10 December. Only the Nobel Peace Prize is given in Oslo.
50869.m: The Nobel Prizes are presented in Stockholm.

50870.q: What is Stockholm sometimes called because of its many waterways?
50870.e: Stockholm has as much water between its islands as Venice. That is why it is also called the “Venice of the North”.
50870.m: Stockholm is also called the Venice of the North.

50871.e: Stockholm lies where Lake Mälaren flows into the Baltic Sea. Ferries sail from here as far as Finland.
50871.m: Stockholm is on the Baltic Sea.

50872.q: Which strong children's book character with red plaits can you meet at the Junibacken museum in Stockholm?
50872.e: At Junibacken, children can dive into Astrid Lindgren's stories. Pippi Longstocking lives there too.
50872.m: You can meet Pippi Longstocking at Junibacken in Stockholm.

50873.q: What is the flag of Denmark called?
50873.e: The Danish flag is called the Dannebrog. It shows a white cross on a red background and is thought to be one of the oldest flags in the world.
50873.m: The flag of Denmark is called the Dannebrog.

50874.q: Which is the only country Denmark borders on land?
50874.e: Denmark has only one land border. It runs in the south, with Germany.
50874.m: On land, Denmark only borders Germany.

50875.q: What is the large peninsula on which part of Denmark lies called?
50875.e: Jutland is a peninsula north of Germany. The rest of Denmark is made up of many islands.

50876.q: What is the landscape in Denmark usually like?
50876.e: Denmark has no high mountains. The highest point is only about 170 metres high.
50876.m: Denmark is a very flat country.

50877.q: Who has been King of Denmark since 2024 (as of 2026)?
50877.e: In January 2024, Queen Margrethe II stepped down. Since then, her son Frederik X has been King of Denmark.
50877.m: Frederik X has been King of Denmark since 2024.

50878.q: Which large island in the north belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark?
50878.e: Greenland is the largest island in the world. It belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark but largely governs itself.
50878.m: Greenland belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.

50879.q: Which bridge connects Denmark with Sweden?
50879.e: The Øresund Bridge crosses a strait called the Øresund. Cars and trains travel over it.
50879.m: The Øresund Bridge connects Denmark and Sweden.

50880.q: What money do you pay with in Denmark?
50880.e: Denmark is in the EU, but it has not introduced the euro. People pay with the Danish krone.
50880.m: In Denmark you pay with kroner.

50881.q: Copenhagen is the capital of which country?
50881.e: Copenhagen is the largest city in Denmark. The royal family also lives there.
50881.m: Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark.

50882.q: What is the famous harbour in Copenhagen with colourful houses called?
50882.e: Nyhavn means “New Harbour”. Colourful houses and old wooden ships line it.
50882.m: Nyhavn is the colourful harbour of Copenhagen.

50883.q: What is the old amusement park in the middle of Copenhagen called?
50883.e: Tivoli opened in 1843. It is one of the oldest amusement parks in the world.
50883.m: Tivoli is an old amusement park in Copenhagen.

50884.q: Which vehicle do especially many people in Copenhagen use to get to work?
50884.e: Copenhagen has many wide cycle paths. A large share of people cycle every day.
50884.m: Lots of people in Copenhagen ride bicycles.

50885.q: What is the royal family's palace in Copenhagen called?
50885.e: Amalienborg is made up of four identical palaces around a square. The guards change there every day.
50885.m: Amalienborg is the royal palace in Copenhagen.

50886.q: On which Danish island is Copenhagen?
50886.e: Copenhagen lies on the island of Zealand. It is the largest island of Denmark itself, not counting Greenland.
50886.m: Copenhagen is on the island of Zealand.

50887.q: Which Swedish city lies opposite Copenhagen on the other side of the sea?
50887.e: Only a narrow strait lies between Copenhagen and Malmö. By train the journey takes only about 35 to 40 minutes.

50888.q: In which city does the famous statue of the Little Mermaid sit?
50888.e: The Little Mermaid sits on a stone at the harbour. She is one of the best-known landmarks of Denmark.
50888.m: The Little Mermaid sits in Copenhagen.

50889.q: Who wrote the fairy tale “The Little Mermaid”?
50889.e: The fairy tale came out in 1837. In it, the Danish writer tells of a mermaid who loves a prince.
50889.m: Hans Christian Andersen wrote “The Little Mermaid”.

50890.q: What is the statue of the Little Mermaid made of?
50890.e: The statue is cast in bronze. It sits on a large stone.
50890.m: The Little Mermaid is made of bronze.

50891.q: What does the statue of the Little Mermaid sit on?
50891.e: The Little Mermaid sits on a rock by the shore. She gazes out over the water.
50891.m: The Little Mermaid sits on a stone by the water.

50892.q: Roughly how big is the statue of the Little Mermaid?
50892.e: Many tourists are surprised at how small the statue is. It is only about 1.25 metres tall.
50892.m: The Little Mermaid is only about 1.25 metres tall.

50893.q: Which Danish writer wrote the fairy tale of the Little Mermaid?
50893.e: Hans Christian Andersen wrote the fairy tale in 1837. The statue of the Little Mermaid has sat at Copenhagen harbour since 1913.
50893.m: The Little Mermaid comes from Hans Christian Andersen.

a: The land of a thousand lakes
50894.e: There are so many lakes in Finland that you can hardly count them. In fact, there are well over a hundred thousand.
50894.m: Finland is also called the land of a thousand lakes.

50895.q: What colours is the flag of Finland?
50895.e: The Finnish flag shows a blue cross on a white background. People often say the blue stands for the lakes and the white for the snow.
50895.m: The Finnish flag is blue and white.

50896.q: What money do you pay with in Finland?
50896.e: Finland is the only Nordic country that has the euro. Euro coins and notes have been used there since 2002.
50896.m: In Finland you pay with the euro.

50897.q: Which hot sweat bath comes from Finland?
50897.e: The word sauna is Finnish. There are around three million saunas in Finland, so almost every home has one.

50898.q: Which fantasy creatures by the Finnish author Tove Jansson are world-famous?
50898.e: Tove Jansson created the Moomins, friendly troll creatures with round noses. Her books are available in many languages.

50899.q: What is a large part of Finland covered with?
50899.e: About three quarters of Finland is forest. That makes Finland one of the most forested countries in Europe.

50900.q: Which large country does Finland border in the east?
50900.e: Finland has a long border with Russia in the east. To the west lie Sweden and Norway.
50900.m: In the east, Finland borders Russia.

50901.q: In which country can you visit Santa Claus's village?
50901.e: In Rovaniemi in the north of Finland there is a Santa Claus village. Lots of children visit every year.
50901.m: Santa Claus's village is in Finland.

50902.q: Helsinki is the capital of which country?
50902.e: Helsinki is the largest city in Finland. It lies in the south of the country by the sea.
50902.m: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.

50903.e: Helsinki lies on the Gulf of Finland. This is part of the Baltic Sea.
50903.m: Helsinki is on the Baltic Sea.

50904.q: What colour is the famous cathedral of Helsinki?
50904.e: Helsinki Cathedral is white and has green domes. It stands at the top of a big flight of steps above Senate Square.

50905.q: What stands on the islands of Suomenlinna off Helsinki?
50905.e: Suomenlinna is a fortress on islands off Helsinki. It was meant to protect the city from the sea and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
50905.m: Suomenlinna is a sea fortress off Helsinki.

50906.q: Which big sporting event took place in Helsinki in 1952?
50906.e: The 1952 Summer Olympics took place in Helsinki. The Olympic Stadium is still standing today.
50906.m: Helsinki was an Olympic city in 1952.

50907.q: Which capital can you reach from Helsinki by ferry in only about two hours?
50907.e: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia and lies opposite Helsinki. By ferry the journey takes only about two hours.
50907.m: Ferries sail from Helsinki to Tallinn.

50908.q: Which languages are on the street signs in Helsinki?
50908.e: Finland has two official languages. That is why street names in Helsinki are written in Finnish and Swedish.
50908.m: In Helsinki, signs are in Finnish and Swedish.

50909.q: Why is Iceland called a volcanic island?
a: Because it was formed by volcanoes
Because it is made entirely of sand
Because it is in the Mediterranean
50909.e: Iceland grew out of the sea through volcanic eruptions. There are still many active volcanoes there today.

50910.q: What is the capital of Iceland?
50910.e: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of an independent country. A large share of Iceland's people live there.
50910.m: Reykjavík is the capital of Iceland.

50911.q: What do you call a hot spring that shoots water high into the air?
50911.e: The word geyser comes from Iceland. The geyser Strokkur shoots a column of water into the air every few minutes.
50911.m: A geyser shoots hot water into the air.

50912.q: What is Iceland often called because of its volcanoes and glaciers?
a: The land of fire and ice
50912.e: Iceland has hot volcanoes and at the same time big glaciers. That is why people speak of the land of fire and ice.
50912.m: Iceland is the land of fire and ice.

50913.q: What is the largest glacier in Iceland called?
50913.e: Vatnajökull is the largest glacier in Iceland. There are even volcanoes under its ice.

50914.q: Which Icelandic volcano brought air traffic in Europe to a standstill with its ash cloud in 2010?
50914.e: Eyjafjallajökull erupted in 2010. Its ash drifted over Europe, and many aeroplanes had to stay on the ground.

50915.q: What is the special gait of the Icelandic horse called, in which the rider is hardly shaken about?
50915.e: The Icelandic horse can do the tölt. It moves fast and very smoothly, so the rider is hardly shaken about.
50915.m: Icelandic horses can do the tölt.

50916.q: Which bird with a colourful beak nests in large numbers on the cliffs of Iceland?
50916.e: The puffin has a colourful beak. Millions of these birds nest on steep cliffs in Iceland.

50917.q: What do many houses in Iceland use for heating?
50917.e: Under Iceland the earth is very hot. Hot water from the ground is used directly to heat the houses.
50917.m: In Iceland, homes are heated with heat from the earth.

a: In the far north of Europe
50918.e: Lapland is in the north of Norway, Sweden and Finland. A small part also belongs to Russia.
50918.m: Lapland is in the far north of Europe.

50919.q: What are the people who have lived in Lapland for a long time called?
50919.e: The Sámi are the indigenous people of Lapland. Many of them have kept reindeer for centuries.
50919.m: The Sámi are the people of Lapland.

50920.q: What happens to the sun in Lapland in summer?
a: It does not set at night
It does not rise at all
50920.e: In the far north, the midnight sun shines in summer. Then it stays light even at night.
50920.m: In summer the midnight sun shines in Lapland.

50921.q: What is the time in winter when the sun does not rise at all in Lapland called?
50921.e: In winter, the sun stays below the horizon for weeks in the far north. This dark time is called the polar night.
50921.m: During the polar night the sun does not rise.

50922.q: Which coloured lights can you see in the sky over Lapland in winter?
50922.e: The northern lights glow green, sometimes also red or purple. They are caused by particles from the sun.
50922.m: The northern lights glow over Lapland in winter.

50923.q: Which imaginary line on Earth runs through Lapland?
50923.e: The Arctic Circle runs right across Lapland. It goes all the way round the Earth in the far north.
50923.m: The Arctic Circle runs through Lapland.

50924.q: What is the weather in Lapland usually like in winter?
50924.e: In winter there is a lot of snow in Lapland. It is often far below zero degrees.
50924.m: Winter in Lapland is cold and snowy.

50925.q: Which animals pull Santa Claus's sleigh in stories?
50925.e: In many Christmas stories, reindeer pull the sleigh.

50926.q: What do reindeer like to eat most in winter?
50926.e: Reindeer scrape in the snow with their hooves to find lichen. That is why one kind of lichen is even called reindeer lichen.

50927.q: Why do the Sámi in the far north keep reindeer?
50927.e: The Sámi are a people of the far north. Their reindeer provide meat and warm hides. In the past they also pulled sledges.
50927.m: The Sámi keep reindeer for meat and hides.

50928.q: What is the name of the reindeer with the red nose from the Christmas song?
50928.e: Rudolph lights the way through the fog with his red nose. Many children all over the world know the song.
50928.m: Rudolph is the reindeer with the red nose.

50929.q: Which is the largest kind of deer in the world?
50929.e: The moose is the largest deer. A male can be more than 2 metres tall at the shoulder.
50929.m: The moose is the largest deer in the world.

50930.q: What do the antlers of a male moose often look like?
50930.e: Many bull moose have wide, flat antlers. That is why they are called palmate antlers, shaped like a shovel.

50931.q: What do many road signs in Sweden warn about?
50931.e: A great many moose live in Sweden. They often cross roads, so there are special warning signs.
50931.m: In Sweden, signs warn about moose.

a: Plants such as leaves and twigs
50932.e: Moose are herbivores. They eat leaves, twigs, bark and also water plants.

50933.q: What are moose surprisingly good at?
50933.e: Moose are good swimmers. They even swim across wide lakes and rivers.

50934.q: What is a male moose called?
50934.e: Male moose are called bulls, females are called cows. The young are called calves.
50934.m: A male moose is called a bull.

50935.e: The Faroes lie in the North Atlantic between Iceland, Norway and Scotland. It is windy there and often foggy.
50935.m: The Faroes are in the North Atlantic.

50936.q: Which kingdom do the Faroe Islands belong to?
50936.e: The Faroes belong to the Kingdom of Denmark. But they run most things themselves.
50936.m: The Faroes belong to the Kingdom of Denmark.

50937.q: What does the name “Faroe” probably mean?
50937.e: A great many sheep live on the islands. That is why the name is usually explained as “sheep islands”.

50938.q: How many larger islands make up the Faroes?
50938.e: The Faroes are made up of 18 larger islands. All but one are inhabited.
50938.m: The Faroes are made up of 18 islands.

50939.q: What is the capital of the Faroes?
50939.e: Tórshavn is one of the smallest capitals in the world. It has colourful houses with grass roofs.
50939.m: Tórshavn is the capital of the Faroes.

50940.e: Poland has a long coastline on the Baltic Sea in the north. There are many sandy beaches there.
50940.m: Poland is on the Baltic Sea.

50941.q: Which long river flows right across Poland?
50941.e: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland. It flows from the mountains in the south to the Baltic Sea.
50941.m: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland.

50942.q: What colours is the flag of Poland?
50942.e: The Polish flag has two stripes. It is white at the top and red at the bottom.
50942.m: The flag of Poland is white and red.

50943.q: What is the money in Poland called?
50943.e: In Poland you pay with the złoty. Poland has not introduced the euro.
50943.m: In Poland you pay with the złoty.

50944.q: Which neighbouring country does Poland have in the west?
50944.e: In the west, Poland borders Germany. Much of the border runs along the Oder and Neisse rivers.

50945.q: Which famous composer came from Poland?
50945.e: Frédéric Chopin was born in Poland in 1810. He wrote mainly beautiful music for the piano.
50945.m: Frédéric Chopin was a famous composer from Poland.

50946.q: Which beautiful old city in Poland used to be the capital for a long time?
50946.e: Kraków was the capital of Poland for many centuries. Wawel Castle stands there.
50946.m: Kraków used to be the capital of Poland.

50947.q: Which scientist from Poland worked out that the Earth goes round the sun?
50947.e: Nicolaus Copernicus lived in Poland around 500 years ago. He realised that the Earth circles the sun and not the other way round.
50947.m: Copernicus realised that the Earth circles the sun.

50948.e: Warsaw lies on both banks of the Vistula. Many bridges connect the two sides.

50949.q: Which mythical creature is on the coat of arms of Warsaw?
50949.e: The coat of arms of Warsaw shows a mermaid with a sword and shield. A statue of her stands in the old town.
50949.m: A mermaid is the symbol of Warsaw.

50950.q: Which famous scientist was born in Warsaw?
50950.e: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1867. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
50950.m: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw.

50951.q: What happened to the old town of Warsaw after the Second World War?
a: It was turned into a park.
It was turned into a lake.
50951.e: In the Second World War the old town was almost completely destroyed. Afterwards it was rebuilt using old pictures.
50951.m: The old town of Warsaw was rebuilt after the war.

50952.q: What special heritage list does the old town of Warsaw belong to?
50952.e: The old town of Warsaw has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980. That is a list of especially valuable places in the world.
50952.m: The old town of Warsaw is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

50953.q: What is the very tall building in the centre of Warsaw called?
50953.e: The Palace of Culture is a big tower block in the middle of Warsaw. It has theatres, cinemas and museums inside.
50953.m: The Palace of Culture is a well-known tower block in Warsaw.

50954.q: Which musician is Warsaw's big airport named after?
50954.e: Warsaw's largest airport is called Warsaw Chopin Airport. It bears the name of the famous composer.
50954.m: Warsaw's airport is named after Chopin.

50955.q: Which city is the largest in Poland?
50955.e: Warsaw has more than 1.8 million inhabitants (as of 2020). No other city in Poland is as big.
50955.m: Warsaw is the largest city in Poland.

50956.q: What is the capital of the Czech Republic?
50956.e: The capital of the Czech Republic is Prague. It is in the west of the country.
50956.m: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic.

50957.q: What is the money in the Czech Republic called?
50957.e: In the Czech Republic you pay with the Czech koruna. The euro is not the national currency there.
50957.m: In the Czech Republic you pay with koruna.

50958.q: Does the Czech Republic have a coastline on the sea?
a: No, it has no sea coast.
50958.e: The Czech Republic is a landlocked country like Switzerland. It is surrounded by other countries on all sides.
50958.m: Like Switzerland, the Czech Republic has no sea.

50959.q: Which famous cartoon character comes from the Czech Republic?
50959.e: The Little Mole was created by the Czech artist Zdeněk Miler. Children all over the world know his films.
50959.m: The Little Mole comes from the Czech Republic.

50960.q: Which big river has its source in the Czech Republic and flows into Germany?
50960.e: The Elbe rises in the Giant Mountains in the Czech Republic. It flows through Germany to the North Sea.
50960.m: The Elbe has its source in the Czech Republic.

50961.q: Which country did the Czech Republic and Slovakia come from in 1993?
50961.e: Until the end of 1992, the Czech Republic and Slovakia together formed Czechoslovakia. On 1 January 1993 they became two countries.
50961.m: The Czech Republic and Slovakia used to be one country.

50962.q: What is the highest mountain in the Czech Republic called?
50962.e: Sněžka is around 1,600 metres high. It is in the Giant Mountains on the border with Poland.
50962.m: Sněžka is the highest mountain in the Czech Republic.

50963.q: What is the western part of the Czech Republic, where Prague is, called?
50963.e: The Czech Republic is made up mainly of Bohemia and Moravia. Prague is in Bohemia.

50964.q: Which neighbouring country does the Czech Republic have to the south?
50964.e: To the south, the Czech Republic borders Austria. Its other neighbours are Germany, Poland and Slovakia.
50964.m: Austria lies south of the Czech Republic.

50965.q: What is the river that flows through Prague called?
50965.e: The Vltava flows through Prague. Later it flows into the Elbe.

50966.q: What is the famous old stone bridge in Prague called?
50966.e: Charles Bridge is more than 600 years old. Many stone statues stand on it.
50966.m: Charles Bridge is the most famous bridge in Prague.

50967.q: What does the famous old clock on Prague's town hall show on the hour?
50967.e: The Astronomical Clock in Prague is around 600 years old. On the hour, figures of the apostles pass by little windows.
50967.m: Figures move on Prague's town hall clock.

50968.q: Which huge complex on a hill is a landmark of Prague?
50968.e: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world. Today the President of the Czech Republic works there.
50968.m: Prague Castle is a huge castle complex.

50969.q: What nickname does Prague have because of its many towers?
50969.e: Prague has a great many church towers and gate towers. That is why it is called the City of a Hundred Spires.
50969.m: Prague is also called the City of a Hundred Spires.

50970.q: Which famous writer was born in Prague?
50970.e: Franz Kafka was born in Prague in 1883. He wrote his books in German.

50971.q: What is the big, long square in Prague's New Town called?
50971.e: Wenceslas Square is named after Saint Wenceslas. The National Museum stands at its upper end.
50971.m: Wenceslas Square is a big square in Prague.

50972.q: What colour are many roofs in Prague's old town?
50972.e: Many houses in Prague have red tiled roofs. That is why the old town looks red from above.
50972.m: Prague has lots of red roofs.

50973.q: What is the capital of Hungary?
50973.e: The capital of Hungary is Budapest. About one in five people in the country lives there.
50973.m: Budapest is the capital of Hungary.

50974.q: What is the big lake in Hungary called?
50974.e: Lake Balaton is called Plattensee in German. It is the largest lake in Central Europe.
50974.m: The big lake in Hungary is called Balaton.

50975.q: What is the money in Hungary called?
50975.e: In Hungary you pay with the forint. Hungary has not introduced the euro.
50975.m: In Hungary you pay with the forint.

50976.q: Which red spice is typical of Hungary?
50976.e: Hungary is known for its paprika powder. It goes into many dishes, for example goulash.
50976.m: Paprika is a typical spice from Hungary.

50977.q: Which stew with meat and paprika comes from Hungary?
50977.e: Goulash is a dish from Hungary. In the past, cattle herders cooked it in a pot over the fire.
50977.m: Goulash is a dish from Hungary.

50978.q: Which well-known toy did the Hungarian Ernő Rubik invent?
50978.e: Ernő Rubik invented the Rubik's Cube in 1974. You have to twist it so that each side has only one colour.
50978.m: The Rubik's Cube was invented in Hungary.

50979.q: Which language is spoken in Hungary?
50979.e: People in Hungary speak Hungarian. The language is hardly related to German or the Slavic languages.

50980.q: Which neighbouring country does Hungary have in the west?
50980.e: In the west, Hungary borders Austria. Hungary has no coastline on the sea.

50981.q: Which river divides Budapest into two parts?
50981.e: The Danube flows right through the middle of Budapest. Many bridges connect the two banks.
50981.m: The Danube flows through the middle of Budapest.

50982.q: Budapest has one of the oldest underground railways in Europe. In which year did it first run?
50982.e: Budapest's first underground line opened in 1896. It was the first electric underground railway on the European mainland.
50982.m: Budapest's underground has been running since 1896.

50983.q: Which huge building with a dome stands in Budapest right on the Danube?
50983.e: The Hungarian Parliament is one of the largest parliament buildings in the world. It stands on the bank of the Danube.
50983.m: The Parliament in Budapest stands on the Danube.

50984.q: What is the famous bridge with two pairs of lions in Budapest called?
50984.e: The Chain Bridge was the first permanent bridge between Buda and Pest. Stone lions lie at both ends.
50984.m: The Chain Bridge connects Buda and Pest.

50985.q: With its many warm springs, what is Budapest known for?
50985.e: There are many warm springs under Budapest. They supply large thermal baths, for example the Széchenyi Baths.
50985.m: Budapest is known for its thermal baths.

50986.q: What is the green island in the Danube in the middle of Budapest called?
50986.e: Margaret Island lies in the Danube between Buda and Pest. It is a big park without many cars.
50986.m: Margaret Island is a park in the Danube.

50987.q: What is the beautiful viewing terrace with little towers in Buda called?
50987.e: Fisherman's Bastion stands on Castle Hill in Buda. From there you can see far across the Danube and the Parliament.
50987.m: Fisherman's Bastion is a viewpoint in Budapest.

50988.q: Who used to live in the big palace on Castle Hill in Budapest?
50988.e: The big Royal Palace stands on Castle Hill in Budapest. The kings of Hungary used to live there.
50988.m: Kings used to live in Budapest's Royal Palace.

50989.q: What is the capital of Slovakia?
50989.e: The capital of Slovakia is Bratislava. In German it used to be called Pressburg.
50989.m: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia.

50990.q: What money do you pay with in Slovakia?
50990.e: Slovakia introduced the euro in 2009. Before that there was the Slovak koruna.
50990.m: In Slovakia you pay with the euro.

50991.q: What are the high mountains in the north of Slovakia called?
50991.e: The High Tatras are the highest range of the Carpathians. Part of them belongs to Poland.
50991.m: The High Tatras are in the north of Slovakia.

50992.q: Which big river flows through Bratislava?
50992.e: The Danube flows through Bratislava. Ships sail along it as far as Vienna and Budapest.

50993.q: Which language is spoken in Slovakia?
50993.e: People in Slovakia speak Slovak. The language is closely related to Czech.

50994.q: Does Slovakia have a coastline on the sea?
a: No, it has no sea coast.
50994.e: Slovakia is a landlocked country. It has no coast, just like Switzerland.

50995.q: Which capital lies very close to Bratislava, only around 60 kilometres away?
50995.e: Bratislava lies right on the border with Austria. It is only about 60 kilometres to Vienna.
50995.m: Bratislava and Vienna are close to each other.

50996.q: What colours is the flag of Slovakia?
50996.e: The Slovak flag has three stripes in white, blue and red. On the left there is also a coat of arms with a double cross.
50996.m: The flag of Slovakia is white, blue and red.

50997.q: What is the capital of Romania?
50997.e: The capital of Romania is Bucharest. Do not mix it up with Budapest in Hungary.
50997.m: Bucharest is the capital of Romania.

50998.e: In the east, Romania has a coastline on the Black Sea. The port of Constanța is there.
50998.m: Romania is on the Black Sea.

50999.q: Which big mountain range curves through Romania?
50999.e: The Carpathians form a big arc through Romania. Many bears and wolves still live there.

51000.q: Where does the Danube flow into the sea in Romania?
51000.e: Just before the Black Sea, the Danube splits into many branches. This area is called the Danube Delta and is a paradise for birds.
51000.m: The Danube ends in the Danube Delta on the Black Sea.

51001.q: Which well-known spooky character is linked with Romania?
51001.e: The vampire Count Dracula comes from a famous book. In it he lives in a castle in the mountains of Romania. Bran Castle is often called Dracula's Castle.
51001.m: The Dracula story is set in Romania.

51002.q: What is the region in the middle of Romania called?
51002.e: Transylvania is called Siebenbürgen in German. There are many old castles and fortified churches there.
51002.m: Transylvania lies in the middle of Romania.

51003.q: What is the money in Romania called?
51003.e: In Romania you pay with the leu. The word means lion.
51003.m: In Romania you pay with the leu.

51004.q: Which gymnast from Romania was the first to get a perfect 10 at the Olympics in 1976?
51004.e: Nadia Comăneci performed without a single mistake in Montreal in 1976. She was only 14 years old and was the first to get the perfect score of 10.
51004.m: Nadia Comăneci was the first to score a perfect 10.

51005.q: Which big wild animals live in the forests of Romania?
51005.e: A great many brown bears live in the mountain forests of Romania, more than in almost any other country in Europe.
51005.m: Lots of brown bears live in Romania.

51006.q: What is the capital of Bulgaria?
51006.e: The capital of Bulgaria is Sofia. It lies at the foot of Mount Vitosha.
51006.m: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria.

51007.e: In the east, Bulgaria has a coast on the Black Sea. Many people go there for beach holidays.
51007.m: Bulgaria is on the Black Sea.

51008.q: Which alphabet is used in Bulgaria?
51008.e: In Bulgaria people write with Cyrillic letters. This alphabet was created more than 1000 years ago in the area of Bulgaria.
51008.m: In Bulgaria people write in Cyrillic.

51009.q: Which flowers is Bulgaria famous for?
51009.e: Huge fields of roses grow in Bulgaria. Their petals are used to make valuable rose oil for perfume.
51009.m: Bulgaria is famous for its roses.

51010.q: What does a nod of the head often mean in Bulgaria?
51010.e: In Bulgaria nodding often means “no” and shaking your head means “yes”. Here it is exactly the other way round.
51010.m: In Bulgaria a nod often means no.

51011.q: Which dairy product is especially well known in Bulgaria?
51011.e: Bulgaria is famous for its yoghurt. One yoghurt bacterium is even named after the country.

51012.q: What is the name of the large church with the golden main dome in Sofia?
51012.e: The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is the landmark of Sofia. Its large main dome is covered in gold.
51012.m: The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is in Sofia.

51013.q: Which famous monastery lies in the mountains of Bulgaria?
51013.e: Rila Monastery lies in the Rila Mountains. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and has colourful paintings on its walls.
51013.m: Rila Monastery is a famous monastery in Bulgaria.

51014.q: What is the capital of Ukraine?
51014.e: The capital of Ukraine is Kyiv. It is the largest city in the country.
51014.m: Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine.

51015.q: Which big river flows through Kyiv?
